know_before_you_go: Visa: Most nationalities, including Indians, receive a visa-on-arrival for up to 60 days in Mauritius.
Currency: The local currency is the Mauritian Rupee (MUR); carry small denominations for local purchases.
Best Time to Visit: May to December is cooler and less humid; avoid January–March (cyclone season).
Language: English and French are widely spoken; Creole is the local language.
Weather: Tropical climate — light cotton clothes are best; pack a light jacket for evenings.
Driving: They drive on the left-hand side; an international driving permit is required for rentals.
Local Transport: Taxis are common but negotiate fares in advance or use hotel transfers.
Electricity: Standard voltage is 230V; plug type C & G (UK style). Carry an adapter.
Water Safety: Tap water is generally treated, but bottled water is recommended for tourists.
Beach Safety: Currents can be strong in some areas — swim only in designated safe zones.
Cultural Etiquette: Dress modestly when visiting temples, churches, or mosques.
Food: Seafood is fresh and popular; vegetarian options are widely available.
Tipping: Not mandatory, but 5–10% is appreciated for good service.
Shopping: Popular souvenirs include rum, vanilla tea, model ships, and handmade crafts.
Wildlife: Avoid feeding wildlife, especially monkeys in nature parks.
Snorkeling & Diving: Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral life.
Health: No mandatory vaccines, but mosquito repellent is a must.
Connectivity: Prepaid SIM cards are easily available at the airport.
Time Zone: Mauritius Time (MUT) is GMT+4.
Emergency Numbers: Police – 999, Ambulance – 114, Fire – 115

dos: Respect Local Culture – Always remove shoes before entering temples and dress appropriately.
Try Local Cuisine – Sample street food like dholl puri, gateaux piments, and fresh seafood.
Explore Beyond Beaches – Visit waterfalls, sugar plantations, and volcanic craters.
Bargain Politely – Negotiation is expected in markets, but be respectful.
Book Activities Early – Dolphin watching, catamaran cruises, and diving trips get booked fast.
Use Reef-Safe Sunscreen – Protects your skin and marine life.
Keep Hydrated – Especially important during full-day excursions.
Support Local Artisans – Buy from small craft shops and roadside stalls.
Carry Local Cash – Many small shops and rural areas don’t accept cards.
Learn Basic Creole Phrases – Locals appreciate a simple 'Bonzur' (Hello) or 'Mersi' (Thank you).
donts: Don’t Sunbathe Topless – Public nudity is prohibited except in designated private areas.
Don’t Litter – Mauritius is proud of its clean environment; dispose of trash responsibly.
Don’t Touch Coral – It’s fragile and essential for marine ecosystems.
Don’t Take Shells or Sand Home – It’s illegal and can result in fines.
Don’t Photograph People Without Permission – Especially in rural villages or religious sites.
Don’t Overstay Your Visa – Fines and penalties apply.
Don’t Swim Outside Safe Zones – Currents can be dangerous, especially on the east coast.
Don’t Expect 24/7 Shopping – Many shops close early in the evening and on Sundays.
Don’t Haggle Aggressively – Bargain politely; overly aggressive tactics are frowned upon.
Don’t Ignore Local Wildlife Warnings – Some areas have jellyfish or sea urchins; ask locals before swimming.

know_before_you_go: Visa: Most nationalities, including Indians, receive a visa-on-arrival for up to 60 days in Mauritius.
Currency: The local currency is the Mauritian Rupee (MUR); carry small denominations for local purchases.
Best Time to Visit: May to December is cooler and less humid; avoid January–March (cyclone season).
Language: English and French are widely spoken; Creole is the local language.
Weather: Tropical climate — light cotton clothes are best; pack a light jacket for evenings.
Driving: They drive on the left-hand side; an international driving permit is required for rentals.
Local Transport: Taxis are common but negotiate fares in advance or use hotel transfers.
Electricity: Standard voltage is 230V; plug type C & G (UK style). Carry an adapter.
Water Safety: Tap water is generally treated, but bottled water is recommended for tourists.
Beach Safety: Currents can be strong in some areas — swim only in designated safe zones.
Cultural Etiquette: Dress modestly when visiting temples, churches, or mosques.
Food: Seafood is fresh and popular; vegetarian options are widely available.
Tipping: Not mandatory, but 5–10% is appreciated for good service.
Shopping: Popular souvenirs include rum, vanilla tea, model ships, and handmade crafts.
Wildlife: Avoid feeding wildlife, especially monkeys in nature parks.
Snorkeling & Diving: Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral life.
Health: No mandatory vaccines, but mosquito repellent is a must.
Connectivity: Prepaid SIM cards are easily available at the airport.
Time Zone: Mauritius Time (MUT) is GMT+4.
Emergency Numbers: Police – 999, Ambulance – 114, Fire – 115

dos: Respect Local Culture – Always remove shoes before entering temples and dress appropriately.

Bargain Politely – Negotiation is expected in markets, but be respectful.

Use Reef-Safe Sunscreen – Protects your skin and marine life.
Keep Hydrated – Especially important during full-day excursions.
Support Local Artisans – Buy from small craft shops and roadside stalls.
Carry Local Cash – Many small shops and rural areas don’t accept cards.

donts: Don’t Sunbathe Topless – Public nudity is prohibited except in designated private areas.

Don’t Touch Coral – It’s fragile and essential for marine ecosystems.
Don’t Take Shells or Sand Home – It’s illegal and can result in fines.
Don’t Photograph People Without Permission – Especially in rural villages or religious sites.
Don’t Overstay Your Visa – Fines and penalties apply.
Don’t Swim Outside Safe Zones – Currents can be dangerous, especially on the east coast.
Don’t Expect 24/7 Shopping – Many shops close early in the evening and on Sundays.
Don’t Haggle Aggressively – Bargain politely; overly aggressive tactics are frowned upon.
Don’t Ignore Local Wildlife Warnings – Some areas have jellyfish or sea urchins; ask locals before swimming.

know_before_you_go: Visa: Most nationalities, including Indians, receive a visa-on-arrival for up to 60 days in Mauritius.
Currency: The local currency is the Mauritian Rupee (MUR); carry small denominations for local purchases.
Best Time to Visit: May to December is cooler and less humid; avoid January–March (cyclone season).
Language: English and French are widely spoken; Creole is the local language.
Weather: Tropical climate — light cotton clothes are best; pack a light jacket for evenings.
Driving: They drive on the left-hand side; an international driving permit is required for rentals.
Local Transport: Taxis are common but negotiate fares in advance or use hotel transfers.
Electricity: Standard voltage is 230V; plug type C & G (UK style). Carry an adapter.
Water Safety: Tap water is generally treated, but bottled water is recommended for tourists.
Beach Safety: Currents can be strong in some areas — swim only in designated safe zones.
Cultural Etiquette: Dress modestly when visiting temples, churches, or mosques.
Food: Seafood is fresh and popular; vegetarian options are widely available.
Tipping: Not mandatory, but 5–10% is appreciated for good service.
Shopping: Popular souvenirs include rum, vanilla tea, model ships, and handmade crafts.
Wildlife: Avoid feeding wildlife, especially monkeys in nature parks.
Snorkeling & Diving: Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral life.
Health: No mandatory vaccines, but mosquito repellent is a must.
Connectivity: Prepaid SIM cards are easily available at the airport.
Time Zone: Mauritius Time (MUT) is GMT+4.
Emergency Numbers: Police – 999, Ambulance – 114, Fire – 115

dos: Respect Local Culture – Always remove shoes before entering temples and dress appropriately.
Try Local Cuisine – Sample street food like dholl puri, gateaux piments, and fresh seafood.
Explore Beyond Beaches – Visit waterfalls, sugar plantations, and volcanic craters.
Bargain Politely – Negotiation is expected in markets, but be respectful.
Book Activities Early – Dolphin watching, catamaran cruises, and diving trips get booked fast.
Use Reef-Safe Sunscreen – Protects your skin and marine life.
Keep Hydrated – Especially important during full-day excursions.
Support Local Artisans – Buy from small craft shops and roadside stalls.
Carry Local Cash – Many small shops and rural areas don’t accept cards.
Learn Basic Creole Phrases – Locals appreciate a simple 'Bonzur' (Hello) or 'Mersi' (Thank you).
donts: Don’t Sunbathe Topless – Public nudity is prohibited except in designated private areas.
Don’t Litter – Mauritius is proud of its clean environment; dispose of trash responsibly.
Don’t Touch Coral – It’s fragile and essential for marine ecosystems.
Don’t Take Shells or Sand Home – It’s illegal and can result in fines.
Don’t Photograph People Without Permission – Especially in rural villages or religious sites.
Don’t Overstay Your Visa – Fines and penalties apply.
Don’t Swim Outside Safe Zones – Currents can be dangerous, especially on the east coast.
Don’t Expect 24/7 Shopping – Many shops close early in the evening and on Sundays.
Don’t Haggle Aggressively – Bargain politely; overly aggressive tactics are frowned upon.
Don’t Ignore Local Wildlife Warnings – Some areas have jellyfish or sea urchins; ask locals before swimming.

activities: Dive into local life with a guided cultural tour. Visit traditional villages, taste Mauritian street food, and see artisans at work. Explore a tea plantation and learn about the island’s sugar and rum history with tastings included.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Colombo | Evening Leisure
activities: Arrive at Bandaranaike International Airport and transfer to your hotel in Colombo. After check-in, unwind with a leisurely stroll along Galle Face Green, enjoy the sea breeze, and watch the sunset over the Indian Ocean. End your evening with a welcome dinner, sampling Sri Lankan specialties like hoppers and seafood curry.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Colombo to Kandy | Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage & Temple of the Tooth
activities: After breakfast, drive to Kandy, stopping at Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage to see elephants bathing in the river. Continue to Kandy city and visit the Temple of the Tooth, a sacred Buddhist site. Explore Kandy Lake and local markets, then enjoy a traditional cultural dance performance in the evening.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Kandy to Sigiriya | Rock Fortress & Dambulla Cave Temple
activities: Travel to Sigiriya and climb the Sigiriya Rock Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with stunning views and ancient frescoes. Visit the nearby Dambulla Cave Temple, famous for its rock-cut Buddha statues and wall paintings. Spend the evening at leisure in Sigiriya or your hotel, enjoying the lush surroundings.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Sigiriya to Nuwara Eliya | Scenic Hill Country Drive
activities: Depart Sigiriya and journey through Sri Lanka’s scenic hill country to Nuwara Eliya. Stop at tea plantations along the way to witness tea processing and sample fresh Ceylon tea. Explore Gregory Lake, stroll through the Nuwara Eliya town, and enjoy the cool mountain air before dinner at your hotel.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Nuwara Eliya – Horton Plains & World’s End
activities: Early morning excursion to Horton Plains National Park, trekking to World’s End, a dramatic cliff offering panoramic views of the valleys below. Return to Nuwara Eliya for leisure and optional local shopping. In the evening, enjoy a peaceful walk around Gregory Lake or a cozy dinner at your hotel.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Nuwara Eliya to Colombo | Departure
activities: After breakfast, drive back to Colombo. If time permits, visit Gangaramaya Temple, Independence Square, or Pettah Market. Later, transfer to Bandaranaike International Airport for your onward journey, leaving Sri Lanka with unforgettable memories of its cultural heritage, wildlife, and scenic landscapes.

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa to travel to Sri Lanka?
faqs.answer: Yes, an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) is required. It’s easy to apply online.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Sri Lanka?
faqs.answer: December–April for the west/south coast; May–September for the east coast.

faqs.question: How many days are ideal for a Sri Lanka trip?
faqs.answer: 6 to 8 days is perfect for a cultural and beach combo itinerary.

faqs.question: Is Sri Lanka safe for Indian tourists?

faqs.question: Is Indian currency accepted in Sri Lanka?

faqs.question: Are Indian meals available?

faqs.question: Can I drink alcohol in Sri Lanka?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is legal and widely available in hotels and restaurants.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation is available?
faqs.answer: From budget guesthouses to luxury beachfront resorts – all types are available.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, but highly recommended.

faqs.question: What should I wear in Sri Lanka?
faqs.answer: Light cotton clothes for the beach, and modest clothes for temples and hill stations.

faqs.question: Are local SIM cards available?
faqs.answer: Yes, very cheap and easy to buy at the airport or shops.

faqs.question: Can I self-drive or rent a car in Sri Lanka?
faqs.answer: Possible, but local drivers are recommended due to road conditions.

faqs.question: Are beaches safe for swimming?
faqs.answer: Most tourist beaches are safe, but always check local signs and currents.

faqs.question: Is tipping common?
faqs.answer: Yes, 5–10% is standard for guides, drivers, and restaurants.

faqs.question: Are there direct flights from India to Sri Lanka?
faqs.answer: Yes, from Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore, and more.

faqs.question: Can I customize my Sri Lanka package?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. TripDekhoo offers tailor-made itineraries for families, couples, or groups.

faqs.question: What activities are good for kids and families?
faqs.answer: Turtle hatcheries, safaris, beach fun, and tea plantation tours are kid-friendly.

faqs.question: Are there spiritual or wellness retreats?
faqs.answer: Yes, yoga, Ayurveda, and meditation centers are available across the country.

faqs.question: Is vegetarian food easily available?
faqs.answer: Yes, Sri Lankan cuisine has plenty of veg options.

faqs.question: How much does an average meal cost?
faqs.answer: Local meals cost ₹200–₹400; restaurant meals range from ₹500–₹1200 depending on the place.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Colombo | Evening Leisure
activities: Arrive at Bandaranaike International Airport and transfer to your hotel in Colombo. Spend your evening exploring Galle Face Green, watching locals fly kites and the sunset over the Indian Ocean. End the day with a welcome dinner featuring authentic Sri Lankan cuisine.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Colombo to Kandy | Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage & Temple of the Tooth
activities: Drive to Kandy after breakfast, stopping at Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage to see elephants being fed and bathed in the river. Continue to Kandy city and visit the Temple of the Tooth, one of Sri Lanka’s most sacred Buddhist sites. Stroll around Kandy Lake and explore the local markets. In the evening, enjoy a traditional cultural dance performance

itinerary.day: Day 3: Kandy to Sigiriya | Rock Fortress & Dambulla Cave Temple
activities: Travel to Sigiriya and climb the Sigiriya Rock Fortress, famous for its ancient frescoes and panoramic views. Visit the Dambulla Cave Temple, adorned with Buddha statues and murals. Spend the evening at leisure in Sigiriya, surrounded by lush landscapes.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Sigiriya to Nuwara Eliya | Scenic Hill Country Drive
activities: Journey through the picturesque hill country to Nuwara Eliya, stopping at tea plantations to witness tea production and sample Ceylon tea. Explore Gregory Lake and stroll through the town, enjoying the cool mountain air and colonial-era architecture.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Horton Plains & World’s End Excursion
activities: Early morning excursion to Horton Plains National Park, trekking to World’s End, a dramatic cliff with stunning valley views. Observe waterfalls, wildlife, and the pristine natural beauty. Return to Nuwara Eliya for leisure and optional sightseeing.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Nuwara Eliya to Ella / Adam’s Peak Excursion
activities: Drive to Ella, enjoying scenic landscapes, tea plantations, and waterfalls along the way. For early risers, consider an optional Adam’s Peak hike to witness a magical sunrise. In Ella, visit Nine Arches Bridge and Ravana Falls. Relax in the evening at a cozy hilltop café or your hotel.

itinerary.day: Day 7: Ella to Southern Beaches (Bentota / Mirissa)
activities: After breakfast, head to Sri Lanka’s southern coast for a relaxing beach stay in Bentota or Mirissa. Spend your day sunbathing, swimming, or enjoying water sports. Optional activities include whale watching (Mirissa), river cruises, or exploring nearby fishing villages. Enjoy a beachside dinner to end the day.

itinerary.day: Day 8: Departure from Colombo
activities: After breakfast, transfer back to Colombo. If time permits, explore Gangaramaya Temple, Independence Square, or Pettah Market. Proceed to Bandaranaike International Airport for your onward flight, taking with you unforgettable memories of Sri Lanka’s culture, mountains, and tropical coastlines.

packages.fagHeading: Top FAQs for Thailand Tour Package

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa for Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, Visa on Arrival is available. TripDekhoo can help pre-arrange it if needed.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Thailand?
faqs.answer: November to March offers pleasant weather; avoid monsoon season (July–Oct).

faqs.question: What’s the ideal duration for a Thailand trip?
faqs.answer: 5 to 7 days is great for a Bangkok–Pattaya or Phuket–Krabi combo.

faqs.question: Is Thailand suitable for family trips?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Family-friendly resorts and activities are widely available.

faqs.question: Can I combine multiple destinations in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes. Popular combos: Bangkok–Pattaya, Phuket–Krabi, or a full Thailand circuit.

faqs.question: What currency should I carry?
faqs.answer: Thai Baht (THB); you can carry USD or INR and convert in Thailand.

faqs.question: Is Indian food easily available?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially in tourist hubs like Bangkok, Pattaya, and Phuket.

faqs.question: Are Thailand packages budget-friendly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Thailand is one of the most affordable international destinations.

faqs.question: Can I add water sports or island tours to my plan?
faqs.answer: Yes. TripDekhoo offers customizable add-ons like scuba diving, parasailing, etc.

faqs.question: Is tipping mandatory in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, but small tips are appreciated for good service.

faqs.question: What clothing should I pack?
faqs.answer: Light casual wear, beachwear, and modest clothes for temples.

faqs.question: Is public transport safe in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, very safe – use Grab for convenience in cities.

faqs.question: Can I use international credit/debit cards?
faqs.answer: Yes, but small vendors prefer cash.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance required?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, but strongly recommended.

faqs.question: Are massages and spas safe and professional?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you choose certified and well-reviewed centers.

faqs.question: Is nightlife safe for tourists?
faqs.answer: Yes, but stay alert and avoid isolated areas late at night.

faqs.question: Can I rent a scooter or car in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you need an international driving permit.

faqs.question: Are there any religious or cultural restrictions?
faqs.answer: Avoid disrespect in temples, don’t climb Buddha statues, and dress appropriately.

faqs.question: Can I drink alcohol in public places?
faqs.answer: It’s legal in many areas but restricted near temples or on some public holidays.

faqs.question: Is Thailand safe for solo women travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, with general travel precautions in place.

itinerary.day: DAY 1: Arrival in Bangkok | Evening City & Nightlife
activities: Welcome to Thailand! Upon arrival at Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi Airport, you’ll be greeted by your tour representative and transferred to your hotel. After check-in, enjoy a short rest before heading out for an exciting evening city tour. Visit illuminated temples and vibrant street markets. Later, dive into Bangkok’s famous nightlife — from rooftop bars to buzzing night markets — soaking in the electric atmosphere. End the night with authentic Thai street food under the twinkling city lights.

itinerary.day: DAY 2: Bangkok City & Temple Tour | Chao Phraya River Cruise
activities: Begin your morning with a visit to Bangkok’s iconic temples: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn), Wat Pho (home to the Reclining Buddha), and the Grand Palace, a masterpiece of Thai architecture. Stroll through bustling local markets filled with tropical fruits, spices, and souvenirs. In the evening, enjoy a romantic Chao Phraya River cruise with dinner, watching the city skyline sparkle as you pass historic landmarks. The mix of tradition and modernity will leave you enchanted.

itinerary.day: DAY 3: Pattaya Coral Island Tour | Beach Activities
activities: After breakfast, transfer to Pattaya and board a speedboat to Coral Island (Koh Larn). Spend the day indulging in thrilling water sports like parasailing, snorkeling, and banana boat rides. Relax on pristine sandy beaches or enjoy fresh seafood by the sea. Later in the evening, witness the dazzling Alcazar Cabaret Show — a vibrant mix of lights, costumes, and performances. Return to the hotel for an overnight stay in Pattaya.

itinerary.day: DAY 4: Floating Market & Cultural Experiences
activities: Return to Bangkok for a visit to the famous Damnoen Saduak Floating Market. Glide through colorful canals on a longtail boat, shopping for local snacks, handicrafts, and tropical treats. Continue your cultural journey with a visit to Jim Thompson House — a beautiful museum showcasing Thai silk and architecture. Spend your last evening exploring Bangkok’s shopping malls or night bazaars for souvenirs and fashion finds.

itinerary.day: DAY 5: Departure from Bangkok
activities: Enjoy your final morning in Thailand with a leisurely breakfast. Depending on your flight schedule, you may have free time for last-minute shopping or a relaxing Thai massage. You’ll then be transferred to the airport for your onward journey, carrying with you the colors, flavors, and memories of your Thai adventure.

packages.fagHeading: Top FAQs for Thailand Tour Package

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa for Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, Visa on Arrival is available. TripDekhoo can help pre-arrange it if needed.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Thailand?
faqs.answer: November to March offers pleasant weather; avoid monsoon season (July–Oct).

faqs.question: What’s the ideal duration for a Thailand trip?
faqs.answer: 5 to 7 days is great for a Bangkok–Pattaya or Phuket–Krabi combo.

faqs.question: Is Thailand suitable for family trips?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Family-friendly resorts and activities are widely available.

faqs.question: Can I combine multiple destinations in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes. Popular combos: Bangkok–Pattaya, Phuket–Krabi, or a full Thailand circuit.

faqs.question: What currency should I carry?
faqs.answer: Thai Baht (THB); you can carry USD or INR and convert in Thailand.

faqs.question: Is Indian food easily available?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially in tourist hubs like Bangkok, Pattaya, and Phuket.

faqs.question: Are Thailand packages budget-friendly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Thailand is one of the most affordable international destinations.

faqs.question: Can I add water sports or island tours to my plan?
faqs.answer: Yes. TripDekhoo offers customizable add-ons like scuba diving, parasailing, etc.

faqs.question: Is tipping mandatory in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, but small tips are appreciated for good service.

faqs.question: What clothing should I pack?
faqs.answer: Light casual wear, beachwear, and modest clothes for temples.

faqs.question: Is public transport safe in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, very safe – use Grab for convenience in cities.

faqs.question: Can I use international credit/debit cards?
faqs.answer: Yes, but small vendors prefer cash.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance required?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, but strongly recommended.

faqs.question: Are massages and spas safe and professional?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you choose certified and well-reviewed centers.

faqs.question: Is nightlife safe for tourists?
faqs.answer: Yes, but stay alert and avoid isolated areas late at night.

faqs.question: Can I rent a scooter or car in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you need an international driving permit.

faqs.question: Are there any religious or cultural restrictions?
faqs.answer: Avoid disrespect in temples, don’t climb Buddha statues, and dress appropriately.

faqs.question: Can I drink alcohol in public places?
faqs.answer: It’s legal in many areas but restricted near temples or on some public holidays.

faqs.question: Is Thailand safe for solo women travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, with general travel precautions in place.

itinerary.day: DAY 1: Arrival in Bangkok | Evening Temple Tour & Night Bazaar
activities: Arrive at Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi Airport where your representative will greet you and transfer you to the hotel. After a short rest, head out for an evening exploration of Bangkok’s famous illuminated temples — Wat Arun and Wat Pho. Wander through Asiatique Night Bazaar, where the Chao Phraya River breeze meets lively street performances, boutiques, and food stalls. Try authentic Pad Thai or mango sticky rice before returning for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2: Bangkok City & Grand Palace Tour | Chao Phraya Cruise
activities: After breakfast, set out for a guided tour of Bangkok’s must-see attractions, starting with the Grand Palace, a magnificent blend of Thai and European architecture. Visit the Emerald Buddha Temple (Wat Phra Kaew) and stroll through Chinatown for a burst of colors and aromas. In the evening, embark on a luxurious Chao Phraya River cruise with dinner, passing landmarks like the Rama VIII Bridge and Wat Arun glowing under the night sky.

itinerary.day: DAY 3: Transfer to Pattaya | Coral Island Water Adventures
activities: This morning, travel to Pattaya and board a speedboat to Coral Island (Koh Larn). Spend the day soaking up the sun, swimming, or enjoying water sports like parasailing and snorkeling in crystal-clear waters. Feast on fresh seafood at a beachfront restaurant before returning to Pattaya. In the evening, witness the dazzling Alcazar Cabaret Show, known for its stunning costumes and energetic performances.

itinerary.day: DAY 4: Nong Nooch Tropical Garden & Cultural Village
activities: Explore Nong Nooch Tropical Garden, a beautifully landscaped park filled with themed gardens, elephant shows, and cultural performances. Experience traditional Thai dance and martial arts displays, followed by leisure time to enjoy Pattaya’s beachside cafes or local shopping streets. Sunset at Pattaya Viewpoint offers a perfect photo spot before heading back to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 5: Floating Market & Shopping in Bangkok
activities: Return to Bangkok and head to Damnoen Saduak Floating Market. Glide through canals lined with vendors selling tropical fruits, snacks, and handicrafts from colorful wooden boats. In the afternoon, enjoy free time exploring MBK Center or Siam Paragon for luxury shopping. For a cultural twist, visit Jim Thompson House, a preserved traditional Thai house showcasing silk weaving.

itinerary.day: DAY 6: Departure from Bangkok
activities: Enjoy your final Thai breakfast before being transferred to the airport. Depending on your flight time, you may squeeze in a quick Thai massage or last-minute souvenir shopping. Depart with a heart full of beaches, temples, flavors, and smiles.

itinerary.day: DAY 1: Arrival in Bangkok | Evening Temple & Night Market Tour
activities: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi Airport, meet your representative, and transfer to your hotel. After check-in, start your trip with an evening temple tour, visiting Wat Arun’s riverside beauty and Wat Pho’s massive reclining Buddha. End your night at the vibrant Asiatique Riverfront Night Bazaar, tasting Thai street delicacies and enjoying the river breeze before heading back for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2: Bangkok City Tour | Grand Palace & Chao Phraya Dinner Cruise
activities: Post breakfast, enjoy a full-day Bangkok city tour. Explore the majestic Grand Palace and Emerald Buddha Temple, walk through Chinatown’s busy lanes, and shop for souvenirs. Evening brings a magical Chao Phraya River dinner cruise — savor Thai delicacies while gliding past illuminated landmarks like the Rama VIII Bridge and Wat Arun sparkling under the night sky.

itinerary.day: DAY 3: Transfer to Pattaya | Coral Island Water Sports
activities: After breakfast, travel to Pattaya and head to Coral Island (Koh Larn) by speedboat. Relax on its pristine beaches or indulge in activities like parasailing, snorkeling, or banana boat rides. Lunch is served at a beachfront restaurant before returning. At night, enjoy the colorful Alcazar Cabaret Show with dazzling costumes and energetic performances.

itinerary.day: DAY 4: Nong Nooch Tropical Garden & Cultural Village
activities: Today’s adventure takes you to Nong Nooch Tropical Garden — famous for its themed gardens, elephant shows, and cultural performances. Experience traditional Thai dances, martial arts displays, and orchid gardens. Spend the evening exploring Pattaya Beach Road, filled with restaurants, bars, and souvenir shops.

itinerary.day: DAY 5: Transfer to Phuket | Leisure & Patong Beach
activities: Fly to Phuket, Thailand’s island paradise. Check in to your hotel and spend the afternoon unwinding at Patong Beach, known for its golden sands and water activities. In the evening, stroll through Bangla Road, famous for its vibrant nightlife, live music bars, and street performances.

itinerary.day: DAY 6: Phi Phi Island Tour with Lunch
activities: Sail across turquoise waters to the breathtaking Phi Phi Islands. Visit Maya Bay (famed from The Beach movie), swim in Loh Samah Bay, and snorkel at Pileh Lagoon. Enjoy a buffet lunch on Phi Phi Don before some free time for beach relaxation. Return to Phuket by evening for leisure.

itinerary.day: DAY 7: Departure from Phuket
activities: After breakfast, depending on your flight schedule, enjoy last-minute shopping or a quick Thai massage. Transfer to Phuket International Airport with unforgettable memories of temples, beaches, and island adventures.

packages.fagHeading: Top FAQs for Thailand Tour Package

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa for Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, Visa on Arrival is available. TripDekhoo can help pre-arrange it if needed.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Thailand?
faqs.answer: November to March offers pleasant weather; avoid monsoon season (July–Oct).

faqs.question: What’s the ideal duration for a Thailand trip?
faqs.answer: 5 to 7 days is great for a Bangkok–Pattaya or Phuket–Krabi combo.

faqs.question: Is Thailand suitable for family trips?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Family-friendly resorts and activities are widely available.

faqs.question: Can I combine multiple destinations in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes. Popular combos: Bangkok–Pattaya, Phuket–Krabi, or a full Thailand circuit.

faqs.question: What currency should I carry?
faqs.answer: Thai Baht (THB); you can carry USD or INR and convert in Thailand.

faqs.question: Is Indian food easily available?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially in tourist hubs like Bangkok, Pattaya, and Phuket.

faqs.question: Are Thailand packages budget-friendly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Thailand is one of the most affordable international destinations.

faqs.question: Can I add water sports or island tours to my plan?
faqs.answer: Yes. TripDekhoo offers customizable add-ons like scuba diving, parasailing, etc.

faqs.question: Is tipping mandatory in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, but small tips are appreciated for good service.

faqs.question: What clothing should I pack?
faqs.answer: Light casual wear, beachwear, and modest clothes for temples.

faqs.question: Is public transport safe in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, very safe – use Grab for convenience in cities.

faqs.question: Can I use international credit/debit cards?
faqs.answer: Yes, but small vendors prefer cash.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance required?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, but strongly recommended.

faqs.question: Are massages and spas safe and professional?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you choose certified and well-reviewed centers.

faqs.question: Is nightlife safe for tourists?
faqs.answer: Yes, but stay alert and avoid isolated areas late at night.

faqs.question: Can I rent a scooter or car in Thailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you need an international driving permit.

faqs.question: Are there any religious or cultural restrictions?
faqs.answer: Avoid disrespect in temples, don’t climb Buddha statues, and dress appropriately.

faqs.question: Can I drink alcohol in public places?
faqs.answer: It’s legal in many areas but restricted near temples or on some public holidays.

faqs.question: Is Thailand safe for solo women travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, with general travel precautions in place.

itinerary.day: DAY 1: Arrival in Bangkok | Evening City Stroll & Night Markets
activities: Land at Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi Airport and meet your travel representative. Transfer to your hotel for check-in and some rest. In the evening, take a guided stroll through Bangkok’s bustling night markets like Rod Fai Market or Asiatique Riverfront. itinerary.day: DAY 2: Bangkok City Tour | Grand Palace & Floating Market

Return to Bangkok for leisure and an optional evening rooftop dinner overlooking the city skyline.

itinerary.day: DAY 3: Ayutthaya Day Trip
activities: Travel to Ayutthaya, the ancient capital of Siam, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore ruins of royal temples like Wat Mahathat with its famous Buddha head entwined in tree roots. Enjoy a riverside lunch before returning to Bangkok in the evening, where you can relax or enjoy a traditional Thai massage.

itinerary.day: DAY 4: Transfer to Pattaya | Coral Island & Water Sports
activities: Head to Pattaya and board a speedboat for Coral Island (Koh Larn). Enjoy sunbathing or try water activities such as snorkeling, parasailing, or underwater walking. Lunch will be served at a beachside restaurant. In the evening, experience the dazzling Alcazar Cabaret Show, known for its colorful costumes and lively performances.

itinerary.day: DAY 5: Nong Nooch Tropical Garden & Pattaya Beach Leisure
activities: Spend the morning exploring Nong Nooch Tropical Garden’s themed landscapes, elephant performances, and cultural shows. Afternoon is free for relaxation at Pattaya Beach or to explore Walking Street for local food and nightlife.

itinerary.day: DAY 6: Flight to Phuket | Patong Beach & Nightlife
activities: Catch a morning flight to Phuket. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and spend the afternoon at Patong Beach. In the evening, explore Bangla Road — the epicenter of Phuket’s nightlife, filled with music, bars, and street performances.

itinerary.day: DAY 7: Phi Phi Island Tour with Lunch
activities: Embark on a speedboat journey to the world-famous Phi Phi Islands. Visit Maya Bay, snorkel in Pileh Lagoon, and swim in crystal-clear waters. Lunch will be served on Phi Phi Don Island, followed by some free time before returning to Phuket for your last evening in Thailand.

know_before_you_go: Visa Requirements: Most Indian travelers will require a Schengen Visa for this multi-country trip. Apply at least 6–8 weeks in advance.
Travel Insurance: Mandatory for Schengen countries, covering medical emergencies and trip cancellations.
Currency: Euro (€) is used in most countries on this itinerary; Switzerland uses the Swiss Franc (CHF).
Power Adapters: Carry a universal adapter (Type C, E, F) to match European sockets.
Weather & Clothing: Pack layers – Europe’s weather can change quickly, even in summer.
Language: English is widely understood in tourist areas, but learning basic greetings in French, Italian, and German adds charm to interactions.
Public Transport: Cities like Paris, Amsterdam, and Rome have excellent metro and tram systems — cheaper than taxis.
Tipping Culture: Not mandatory, but rounding up the bill or leaving 5–10% is appreciated.
Local SIM & Data: Consider buying an international SIM or eSIM with a Europe-wide data plan.
Tap Water Safety: Safe to drink in most European countries, including France, Germany, and Switzerland.
Cultural Etiquette: Dress modestly in churches, cathedrals, and the Vatican.
Walking Shoes: Expect a lot of walking on cobblestone streets — comfortable shoes are essential.
Punctuality: Trains and tours run on strict schedules — arrive early to avoid being left behind.
Currency Exchange: Exchange small amounts at airports and larger amounts in city centers for better rates.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Paris | Evening Seine River Cruise
activities: Welcome to the City of Lights! After arriving in Paris, check in to your hotel and relax. In the evening, embark on a magical Seine River cruise to admire the illuminated Eiffel Tower, Notre Dame Cathedral, and charming bridges. Feel the romantic charm of Paris as you sail under the twinkling night sky.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Paris City Tour & Eiffel Tower Experience
activities: Begin your day with a guided city tour covering the Champs-Élysées, Arc de Triomphe, and the Louvre’s iconic glass pyramid. Ascend to the 2nd level of the Eiffel Tower for panoramic city views. Later, stroll through Montmartre’s cobblestone streets, famous for its artists and cafés.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – Paris to Switzerland | Scenic Train Journey
activities: Board a high-speed train from Paris to Lucerne, Switzerland. Witness breathtaking views of the French and Swiss countryside along the way. Upon arrival, enjoy a lakeside walk and explore Lucerne’s Chapel Bridge, Water Tower, and Lion Monument.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Mount Titlis & Lucerne Exploration
activities: Experience the snow-covered paradise of Mount Titlis! Ride the world’s first rotating cable car, walk across the Cliff Suspension Bridge, and enjoy snow activities. Return to Lucerne for leisure time—perfect for chocolate shopping or relaxing by Lake Lucerne.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 – Lucerne to Venice | Gondola Ride Experience
activities: Travel through the Alps into Italy’s romantic city—Venice. Check in to your hotel and explore St. Mark’s Square, the Basilica, and the iconic Rialto Bridge. End your day with a traditional gondola ride through Venice’s charming canals.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 – Venice to Rome | Colosseum & Vatican City
activities: Depart for Rome, the Eternal City. Discover the mighty Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Trevi Fountain. In the afternoon, visit Vatican City to marvel at St. Peter’s Basilica and Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel masterpiece.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Departure from Rome
activities: Enjoy your final European breakfast before your transfer to the airport. Take with you timeless memories of Parisian romance, Swiss beauty, and Italian history.

activities: See the beauty of Paris unfold with a guided city tour covering Champs-Élysées, Arc de Triomphe, and the Louvre’s iconic pyramid. Then, ascend to the 2nd level of the Eiffel Tower for stunning views. End your evening wandering Montmartre’s romantic alleys.

activities: Journey into the floating city of Venice. Visit St. Mark’s Square, St. Mark’s Basilica, the Doge’s Palace, and the Rialto Bridge. End your day with a serene gondola ride along Venice’s canals.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 – Venice to Florence | Birthplace of the Renaissance
activities: Travel to Florence, where art and history come alive. Visit the Florence Cathedral, Piazza della Signoria, and Ponte Vecchio. Admire Michelangelo’s David at the Accademia Gallery before enjoying leisure time in this romantic city.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Florence to Rome | Ancient Wonders & Vatican City
activities: Travel to Rome and explore the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Trevi Fountain. Later, enter Vatican City to see St. Peter’s Basilica and the Sistine Chapel.

activities: Enjoy your final breakfast before departing. Carry home memories of Parisian romance, Swiss peaks, Venetian canals, and Italy’s timeless treasures.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Paris | Evening Seine River Cruise
activities: Land in the City of Lights! After a smooth transfer to your hotel, enjoy a relaxing evening cruise on the Seine River, admiring Paris’ illuminated landmarks and Eiffel Tower’s sparkling show.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Paris City Tour & Eiffel Tower Experience
activities: Dive into the romance of Paris with a guided tour covering Champs-Élysées, Arc de Triomphe, Louvre’s glass pyramid, and Notre Dame exterior. End with breathtaking views from the Eiffel Tower’s 2nd level.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – Versailles Palace & Gardens
activities: Step into royal history at the Palace of Versailles. Wander through opulent halls, grand gardens, and the Hall of Mirrors. Return to Paris for leisure shopping at Galeries Lafayette.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Paris to Lucerne | Lakeside Evening
activities: Board a scenic train to Lucerne, Switzerland. Spend the evening strolling along Chapel Bridge, the Water Tower, and Lake Lucerne’s tranquil promenade.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 – Mount Titlis Adventure
activities: Ride the world’s first rotating cable car to Mount Titlis. Enjoy snow activities, the Cliff Walk, and stunning alpine views before returning to Lucerne.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 – Interlaken & Lauterbrunnen Valley Excursion
activities: Explore Interlaken’s charming streets and continue to Lauterbrunnen Valley — a postcard-perfect landscape with 72 waterfalls. Optional Jungfraujoch trip for panoramic glacier views.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Lucerne to Venice | Gondola Ride
activities: Travel to Venice, the city of canals. Visit St. Mark’s Basilica, the Doge’s Palace, and Rialto Bridge, ending your evening with a romantic gondola ride.

itinerary.day: DAY 8 – Venice to Florence | Renaissance Highlights
activities: Discover Florence’s treasures: the Duomo, Piazza della Signoria, Ponte Vecchio, and Michelangelo’s David at the Accademia Gallery.

itinerary.day: DAY 9 – Florence to Rome | Ancient Wonders
activities: Arrive in Rome and step back in time at the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Pantheon. Toss a coin at the Trevi Fountain for luck.

itinerary.day: DAY 10 – Vatican City & Rome Leisure
activities: Visit Vatican City’s St. Peter’s Basilica, Sistine Chapel, and Vatican Museums. Spend your last Italian evening enjoying gelato and piazzas.

itinerary.day: DAY 11 – Rome to Barcelona | Departure
activities: Take a morning flight to Barcelona. Depending on your departure time, explore Las Ramblas and Gothic Quarter before your onward flight, carrying memories of Europe’s best.

testimonals.name: Aarav & Kiara
testimonals.review: Our Europe honeymoon was nothing short of a fairytale! Tripdekhoo took care of everything — from Schengen visas to curated local experiences. Watching the sunset over the Swiss Alps, enjoying gondola rides in Venice, and sipping wine in Tuscany were memories we’ll cherish forever. The romantic touches they added made the trip even more special.

testimonals.name: The Reddys
testimonals.review: Traveling to Europe with kids and parents was a challenge we didn’t want to handle on our own, and Tripdekhoo came to the rescue. We covered Paris, Amsterdam, and Switzerland over 12 days, with well-timed breaks, Indian meals, and skip-the-line passes for major attractions. The coordination was flawless — we didn’t feel rushed once!

testimonals.name: Isha Gupta
testimonals.review: As a solo female traveler, I was a bit hesitant at first, but Tripdekhoo crafted a fantastic itinerary across Prague, Budapest, and Krakow. The hostels were safe and centrally located, and I met fellow travelers easily. Walking tours, river cruises, and local cuisines — it was liberating, fun, and very affordable too!

testimonals.name: Singhania Group
testimonals.review: Our 10-member group trip to Europe was an experience of pure class. Tripdekhoo arranged business class flights, premium stays in Paris and Lucerne, and private vehicles throughout. From champagne at the Eiffel Tower to a Michelin-star dinner in Rome — every moment was curated to perfection. True luxury at its finest.

testimonals.name: Siddharth & Tanya
testimonals.review: We wanted to experience Europe like locals — on a budget. Tripdekhoo helped us with Eurail passes, hostel bookings, and daily metro guidance. We covered 5 countries in 15 days and still stayed within our budget! Even the free walking tours and night buses were suggested by them. We couldn’t have done this on our own!

testimonals.name: Verma Family
testimonals.review: Europe with kids can be overwhelming, but Tripdekhoo made it a joy. They included fun spots like Disneyland Paris, LEGOLAND in Germany, and a chocolate factory in Switzerland. Our kids were thrilled, and we parents had the time to enjoy the culture and history. Everything was age-appropriate and exciting!

testimonals.name: Ritika & Sahil
testimonals.review: We booked a romantic getaway with Tripdekhoo, and it was magical. Eiffel Tower at night, river cruise on the Seine, and a surprise candlelight dinner in Prague were unforgettable highlights. The hotels were boutique-style with character and charm. The itinerary had just the right amount of leisure and exploration.

testimonals.name: Neha Bansal
testimonals.review: Traveling with my all-women’s group across Europe was both safe and empowering. Tripdekhoo arranged local female guides in cities like Vienna and Florence and made sure every hotel was well-reviewed and centrally located. We laughed, we explored, and we bonded over culture and coffee!

testimonals.name: Deepak Shah
testimonals.review: My wife and I have always dreamed of Europe, and Tripdekhoo made it a reality — without the stress. We were given a slow-paced itinerary with short walks, Indian food options, and wheelchair assistance at airports. From the Alps to Amsterdam canals, every stop was peaceful and rejuvenating.

testimonals.name: Sana & Ayaan
testimonals.review: We’re both art and history lovers, and Tripdekhoo gave us the perfect cultural route — Rome, Florence, Vienna, and Berlin. They arranged museum passes, opera tickets, and private walking tours with passionate local guides. It felt like stepping back in time while enjoying the best of today.

testimonals.name: Tarun Mehta
testimonals.review: As a remote worker, I took a 3-week workation across Spain and Portugal. Tripdekhoo arranged co-working-friendly hotels, SIM cards, and seamless Wi-Fi. I worked from rooftop cafes in Lisbon and beaches in Barcelona. The weekends were packed with tapas trails and Flamenco shows. It was the best mix of work and wanderlust!

testimonals.name: Shalini & Kartik
testimonals.review: We wanted a festive European experience, and Tripdekhoo curated the perfect winter itinerary. We explored Christmas markets in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. The snow, lights, mulled wine, and holiday magic was something we’ll never forget. They even included a special Christmas Eve dinner for us!

testimonals.name: Ravi Chopra
testimonals.review: Our college gang reunited for a Eurotrip after 10 years. Tripdekhoo handled our crazy demands — from clubbing in Berlin to hiking in the Dolomites and staying in a castle in Slovenia. Every night was a new adventure. They nailed the balance between fun, comfort, and affordability!

testimonals.name: Bhavna Arora
testimonals.review: I wanted to explore Europe's sacred sites and Tripdekhoo curated a meaningful itinerary — Vatican City, Lourdes, the Cologne Cathedral, and even the Camino de Santiago trail in Spain. The experience was reflective, spiritual, and deeply personal. I’m grateful for how they tailored it to my needs.

testimonals.name: The Kapoors
testimonals.review: For our 25th anniversary, we asked Tripdekhoo for something unique — and they delivered! We visited Iceland for the Northern Lights and then relaxed in the countryside of Scotland. They added surprises like a winery tour, a handwritten card, and a spa voucher. This wasn’t just a vacation — it was an emotional celebration.

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa for Europe?
faqs.answer: Yes, usually a Schengen visa is required for most European countries.

faqs.question: How long does visa processing take?
faqs.answer: Typically 15 calendar days, apply 3-4 weeks in advance.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Europe?
faqs.answer: Spring (Apr-Jun) and Autumn (Sep-Nov) are ideal.

faqs.question: What currency should I carry?
faqs.answer: Euro for most countries, GBP for UK, CHF for Switzerland.

faqs.question: Can I use credit/debit cards everywhere?
faqs.answer: Yes, but carry some cash for small vendors and transport.

faqs.question: Is tipping mandatory in Europe?
faqs.answer: Usually not mandatory but appreciated (5-10% in restaurants).

faqs.question: Are Indian meals available?
faqs.answer: Indian restaurants are available in major cities.

faqs.question: How to travel between European cities?
faqs.answer: Trains, flights, and buses are commonly used.

faqs.question: Are guided tours included?
faqs.answer: Yes, as per the package.

faqs.question: Can I use mobile internet easily?
faqs.answer: Yes, buy a European SIM or use international roaming.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for travel?
faqs.answer: Passport, visa, travel insurance, hotel bookings.

faqs.question: Are public transport and metro safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, widely used by locals and tourists.

faqs.question: Can I take carry-on luggage only?
faqs.answer: Depends on airline and trip duration.

faqs.question: Are there any cultural etiquette tips?
faqs.answer: Greet politely, respect local customs, avoid loud conversations.

faqs.question: How to book tickets for popular attractions?
faqs.answer: Online in advance to avoid long queues.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance necessary?
faqs.answer: Yes, highly recommended and sometimes mandatory.

faqs.question: What language do locals speak?
faqs.answer: Depends on country; English common in tourist areas.

faqs.question: What are must-see attractions?
faqs.answer: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Big Ben, Sagrada Familia, Louvre.

faqs.question: Can I combine multiple countries in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, multi-country tours are popular.

faqs.question: How early should I book my Europe trip?
faqs.answer: At least 1-2 months in advance, more for peak season.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival in Paris | Evening at Leisure
activities: Welcome to the enchanting city of Paris! As you step out of the airport, the charm of cobbled streets, chic cafés, and the distant silhouette of the Eiffel Tower set the tone for your adventure. After checking in to your hotel, take a gentle stroll through the neighborhood, stopping for fresh croissants and rich coffee at a local patisserie. In the evening, relax by the River Seine as the golden glow of sunset reflects off its calm waters. Your European dream begins with the magic of Paris wrapping around you.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Paris City Tour & Seine River Cruise
activities: Today is all about Parisian icons! Stand in awe before the Eiffel Tower, stroll along the Champs-Élysées, and feel the history inside Notre-Dame Cathedral. The air is filled with the aroma of fresh baguettes and street music as you wander the art-filled lanes of Montmartre. As night falls, step aboard a Seine River cruise, watching the city sparkle in golden lights while the Eiffel Tower shimmers like a diamond. It’s a moment that makes you fall in love with Paris all over again.

itinerary.day: Day 3 – Paris to Brussels | Brussels City Highlights
activities: Leaving Paris behind, you arrive in Brussels, where the grandeur of the Grand Place welcomes you. Ornate guildhalls and the scent of Belgian waffles fill the square as locals and travelers mingle. Discover the quirky charm of the Manneken Pis and indulge in rich, velvety Belgian chocolate. The evening is perfect for sipping beer in a centuries-old café while watching the city’s nightlife come alive.

itinerary.day: Day 4 – Brussels to Amsterdam | Evening Canal Cruise
activities: A scenic journey takes you to Amsterdam, a city laced with dreamy canals and vibrant flower markets. Check into your hotel, then glide through the waterways on a canal cruise as gabled houses reflect in the water. Hear stories of old merchant days as you pass under arched bridges lit with twinkling lights. End your evening strolling through the Jordaan district, where art galleries and cozy cafés create a perfect backdrop for a relaxed night.

itinerary.day: Day 5 – Amsterdam City Tour & Zaanse Schans Windmills
activities: Step into the charm of Dutch heritage today with visits to the iconic windmills of Zaanse Schans. Watch traditional clog-making and taste creamy local cheeses. Back in the city, cycle along the canals or explore the Van Gogh Museum, soaking in the vibrant colors of his masterpieces. As the sun sets, sip hot chocolate by a canal-side café, letting the cool breeze carry the scent of tulips.

itinerary.day: Day 6 – Amsterdam to Cologne | Cologne Cathedral & Old Town
activities: The gothic spires of Cologne Cathedral greet you as you arrive in Germany. Inside, the stained glass tells centuries-old stories bathed in colored light. Wander through the cobbled streets of the Old Town, discovering quaint shops selling artisanal bread and handcrafted trinkets. As evening falls, enjoy a hearty German meal with a view of the Rhine River under a starlit sky.

itinerary.day: Day 7 – Cologne to Lucerne | Evening Lake Stroll
activities: Switzerland welcomes you with snow-capped peaks and crystal-clear lakes. After arriving in Lucerne, explore the famous Chapel Bridge and Water Tower, their wooden beams rich with history. The cool mountain air refreshes you as you stroll by Lake Lucerne, watching swans glide gracefully across the water. The peaceful charm of this lakeside town is the perfect pause in your journey.

itinerary.day: Day 8 – Mt. Titlis Excursion
activities: Adventure awaits as you ascend to Mt. Titlis, passing through layers of snowy wonder on rotating cable cars. At the summit, step onto the thrilling Cliff Walk for panoramic views of the Alps stretching endlessly into the horizon. Play in the snow, take breathtaking photos, and breathe in the pure mountain air. Returning to Lucerne, warm up with Swiss hot chocolate and fondue.

itinerary.day: Day 9 – Lucerne to Venice | Evening Gondola Ride
activities: Cross the Swiss border into Italy’s romantic gem — Venice. Glide through the narrow canals in a gondola, the gondolier’s song echoing softly against ancient stone walls. Wander through St. Mark’s Square, surrounded by grand architecture and the sound of live orchestras. As the evening deepens, the reflections of lanterns dance on the water, creating pure magic.

itinerary.day: Day 10 – Venice to Florence | Renaissance Wonders
activities: Travel to Florence, the cradle of the Renaissance. Admire Michelangelo’s David and the magnificent Florence Cathedral, its dome a marvel of human creativity. The streets hum with life as artisans sell leather goods and gelato shops tempt you with endless flavors. A golden sunset over the Arno River seals the day in memory.

itinerary.day: Day 11 – Florence to Rome | Roman Icons
activities: Arrive in the Eternal City, where history greets you at every turn. Stand inside the mighty Colosseum, imagining the roar of ancient crowds. Toss a coin into the Trevi Fountain, making a wish for your return. In the evening, dine al fresco with views of the illuminated Pantheon.

itinerary.day: Day 12 – Vatican City & Rome Farewell
activities: Explore the treasures of Vatican City, from the grandeur of St. Peter’s Basilica to the breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Walk through the Vatican Museums, where centuries of art and history unfold before you. Your last evening in Rome calls for a farewell feast with pasta, wine, and laughter, under the Roman night sky.

itinerary.day: Day 13 – Departure from Rome
activities: With your heart full of unforgettable memories, bid farewell to Europe. The morning is free for one last espresso at a local café before your airport transfer. As your flight takes off, you look out at the patchwork of cities, mountains, and seas, already dreaming of your return.

destinations.about: At Tripdekhoo, we prioritize exceptional customer service and seamless experiences. From hotels, visas, and flights to sightseeing and end-to-end transfers, we take care of everything so you can travel stress-free.

packages.subTitle: (Covers Nairobi city highlights, Maasai Mara game drives, Lake Naivasha boat safari, and visit to the Great Rift Valley)

testimonals.name: Rohan & Sneha
testimonals.review: Our Kenya safari was nothing short of magical! Watching the Great Migration in the Maasai Mara was a bucket-list moment. Tripdekhoo arranged a luxury tented camp right in the heart of the reserve. Seeing lions, cheetahs, and elephants up close with expert guides was surreal. Every day felt like a National Geographic episode come to life!

testimonals.name: Aliya & Sameer
testimonals.review: Who says honeymoons have to be on a beach? Ours in Kenya was adventurous, romantic, and unforgettable. We had candlelight dinners in the wild, hot air balloon rides at sunrise, and serene moments watching giraffes from our lodge balcony. Tripdekhoo handled everything — from visas to custom decor — and made us feel special throughout.

testimonals.name: Malhotra Family
testimonals.review: Kenya was our first family safari and Tripdekhoo curated it perfectly. Our kids were thrilled to see zebras, wildebeests, and hippos in their natural habitat. The guides were so child-friendly and even arranged a junior ranger program. We stayed at family lodges with all amenities — safe, clean, and full of excitement!

testimonals.name: Tanya Singh
testimonals.review: As a solo traveler, I wanted a safe, well-paced, and meaningful experience — and Tripdekhoo made it happen. From Nairobi to Lake Naivasha and Maasai Mara, everything was smooth. My guides were respectful, knowledgeable, and empowering. The cultural interaction with the Maasai tribe was deeply touching.

testimonals.name: Joshi Group
testimonals.review: We were a group of 6 friends seeking thrill and nature, and Kenya blew us away! From off-road safaris to boat rides in Lake Nakuru, every day had a new adventure. Tripdekhoo even added a bush dinner and a surprise sundowner. The coordination between guides, drivers, and camps was spot on.

testimonals.name: Kavita & Arjun
testimonals.review: Kenya is a paradise for wildlife photographers. We saw a cheetah chase, lion cubs at play, and even a leopard on a tree. Tripdekhoo ensured we had a guide who understood light angles and animal behavior. The early morning game drives were gold. This was the most productive photography trip we’ve ever taken!

testimonals.name: Dr. Ramesh & Family
testimonals.review: We were four couples in our 60s and were a bit unsure about doing an African safari — but Tripdekhoo changed our perception. They arranged senior-friendly vehicles, shorter drives, and luxury lodges with medical facilities nearby. We saw the Big Five and enjoyed every moment in comfort and safety.

testimonals.name: Fatima Khan
testimonals.review: I always wanted to combine wildlife with authentic African culture, and Kenya gave me that. know_before_you_go: Best Time to Visit: June to October for the Great Migration in Maasai Mara; January to February for bird watching and dry season game viewing.
Climate: Varies by region – expect warm days and cool mornings/evenings in the highlands; hotter, drier conditions in Tsavo and Amboseli.
Currency: Kenyan Shilling (KES); carry small denominations for tips and small purchases.
Language: English and Swahili are official languages; knowing basic Swahili phrases can be helpful.
Visa: Most nationalities require an eVisa; apply online before departure.
Vaccinations: Yellow fever vaccination is mandatory; also recommended – Hepatitis A/B, Typhoid, and routine shots.
Malaria Precautions: Carry anti-malarial medication and insect repellent.
Luggage Limit: If taking domestic flights, soft-sided bags with a 15 kg limit are usually required.
Safari Dress Code: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, beige, olive) to blend with the environment; avoid bright colors.
Electricity: Voltage is 240V; plug type G (UK style). Carry a universal adapter.
Water: Drink only bottled or purified water; avoid ice in drinks outside lodges.
Tipping Etiquette: Common practice is $10–20 per person per day for guides and $5–10 per day for lodge staff.
Photography: Ask before photographing locals; use telephoto lenses for wildlife to maintain a safe distance.
Park Entry Rules: Stay in your vehicle unless in designated areas; follow your guide’s instructions.
Wildlife Etiquette: Do not feed or provoke animals; it’s dangerous and illegal.
Connectivity: Mobile coverage is good in urban areas, limited in remote parks; many lodges offer Wi-Fi.
Food: Most lodges offer international cuisine; try local specialties like nyama choma (roast meat) and ugali.
Time Zone: GMT+3, with no daylight savings.
Travel Insurance: Strongly recommended, covering medical evacuation.
Cash & Cards: ATMs are available in cities; carry cash for rural areas and tipping.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Nairobi | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Kenya! Upon arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, you’ll be greeted by our representative and transferred to your hotel in Nairobi. After check-in, unwind and soak in the bustling yet charming vibe of the city. Take a relaxed evening walk, explore local cafes, or enjoy the hotel’s amenities. If time permits, visit a nearby market for a taste of Kenyan culture. As the sun sets, prepare yourself for the wildlife adventures that await in the coming days.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Nairobi to Amboseli National Park | Afternoon Safari
activities: After breakfast, embark on a scenic drive to Amboseli National Park, famed for its views of Mount Kilimanjaro and large elephant herds. Upon arrival, check into your lodge and enjoy lunch. In the afternoon, head out for your first game drive, spotting elephants, lions, cheetahs, and exotic birdlife against the backdrop of Africa’s highest peak. Return to your lodge for a warm dinner under the star-lit African sky, where the sounds of the wild create a magical soundtrack to your evening.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – Morning Safari in Amboseli | Transfer to Lake Naivasha
activities: Rise early for a morning safari, when wildlife is most active. Watch the golden sunrise paint the savannah, with grazing zebras and antelopes completing the scene. After breakfast, drive towards Lake Naivasha, known for its serene waters and abundant birdlife. Upon arrival, check in and relax before heading out for a boat ride on the lake, where you might spot hippos lounging in the water and exotic birds perched on acacia trees. End the day with a peaceful dinner at your lodge.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Lake Naivasha to Maasai Mara | Afternoon Game Drive
activities: After breakfast, set out for the legendary Maasai Mara National Reserve, home to the Great Migration and the Big Five. Arrive at your lodge in time for lunch. In the afternoon, enjoy an exciting game drive across the vast plains, where you may encounter lions lazing in the sun, giraffes striding gracefully, and elephants on the move. As dusk falls, return to your lodge, savor a hearty dinner, and share safari stories by the campfire.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 – Morning Safari in Maasai Mara | Departure
activities: Begin your day with a final sunrise safari, capturing those last magical moments with Africa’s wildlife. After breakfast, bid farewell to the Mara and drive back to Nairobi for your onward flight. Your heart will be filled with unforgettable sights, sounds, and stories from the Kenyan wilderness, ready to share with friends and family back home.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Nairobi | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Kenya! Upon arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, our representative will greet you and transfer you to your hotel in Nairobi. After check-in, relax and enjoy the vibrant city atmosphere. You may take a short walk to a nearby market or enjoy the hotel’s amenities. Rest well tonight — your safari adventure is about to begin.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Nairobi to Amboseli National Park | Afternoon Safari
activities: After breakfast, depart for Amboseli National Park, renowned for its elephant herds and spectacular views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Arrive for lunch at your lodge, then head out for your first game drive, spotting lions, cheetahs, buffaloes, and colorful birdlife. As dusk falls, return for dinner under the starlit African sky.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – Full Day in Amboseli National Park
activities: Wake early for a morning safari, when the light is golden, and wildlife is most active. Capture photos of elephants with Mount Kilimanjaro in the background. Return for lunch and some rest before heading out on an afternoon game drive to explore different parts of the park. Spend your evening by the lodge fire, surrounded by the sounds of the wild.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Amboseli to Lake Naivasha | Boat Ride
activities: Enjoy breakfast before driving through scenic highlands towards Lake Naivasha. After lunch at your lodge, take a peaceful boat ride, spotting hippos, fish eagles, and kingfishers. As the sun sets, enjoy the tranquil atmosphere of the lake before returning for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 – Lake Naivasha to Maasai Mara | Afternoon Game Drive
activities: Today you’ll journey to the legendary Maasai Mara National Reserve. After check-in and lunch, head out for an afternoon game drive, where you may spot lions, zebras, wildebeests, and perhaps even a leopard resting in a tree. Return for dinner and experience the magic of the Mara at night.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 – Full Day in Maasai Mara
activities: Spend the day exploring the vast plains of the Maasai Mara, with both morning and afternoon safaris. Witness incredible wildlife encounters, from elephants grazing to cheetahs on the hunt. Visit a local Maasai village to learn about their traditions and culture. In the evening, relax with dinner and soak in the unforgettable safari atmosphere.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Morning Safari in Maasai Mara | Departure from Nairobi
activities: On your final day, take a sunrise game drive for those last magical moments in the wild. After breakfast, drive back to Nairobi for your departure flight, carrying memories of Africa’s incredible wildlife and landscapes.

testimonals.review: Kenya was our first family safari and Tripdekhoo curated it perfectly. Our kids were thrilled to see zebras, wildebeests, and hippos in their natural habitat. The guides were so child-friendly and even arranged a junior ranger program. We stayed at family lodges with all amenities — safe, clean, and full of excitement!

testimonals.name: Tanya Singh
testimonals.review: As a solo traveler, I wanted a safe, well-paced, and meaningful experience — and Tripdekhoo made it happen. From Nairobi to Lake Naivasha and Maasai Mara, everything was smooth. My guides were respectful, knowledgeable, and empowering. The cultural interaction with the Maasai tribe was deeply touching.

testimonals.name: Joshi Group
testimonals.review: We were a group of 6 friends seeking thrill and nature, and Kenya blew us away! From off-road safaris to boat rides in Lake Nakuru, every day had a new adventure. Tripdekhoo even added a bush dinner and a surprise sundowner. The coordination between guides, drivers, and camps was spot on.

testimonals.name: Kavita & Arjun
testimonals.review: Kenya is a paradise for wildlife photographers. We saw a cheetah chase, lion cubs at play, and even a leopard on a tree. Tripdekhoo ensured we had a guide who understood light angles and animal behavior. The early morning game drives were gold. This was the most productive photography trip we’ve ever taken!

testimonals.name: Dr. Ramesh & Family
testimonals.review: We were four couples in our 60s and were a bit unsure about doing an African safari — but Tripdekhoo changed our perception. They arranged senior-friendly vehicles, shorter drives, and luxury lodges with medical facilities nearby. We saw the Big Five and enjoyed every moment in comfort and safety.

testimonals.name: Fatima Khan
testimonals.review: I always wanted to combine wildlife with authentic African culture, and Kenya gave me that. Tripdekhoo included a village visit where we danced with the Maasai and learned about their traditions. The contrast of wild safaris and deep cultural immersion was powerful. A transformative journey for the soul!

testimonals.name: Aman Sethi
testimonals.review: This wasn’t just a vacation; it was an experience in elegance. Tripdekhoo booked us into award-winning safari lodges with gourmet dining, private decks, and even open-air bathtubs overlooking the savannah. Private guides, wine under the stars, and zero worries — that’s how luxury travel should be.

testimonals.name: Bhavna & Prakash
testimonals.review: We didn’t want to just check animals off a list — we wanted to connect with nature. Tripdekhoo’s slow safari approach gave us time to appreciate the landscapes, birds, and sunsets. We visited Amboseli, where Mount Kilimanjaro loomed in the background. It was peaceful, grounding, and awe-inspiring.

testimonals.name: Rajat & Nidhi
testimonals.review: Kenya was our first international trip and we were nervous. But Tripdekhoo handled everything — from flights, insurance, and currency exchange to daily support on WhatsApp. We saw animals we had only read about in books. This was more than a trip — it was a dream turned real!

testimonals.name: Shalini Verma
testimonals.review: This trip wasn’t just about seeing wildlife — it was about feeling nature's rhythm. The silence of the plains, the early morning sounds of birds, and the peaceful coexistence of animals left me transformed. Tripdekhoo even arranged eco-stays that aligned with my values. Kenya touched my heart.

testimonals.name: The Aroras
testimonals.review: We traveled with grandparents, teens, and toddlers, and everyone came back happy. Tripdekhoo made adjustments in route, meals, and rest breaks. The lodges were family-friendly and even offered babysitting so we could go on a night safari. Truly a trip for all ages!

testimonals.name: Vikram Jain
testimonals.review: I always thought African safaris were only for the rich. But Tripdekhoo proved otherwise. They planned a well-balanced, budget-friendly trip with tented camps, shared game drives, and local meals. I didn’t miss out on anything and even got to see lions up close!

testimonals.name: Sana & Meher
testimonals.review: Kenya was bold, beautiful, and beyond expectation. Tripdekhoo ensured we were paired with a female safari guide who made us feel completely comfortable. We danced with the locals, spotted a rhino at Lake Nakuru, and ended the trip with a beach extension in Diani. Safe, empowering, and unforgettable!

know_before_you_go: Best Time to Visit: June to October for the Great Migration in Maasai Mara; January to February for bird watching and dry season game viewing.
Climate: Varies by region – expect warm days and cool mornings/evenings in the highlands; hotter, drier conditions in Tsavo and Amboseli.
Currency: Kenyan Shilling (KES); carry small denominations for tips and small purchases.
Language: English and Swahili are official languages; knowing basic Swahili phrases can be helpful.
Visa: Most nationalities require an eVisa; apply online before departure.
Vaccinations: Yellow fever vaccination is mandatory; also recommended – Hepatitis A/B, Typhoid, and routine shots.
Malaria Precautions: Carry anti-malarial medication and insect repellent.
Luggage Limit: If taking domestic flights, soft-sided bags with a 15 kg limit are usually required.
Safari Dress Code: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, beige, olive) to blend with the environment; avoid bright colors.
Electricity: Voltage is 240V; plug type G (UK style). Carry a universal adapter.
Water: Drink only bottled or purified water; avoid ice in drinks outside lodges.
Tipping Etiquette: Common practice is $10–20 per person per day for guides and $5–10 per day for lodge staff.
Photography: Ask before photographing locals; use telephoto lenses for wildlife to maintain a safe distance.
Park Entry Rules: Stay in your vehicle unless in designated areas; follow your guide’s instructions.
Wildlife Etiquette: Do not feed or provoke animals; it’s dangerous and illegal.
Connectivity: Mobile coverage is good in urban areas, limited in remote parks; many lodges offer Wi-Fi.
Food: Most lodges offer international cuisine; try local specialties like nyama choma (roast meat) and ugali.
Time Zone: GMT+3, with no daylight savings.
Travel Insurance: Strongly recommended, covering medical evacuation.
Cash & Cards: ATMs are available in cities; carry cash for rural areas and tipping.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Nairobi | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Kenya! Upon arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, meet our representative and transfer to your hotel in Nairobi. After check-in, relax and enjoy the city’s vibrant atmosphere. If time allows, visit a local market or simply unwind at your hotel, preparing for the wildlife adventure ahead.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Nairobi to Amboseli National Park | Afternoon Safari
activities: After breakfast, travel to Amboseli National Park, famous for its large elephant herds and Mount Kilimanjaro backdrop. After lunch, head out for your first game drive, spotting lions, cheetahs, zebras, and giraffes. As evening falls, enjoy dinner at your lodge with the sounds of the African wilderness around you.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – Full Day in Amboseli National Park
activities: Rise early for a morning safari to see wildlife in the golden sunrise light. Capture unforgettable shots of elephants with snow-capped Kilimanjaro in the background. Return for lunch, then venture out again for an afternoon game drive before relaxing at your lodge.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Amboseli to Aberdare National Park
activities: After breakfast, drive to Aberdare National Park, a lush mountainous region known for its waterfalls, rainforests, and rare animals like the bongo antelope. Check into your lodge (often with viewing decks overlooking watering holes where animals gather). Spend the evening spotting nocturnal wildlife from the comfort of your lodge

itinerary.day: DAY 5 – Aberdare to Lake Naivasha | Boat Ride
activities: This morning, travel to Lake Naivasha, a freshwater lake teeming with hippos and birdlife. After lunch, take a boat safari, gliding past hippos, pelicans, and fish eagles. Return to your lodge for a tranquil evening by the lakeside.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 – Lake Naivasha to Maasai Mara | Afternoon Safari
activities: Drive to the world-famous Maasai Mara National Reserve, home to the Big Five and the Great Migration (seasonal). After check-in and lunch, enjoy an afternoon game drive, spotting lions lounging, wildebeests grazing, and elephants roaming. As the sun sets, return to your lodge for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Full Day in Maasai Mara
activities: Spend the day exploring the Mara with morning and afternoon safaris. From graceful giraffes to powerful predators, every moment is a wildlife spectacle. Visit a Maasai village to learn about their culture, traditions, and colorful attire. Return to your lodge for dinner under a starlit sky

itinerary.day: DAY 8 – Morning Safari in Maasai Mara | Return to Nairobi
activities: Begin with a sunrise game drive for a last chance to spot elusive wildlife. After breakfast, drive back to Nairobi. In the evening, you can shop for souvenirs or enjoy a farewell dinner at a local restaurant. Overnight in Nairobi.

itinerary.day: DAY 9 – Departure from Nairobi
activities: After breakfast, transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your flight home, carrying unforgettable memories of Kenya’s landscapes, wildlife, and culture.
