itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Nairobi | Day at Leisure
activities: Karibu Kenya! Your journey begins as you land at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi. A warm smile from our representative greets you, followed by a smooth transfer to your hotel. As you drive through the bustling streets, you’ll notice Nairobi’s unique blend of modern city life and hints of Africa’s wild charm. Once checked in, take time to relax and adjust to the rhythm of the land. Depending on your arrival time, you might wander through a local craft market, tasting Kenyan coffee and seeing colorful beadwork handmade by artisans. In the evening, enjoy a leisurely dinner at the hotel, with the distant hum of the city around you, and let the excitement for your safari adventure build.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Nairobi to Amboseli National Park | Afternoon Safari
activities: After a hearty breakfast, you set off for Amboseli National Park, a place where elephants roam in front of Africa’s highest mountain — the snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro. The drive is filled with scenic views of open savannahs, rural homesteads, and acacia-dotted plains. Arriving at your lodge in time for lunch, you enjoy a refreshing rest before heading out for your first afternoon game drive. The golden light of the setting sun paints the landscape, and the sight of a large elephant herd moving gracefully across the plains leaves you speechless. Lions laze in the grass, giraffes nibble on acacia trees, and the air carries the distinct sounds of the African wild. As darkness falls, return to the lodge for a delicious dinner, the silhouette of Kilimanjaro faintly visible against the night sky.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – Full Day in Amboseli National Park
activities: Your day begins before sunrise, as you step out into the cool morning air for a morning safari. The sky turns pink, then gold, illuminating the majestic Kilimanjaro in the background. Elephants, their tusks gleaming in the sunlight, move slowly across the grasslands. Predators like cheetahs and lions are most active at this hour, and you might witness a thrilling hunt. After returning for a hearty breakfast, you relax at the lodge, perhaps enjoying a dip in the pool or simply gazing out at the stunning scenery. In the afternoon, another game drive takes you deeper into Amboseli’s wetlands and open plains, where birdlife is abundant and the photography opportunities are endless. Dinner is served under a blanket of stars, with the distant call of hyenas echoing through the night.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Amboseli to Tsavo West National Park
activities: Leaving Amboseli, you journey to Tsavo West National Park, a land of striking contrasts — rolling volcanic hills, lush springs, and rugged savannah. After lunch at your lodge, set off on a game drive to discover Tsavo’s famous red elephants, coated in the park’s rust-colored soil. You’ll visit the crystal-clear waters of Mzima Springs, where hippos wallow lazily and fish dart through the shallows. Keep an eye out for leopards draped over tree branches, and listen to the rich symphony of bird calls that fill the air. Evening brings a spectacular African sunset over the Chyulu Hills, followed by a cozy dinner back at your lodge.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 – Full Day in Tsavo West National Park
activities: This day is dedicated to fully exploring Tsavo West. After breakfast, head out for a full-day game drive, covering its varied landscapes — from lava flows to dense bush and open plains. The Shetani Lava Flow, a stark black expanse formed by ancient volcanic activity, stands in dramatic contrast to the greenery around it. Wildlife sightings are plentiful, with herds of zebra, buffalo, and impala grazing while raptors circle overhead. Break for a picnic lunch in the wild, savoring the sights and sounds of nature, before continuing your exploration. Return in the evening for a relaxed dinner, reminiscing about the day’s encounters.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 – Tsavo West to Aberdare National Park
activities: This morning, you travel north to the lush forests of Aberdare National Park. Unlike the open savannahs, Aberdare is a world of dense bamboo forests, misty peaks, and cascading waterfalls. Upon arrival, check into your unique tree lodge, strategically located near a watering hole where elephants, buffalo, and even leopards come to drink. Spend the afternoon on the viewing deck, watching as animals emerge from the forest, their reflections shimmering in the water. Night brings a new kind of magic here — floodlights illuminate the clearing, revealing nocturnal visitors that step silently from the shadows.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Full Day in Aberdare National Park
activities: Wake to the calls of forest birds and head out on a scenic drive through Aberdare’s winding trails. The cool air carries the scent of wet earth and flowers. Spot rare species such as the bongo antelope and Colobus monkeys swinging through the treetops. Stop at Karuru Falls, where water tumbles dramatically down the cliffs. Lunch is enjoyed back at the lodge, followed by a peaceful afternoon watching wildlife from the comfort of your room or deck. As night falls, listen for the sounds of the forest — the deep roar of a distant lion or the splash of an elephant in the watering hole.

itinerary.day: DAY 8 – Aberdare to Samburu National Reserve | Afternoon Safari
activities: Today, the landscapes shift dramatically as you head to Samburu National Reserve in Kenya’s arid north. Upon arrival and lunch at your lodge, embark on a game drive in search of the “Samburu Special Five” — Grevy’s zebra, Somali ostrich, reticulated giraffe, Beisa oryx, and gerenuk. The Ewaso Nyiro River winds through this dry land, attracting elephants, crocodiles, and countless birds. The warm hues of sunset give the reserve a golden glow as you head back to camp for dinner.

itinerary.day: DAY 9 – Full Day in Samburu National Reserve
activities: Spend the entire day exploring Samburu’s unique habitats. Morning brings sightings of elephants cooling off in the river and lions patrolling the plains. Your guide shares fascinating insights about the reserve’s wildlife and Samburu people. After a picnic lunch in the bush, continue your game drive, perhaps spotting leopards slinking through the acacias or gerenuks standing tall to nibble leaves. Evening is for relaxation and star gazing, as the African sky unfolds above you.

itinerary.day: DAY 10 – Samburu to Lake Nakuru National Park
activities: Your journey takes you to Lake Nakuru, a shimmering lake famous for its flamingos and rhinos. After lunch, set out for an afternoon game drive to see both black and white rhinos grazing on the open grasslands, alongside buffaloes, warthogs, and giraffes. The lake itself is a photographer’s dream, with flocks of pelicans and, in the right season, pink-hued flamingos lining its shores. Return to your lodge for a calm evening overlooking the water.

itinerary.day: DAY 11 – Lake Nakuru to Lake Naivasha | Boat Ride
activities: After breakfast, a short drive takes you to Lake Naivasha, a peaceful freshwater lake surrounded by papyrus reeds. Check into your lodge and enjoy lunch before heading out on a boat safari. Glide across calm waters, spotting hippos lazing in the shallows and fish eagles swooping for their catch. Return in time for a lakeside sunset, the air filled with bird calls.

itinerary.day: DAY 12 – Lake Naivasha to Maasai Mara | Afternoon Safari
activities: Today you journey to the crown jewel of Kenya’s parks — Maasai Mara National Reserve. After lunch at your lodge, venture out for an afternoon safari across the sweeping plains. Spot prides of lions, herds of elephants, and the endless movement of zebras and wildebeests. The landscape stretches out under a sky that feels impossibly wide, painted in fiery reds and oranges as the day ends.

itinerary.day: DAY 13 – Full Day in Maasai Mara
activities: This is a day of pure adventure — a full-day safari in the Maasai Mara. Morning light reveals predators on the move and antelopes grazing peacefully. You might spot cheetahs perched on termite mounds, scanning for prey. Break for a picnic lunch by the Mara River, where crocodiles bask and hippos jostle in the water. In the afternoon, your safari continues through different terrains, each revealing new wildlife surprises. Dinner is a lively affair, with stories shared under a canopy of stars.

itinerary.day: DAY 14 – Full Day in Maasai Mara
activities: Another day in the Mara means another chance for extraordinary encounters. Perhaps you’ll follow a leopard’s tracks or witness the drama of a predator-prey chase. A visit to a Maasai village introduces you to their colorful beadwork, traditional dances, and way of life, deeply connected to the land. Evening falls with the calls of night creatures filling the air, a reminder that the wild never sleeps.

itinerary.day: DAY 15 – Morning Safari in Maasai Mara | Departure from Nairobi
activities: Your final safari begins at dawn, the sky glowing softly as the plains wake up. Capture those last magical photos — an elephant family crossing the path, a lone giraffe silhouetted against the sunrise. After breakfast, it’s time to bid farewell to the Mara and drive back to Nairobi for your onward flight, carrying with you a heart full of African memories.

know_before_you_go: Visa Requirements: Most travelers need a tourist visa; check Egypt’s official requirements for your nationality. E-visas are available for many countries.
Best Time to Visit: October to April offers pleasant weather, perfect for sightseeing and Nile cruising.
Currency: Egyptian Pound (EGP); carry small denominations for tips and street shopping.
Language: Arabic is the official language; English is widely understood in tourist areas.
Tipping Culture: Known as “baksheesh” in Egypt, tipping is customary for guides, drivers, and hotel staff.
Dress Code: Modest attire is advised, especially in religious and rural areas; light, breathable fabrics are best.
Water Safety: Drink only bottled or filtered water; avoid ice in drinks unless in reputed hotels.
Health Precautions: No mandatory vaccinations, but Hepatitis A, Typhoid, and routine shots are recommended.
Electricity: 220V supply; European two-round-pin plug is common—carry an adapter.
Photography: Always ask permission before photographing locals; some sites require separate photography tickets.
Internet & SIM Cards: Local SIM cards are cheap; Vodafone Egypt and Orange have good coverage.
Transportation Between Cities: Domestic flights save time; train journeys are slower but scenic.
Security Checks: Expect bag scans at hotels, museums, and temples—security is tight.
Local Time: Egypt Standard Time (GMT+2), no daylight savings.
Alcohol Availability: Alcohol is available in licensed hotels, bars, and duty-free shops but not widely in public spaces.
Shopping Tips: Bargaining is part of the culture; start at half the asking price in markets.
Climate Readiness: The desert climate means hot days and cool nights—pack accordingly.
Cultural Etiquette: Greet with “As-salamu alaykum” and a smile; avoid public displays of affection.
Safety in Crowds: Keep valuables in a money belt, especially in busy tourist zones.
Tourist Police: Present in all major attractions; they are approachable for assistance.

dos: Respect Ancient Sites: Do not climb on monuments or touch carvings unnecessarily.
Use Local Guides: They enhance the experience with history and cultural context.
Stay Hydrated: Carry a reusable bottle and refill at safe water sources.
Learn a Few Arabic Words: Even simple phrases like “Shukran” (Thank you) are appreciated.
Cover Shoulders & Knees: Especially in mosques, temples, and rural areas.
Use Sunscreen Generously: The sun can be harsh even in cooler months.
Carry Small Change: For tipping, public restrooms, and street snacks.
Pre-Book Key Activities: Abu Simbel visits, Nile Cruises, and hot-air balloon rides sell out fast.
Follow Cruise Timings: Nile cruises have fixed schedules for temple visits.
Try Local Cuisine: Sample koshari, falafel, and Egyptian bread.
Ask Before Entering Homes or Shops: Politeness goes a long way in small towns.
Follow Photography Rules: Some artifacts and tombs prohibit flash or cameras entirely.
Take Desert Tours with Registered Operators: For safety and proper equipment.
Keep Copies of Documents: Store passport and visa scans separately.
Respect Prayer Times: Avoid loud behavior near mosques during calls to prayer.
Support Local Artisans: Buy handmade souvenirs instead of mass-produced ones.
Stay Alert in Bazaars: Crowds can be overwhelming—keep an eye on your belongings.
Use Hotel Safes: Store valuables when heading out.
Follow Lifeguard Instructions: When swimming in the Red Sea or hotel pools.
Tip in Local Currency: It’s more appreciated and useful for recipients.
donts: Don’t Drink Tap Water: Even locals often avoid it.
Don’t Wear Revealing Clothes: Especially in conservative areas.
Don’t Touch Antiquities: Oils from your skin can damage ancient surfaces.
Don’t Photograph Military Areas: Includes bridges, airports, and checkpoints.
Don’t Engage in Heated Political Discussions: Sensitive topics should be avoided.
Don’t Show Affection in Public: Kissing or hugging in public can be frowned upon.
Don’t Trust Unofficial Tour Guides: Only hire licensed professionals.
Don’t Forget to Validate Tickets: At museum and temple entrances.
Don’t Overpay Without Bargaining: Prices are often inflated for tourists.
Don’t Feed Street Animals: It can cause disturbances in public spaces.
Don’t Leave Bags Unattended: Petty theft is possible in crowded areas.
Don’t Assume All Taxis Use Meters: Negotiate fares beforehand.
Don’t Enter Mosques During Friday Prayers: Unless you’re a practicing Muslim.
Don’t Swim Outside Designated Areas: Strong currents and coral reefs can be dangerous.
Don’t Rely on Credit Cards Everywhere: Cash is king in local markets.
Don’t Eat Uncooked Street Food: Stick to reputable vendors.
Don’t Skip Travel Insurance: Medical care for foreigners can be costly.
Don’t Walk Alone in Unfamiliar Areas at Night: Use trusted transport instead.
Don’t Accept Drinks from Strangers: Safety first.
Don’t Ignore Cultural Norms: Even unintentional disrespect can offend locals.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Cairo | Evening at Leisure
activities: Welcome to the land of the Pharaohs! Upon arrival at Cairo International Airport, you’ll be greeted by our representative and transferred to your hotel. After check-in, relax and take in the sights and sounds of Egypt’s capital. In the evening, you may choose to stroll through the nearby streets or enjoy a cup of Egyptian mint tea as the city buzzes around you. Rest well for the adventures ahead.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Cairo – Pyramids of Giza & Egyptian Museum
activities: After breakfast, set out to witness the grandeur of the Pyramids of Giza, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Marvel at the colossal Great Sphinx guarding the pyramids. Continue to the Egyptian Museum, home to thousands of ancient artifacts including treasures from King Tutankhamun’s tomb. The evening is free for leisure or an optional sound and light show at the Pyramids.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Full-Day Alexandria Excursion
activities: Today, take a scenic drive to Alexandria, Egypt’s coastal gem. Visit the Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, the Pompey’s Pillar, and the grand Bibliotheca Alexandrina. Enjoy the Mediterranean views and savor fresh seafood by the shore. Return to Cairo in the evening.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Cairo – Khan El Khalili Bazaar & Nile Dinner Cruise
activities: Begin your day with a visit to Khan El Khalili Bazaar, a bustling market filled with spices, souvenirs, jewelry, and traditional handicrafts. Bargain like a local and soak in the vibrant atmosphere. In the evening, enjoy a Nile River dinner cruise complete with live music, traditional Tanoura dance, and breathtaking city views from the deck.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Departure from Cairo
activities: After breakfast, it’s time to say goodbye to Egypt. Depending on your flight time, you may squeeze in some last-minute shopping or sightseeing before being transferred to Cairo International Airport for your onward journey.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Cairo | Evening at Leisure
activities: Step into the timeless land of the Pharaohs! Upon landing at Cairo International Airport, you will be met by our representative and transferred to your hotel. After check-in, relax and enjoy your first glimpse of the city. If you arrive early, explore the streets around your hotel or try a traditional Egyptian mint tea at a local café. The evening is yours to unwind and prepare for your first big adventure tomorrow.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Cairo – Pyramids of Giza, Sphinx & Egyptian Museum
activities: Today is a journey back in time. Begin with a visit to the Pyramids of Giza, marvel at the Great Pyramid, and gaze at the Sphinx guarding the desert sands. Continue to the Egyptian Museum, housing the world’s largest collection of ancient Egyptian artifacts, including the golden treasures of King Tutankhamun. Later, explore the bustling streets or opt for the evening Sound & Light Show at the Pyramids.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Full-Day Alexandria Excursion
activities: Head north to Alexandria, Egypt’s second-largest city and a coastal treasure. Visit the mysterious Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, stand in awe of Pompey’s Pillar, and admire the modern Bibliotheca Alexandrina. Stroll along the Corniche with its Mediterranean breeze and enjoy a delicious seafood lunch by the harbor before returning to Cairo in the evening.

itinerary.day: Day 4 :Fly to Aswan | Philae Temple & Nile Cruise Embarkation
activities: After breakfast, take a short flight to Aswan, a serene city along the Nile. Visit the beautiful Philae Temple, dedicated to the goddess Isis, and admire the High Dam, one of Egypt’s engineering marvels. In the afternoon, board your luxurious Nile Cruise, your floating hotel for the next three nights. Enjoy dinner on board as the Nile’s tranquil waters drift by.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Nile Cruise – Kom Ombo & Edfu Temples
activities: Wake up to the gentle sounds of the Nile. Your first stop is Kom Ombo Temple, a unique double temple dedicated to Sobek (the crocodile god) and Horus (the falcon god). Continue cruising to Edfu Temple, one of the best-preserved temples in Egypt, dedicated to Horus. Watch life along the riverbanks as your cruise sails toward Luxor.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Nile Cruise – Luxor’s East & West Bank Treasures
activities: Start the day with the Valley of the Kings, where pharaohs were laid to rest in richly decorated tombs. Visit the Temple of Queen Hatshepsut and the Colossi of Memnon on the West Bank. In the afternoon, explore Luxor’s East Bank, including the magnificent Karnak Temple Complex and Luxor Temple. In the evening, enjoy your final night on board with a farewell dinner.

itinerary.day: Day 7: Disembark Nile Cruise | Fly Back to Cairo & Departure
activities: After breakfast, disembark from the cruise and take a short flight back to Cairo. Depending on your flight schedule, enjoy last-minute shopping or a quick stroll through Khan El Khalili Bazaar before your transfer to Cairo International Airport for your onward journey.

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa to visit Egypt?
faqs.answer: Yes, Indian citizens need a visa, available online or on arrival at the airport.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Egypt?
faqs.answer: October to April, when the weather is cooler.

faqs.question: How many days should I spend in Egypt?
faqs.answer: 7 to 10 days to cover Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, and Nile cruise.

faqs.question: Is Egypt safe for Indian travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, Egypt is generally safe; stick to tourist areas and travel in groups if possible.

faqs.question: What currency should I carry?
faqs.answer: Egyptian Pound (EGP). USD and Euros are also accepted.

faqs.question: Can I use credit/debit cards in Egypt?
faqs.answer: Yes, but cash is preferred in markets and smaller shops.

faqs.question: Is tipping expected?
faqs.answer: Yes, tipping is customary in Egypt, typically 5-10%.

faqs.question: Are vegetarian food options available?
faqs.answer: Yes, Egyptian cuisine includes many vegetarian dishes.

faqs.question: Is English widely spoken?
faqs.answer: English is common in hotels, restaurants, and tourist spots.

faqs.question: Can I drink tap water?
faqs.answer: No, always drink bottled water.

faqs.question: Are domestic flights included?
faqs.answer: Domestic flights between Cairo, Luxor, and Aswan are often included.

faqs.question: Is the Nile cruise safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, Nile cruises are safe and popular among tourists.

faqs.question: What clothes should I pack?
faqs.answer: Light, breathable fabrics and modest clothing.

faqs.question: Can I use mobile internet easily?
faqs.answer: Yes, local SIM cards are cheap and available at the airport.

faqs.question: Are there any restrictions for tourists?
faqs.answer: Avoid photographing military sites and respect local laws.

faqs.question: Is Egypt suitable for solo female travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, with normal precautions.

faqs.question: Can I visit the pyramids at night?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are light shows in the evening at Giza.

faqs.question: Are there shopping opportunities?
faqs.answer: Yes, famous bazaars like Khan El Khalili offer souvenirs and handicrafts.

faqs.question: Is bargaining common?
faqs.answer: Yes, bargaining is expected in markets.

faqs.question: How early should I book my Egypt trip?
faqs.answer: Book 4–6 weeks in advance to get best prices and visa processing.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Cairo | Evening at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Egypt — the cradle of civilization! Upon arrival at Cairo International Airport, you’ll be greeted and escorted to your hotel. Spend your evening relaxing or exploring the vibrant streets nearby. Perhaps try a cup of traditional hibiscus tea as the city lights twinkle, giving you your first taste of Egypt’s charm.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Cairo – Pyramids of Giza, Sphinx & Egyptian Museum
activities: Begin your Egyptian adventure with a full-day tour of Cairo’s iconic treasures. Marvel at the Pyramids of Giza, a testament to human ingenuity, and stand before the mystical Sphinx. Later, visit the Egyptian Museum, home to over 120,000 ancient artifacts including King Tutankhamun’s golden mask. The evening is free for you to enjoy the city or take in the Sound & Light Show at the pyramids.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Full-Day Alexandria Excursion
activities: Travel north to Alexandria, a Mediterranean jewel founded by Alexander the Great. Explore the Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, one of the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages, admire Pompey’s Pillar, and visit the spectacular Bibliotheca Alexandrina. Stroll along the Corniche, enjoy sea views, and savor fresh seafood before returning to Cairo in the evening.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Fly to Aswan | Abu Simbel Excursion | Nile Cruise Embarkation
activities: Early morning flight to Aswan followed by a breathtaking drive to Abu Simbel, the colossal rock temples of Ramses II. Return to Aswan and board your luxurious Nile Cruise. Visit the serene Philae Temple, dedicated to goddess Isis, and enjoy the views from the High Dam before settling into your floating hotel for dinner and an evening sail.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Nile Cruise – Kom Ombo & Edfu Temples
activities: Sail to Kom Ombo Temple, a unique double temple honoring Sobek and Horus. Continue to Edfu Temple, dedicated to Horus and one of Egypt’s most preserved monuments. Witness rural Nile life as your cruise glides towards Luxor, passing picturesque riverbanks and small villages.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Luxor West Bank – Valley of the Kings & Hatshepsut’s Temple
activities: Step into ancient royal history at the Valley of the Kings, exploring tombs with vivid hieroglyphics. Visit the stunning Temple of Queen Hatshepsut and the towering Colossi of Memnon. In the evening, you may choose to explore Luxor’s markets or relax on board your cruise.

itinerary.day: Day 7: Luxor East Bank – Karnak & Luxor Temples | Fly to Cairo
activities: Discover the grandeur of the Karnak Temple Complex, the largest religious structure ever built, and the elegant Luxor Temple, connected by the Avenue of Sphinxes. Disembark from your cruise and take a short flight back to Cairo. Spend your last evening shopping at Khan El Khalili Bazaar or enjoying a farewell Egyptian feast.

itinerary.day: Day 8: Departure from Cairo
activities: After breakfast, it’s time to say goodbye to Egypt. Depending on your flight schedule, enjoy a last stroll through Cairo before your transfer to the airport for your onward journey.

know_before_you_go: Visa Requirements: Most travelers need a tourist visa; check Egypt’s official requirements for your nationality. E-visas are available for many countries.
Best Time to Visit: October to April offers pleasant weather, perfect for sightseeing and Nile cruising.
Currency: Egyptian Pound (EGP); carry small denominations for tips and street shopping.
Language: Arabic is the official language; English is widely understood in tourist areas.
Tipping Culture: Known as “baksheesh” in Egypt, tipping is customary for guides, drivers, and hotel staff.
Dress Code: Modest attire is advised, especially in religious and rural areas; light, breathable fabrics are best.
Water Safety: Drink only bottled or filtered water; avoid ice in drinks unless in reputed hotels.
Health Precautions: No mandatory vaccinations, but Hepatitis A, Typhoid, and routine shots are recommended.
Electricity: 220V supply; European two-round-pin plug is common—carry an adapter.
Photography: Always ask permission before photographing locals; some sites require separate photography tickets.
Internet & SIM Cards: Local SIM cards are cheap; Vodafone Egypt and Orange have good coverage.
Transportation Between Cities: Domestic flights save time; train journeys are slower but scenic.
Security Checks: Expect bag scans at hotels, museums, and temples—security is tight.
Local Time: Egypt Standard Time (GMT+2), no daylight savings.
Alcohol Availability: Alcohol is available in licensed hotels, bars, and duty-free shops but not widely in public spaces.
Shopping Tips: Bargaining is part of the culture; start at half the asking price in markets.
Climate Readiness: The desert climate means hot days and cool nights—pack accordingly.
Cultural Etiquette: Greet with “As-salamu alaykum” and a smile; avoid public displays of affection.
Safety in Crowds: Keep valuables in a money belt, especially in busy tourist zones.
Tourist Police: Present in all major attractions; they are approachable for assistance.

dos: Respect Ancient Sites: Do not climb on monuments or touch carvings unnecessarily.

Stay Hydrated: Carry a reusable bottle and refill at safe water sources.

Use Sunscreen Generously: The sun can be harsh even in cooler months.
Carry Small Change: For tipping, public restrooms, and street snacks.
Pre-Book Key Activities: Abu Simbel visits, Nile Cruises, and hot-air balloon rides sell out fast.
Follow Cruise Timings: Nile cruises have fixed schedules for temple visits.
Try Local Cuisine: Sample koshari, falafel, and Egyptian bread.
Ask Before Entering Homes or Shops: Politeness goes a long way in small towns.
Follow Photography Rules: Some artifacts and tombs prohibit flash or cameras entirely.
Take Desert Tours with Registered Operators: For safety and proper equipment.
Keep Copies of Documents: Store passport and visa scans separately.
Respect Prayer Times: Avoid loud behavior near mosques during calls to prayer.

Stay Alert in Bazaars: Crowds can be overwhelming—keep an eye on your belongings.
Use Hotel Safes: Store valuables when heading out.
Follow Lifeguard Instructions: When swimming in the Red Sea or hotel pools.
Tip in Local Currency: It’s more appreciated and useful for recipients.
donts: Don’t Drink Tap Water: Even locals often avoid it.
Don’t Wear Revealing Clothes: Especially in conservative areas.
Don’t Touch Antiquities: Oils from your skin can damage ancient surfaces.
Don’t Photograph Military Areas: Includes bridges, airports, and checkpoints.
Don’t Engage in Heated Political Discussions: Sensitive topics should be avoided.
Don’t Show Affection in Public: Kissing or hugging in public can be frowned upon.
Don’t Trust Unofficial Tour Guides: Only hire licensed professionals.
Don’t Forget to Validate Tickets: At museum and temple entrances.
Don’t Overpay Without Bargaining: Prices are often inflated for tourists.
Don’t Feed Street Animals: It can cause disturbances in public spaces.
Don’t Leave Bags Unattended: Petty theft is possible in crowded areas.
Don’t Assume All Taxis Use Meters: Negotiate fares beforehand.
Don’t Enter Mosques During Friday Prayers: Unless you’re a practicing Muslim.
Don’t Swim Outside Designated Areas: Strong currents and coral reefs can be dangerous.
Don’t Rely on Credit Cards Everywhere: Cash is king in local markets.
Don’t Eat Uncooked Street Food: Stick to reputable vendors.
Don’t Skip Travel Insurance: Medical care for foreigners can be costly.
Don’t Walk Alone in Unfamiliar Areas at Night: Use trusted transport instead.
Don’t Accept Drinks from Strangers: Safety first.
Don’t Ignore Cultural Norms: Even unintentional disrespect can offend locals.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Cairo | Welcome to the Land of Pharaohs
activities: Touch down at Cairo International Airport, where your representative will greet you and assist with formalities. Transfer to your hotel, unwind, and take in your first glimpses of Egypt’s lively capital. In the evening, you may choose to enjoy a quiet dinner or stroll through Cairo’s bustling streets lit by golden lamps.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Cairo – Pyramids of Giza, Sphinx & Egyptian Museum
activities: Begin your exploration with the Great Pyramids of Giza and the mysterious Sphinx, a UNESCO World Heritage site that has inspired wonder for millennia. Head to the Egyptian Museum, where treasures like Tutankhamun’s golden mask await. Wrap up your day at leisure or with an optional Nile dinner cruise featuring live music and whirling Tanoura dancers.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Full-Day Alexandria Tour
activities: Journey to Alexandria, the Mediterranean pearl. Explore the Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, admire Pompey’s Pillar, and see the reconstructed Bibliotheca Alexandrina, an architectural masterpiece. Enjoy a seafood lunch by the Corniche before returning to Cairo in the evening.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Fly to Aswan | Abu Simbel & Nile Cruise Embarkation
activities: Board a morning flight to Aswan, then head to the world-famous Abu Simbel Temples, colossal monuments honoring Ramses II and Queen Nefertari. Return to Aswan to board your Nile Cruise. Visit the Philae Temple, a beautiful island sanctuary to the goddess Isis, and take in the view from the High Dam before enjoying a welcome dinner on board.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Kom Ombo & Edfu Temples
activities: Sail north to Kom Ombo Temple, uniquely dedicated to two gods—Sobek the crocodile god and Horus the falcon-headed god. Continue to Edfu Temple, one of the best-preserved temples in Egypt, where you’ll walk through towering sandstone structures adorned with hieroglyphs. Your cruise then continues toward Luxor.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Luxor West Bank – Valley of the Kings & Hatshepsut’s Temple
activities: Walk through history in the Valley of the Kings, where pharaohs were buried with unimaginable treasures. Visit the Temple of Queen Hatshepsut, a stunning mortuary complex, and the Colossi of Memnon, two massive statues that have stood for over 3,000 years.

itinerary.day: Day 7: Luxor East Bank – Karnak & Luxor Temples | Transfer to Hurghada
activities: Discover the grandeur of Karnak Temple, with its forest of giant columns, and the stunning Luxor Temple linked by the Avenue of Sphinxes. After disembarkation, travel to Hurghada on the Red Sea coast for a change of pace and scenery. Check in to your beachfront resort and enjoy the evening at leisure.

itinerary.day: Day 8: Hurghada – Red Sea Leisure
activities: Today is all about relaxation and adventure. Swim in turquoise waters, lounge on sandy beaches, or opt for thrilling water activities like snorkeling, diving, or a glass-bottom boat ride to explore vibrant coral reefs. In the evening, enjoy a sunset stroll by the marina.

itinerary.day: Day 9: Hurghada – Free Day or Optional Desert Safari
activities: Enjoy your final full day in Hurghada. You can relax by the pool or take an optional desert safari with quad biking and camel rides, capped off with a Bedouin-style dinner under the stars.

itinerary.day: Day 10: Fly to Cairo | Departure
activities: After breakfast, transfer to Hurghada Airport for a short flight to Cairo and connect to your onward flight home. Leave Egypt with a heart full of memories—pyramids, temples, the Nile, and the warm Egyptian sun.

know_before_you_go: Dubai is a part of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and follows Islamic cultural values — dress modestly in public areas.
The official currency is the UAE Dirham (AED). Credit and debit cards are widely accepted.
Dubai is GST (5%) applicable on purchases; tax refunds are available for tourists on eligible shopping.
Tap water is generally safe, but bottled water is recommended for visitors.
The best time to visit is November to March when the weather is cooler.
Summer (June–September) can be extremely hot, with temperatures above 40°C — plan outdoor tours early morning or late evening.
Friday is the weekly holiday, so some attractions and shops may open later in the day.
Public display of affection is prohibited; hand-holding is generally fine for married couples.
Alcohol is served only in licensed restaurants, hotels, and bars; drinking in public is illegal.
Always carry your ID or a copy of your passport when going out.
Taxis are metered, and ride-hailing apps like Careem & Uber are widely used.
Public transport includes metro, buses, and water taxis — all require a Nol card.
Photography of government buildings, military sites, and locals without consent is prohibited.
During Ramadan, eating, drinking, or smoking in public during daylight is not allowed.
Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated (5–10% in restaurants).
Some attractions have strict dress codes (e.g., Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque requires modest clothing).
Carry sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat for daytime sightseeing.
Dubai’s malls often have extended hours until late night.
ATMs are easily available across the city.
Bargaining is acceptable in traditional souks, but fixed prices apply in malls.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Dubai | Evening at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Dubai — the land of luxury, innovation, and Arabian charm! Upon arrival at Dubai International Airport, meet your representative and transfer to your hotel. After check-in, you can rest or explore the nearby attractions on your own. Enjoy a relaxing evening walk at Jumeirah Beach or visit Dubai Marina for a delightful dinner with waterfront views. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Half-Day Dubai City Tour | Desert Safari with BBQ Dinner
activities: After breakfast, embark on a city tour covering Dubai Museum, Jumeirah Mosque, photo stop at Burj Al Arab, Atlantis The Palm, and drive past the modern skyscrapers along Sheikh Zayed Road. Explore the traditional Gold and Spice Souks. In the afternoon, get ready for an adventurous Desert Safari with dune bashing, camel riding, sandboarding, and henna painting. End the evening with a BBQ dinner and live Tanoura & Belly Dance performances. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Abu Dhabi City Tour | Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
activities: Post breakfast, drive to Abu Dhabi for a full-day city tour. Visit the grand Sheikh Zayed Mosque, Heritage Village, Corniche, and Marina Mall. Enjoy a photo stop at Emirates Palace and see Qasr Al Watan from outside. Return to Dubai in the evening and spend leisure time exploring nearby markets or dining in style. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Miracle Garden | Global Village | Dhow Cruise Dinner
activities: After breakfast, visit the world-famous Dubai Miracle Garden — a floral paradise with over 150 million flowers arranged in unique displays. Continue to Global Village, a multicultural theme park with pavilions from around the world offering food, shopping, and live performances. In the evening, head for a relaxing Dhow Cruise along Dubai Creek or Marina, with a buffet dinner and live entertainment. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Dubai Frame | Burj Khalifa & Dubai Mall
activities: After breakfast, visit the iconic Dubai Frame for breathtaking panoramic views of old and new Dubai. Later, spend your afternoon at Dubai Mall — shop from world-class brands, visit the Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo, and watch the mesmerizing Dubai Fountain show. End your day with a visit to Burj Khalifa’s observation deck for a spectacular sunset view. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Departure from Dubai
activities: Enjoy your breakfast at the hotel. Depending on your flight schedule, you may indulge in some last-minute shopping or sightseeing. Later, check out and transfer to Dubai International Airport with beautiful memories of your Dubai getaway.

packages.fagHeading: Top FAQs for Dubai Tour Package

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa for Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tourist visas are required and we assist in getting them.

faqs.question: Is Dubai safe for solo travelers and families?
faqs.answer: Yes, it’s one of the safest cities in the world.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Dubai?
faqs.answer: November to March offers pleasant weather.

faqs.question: Is Burj Khalifa entry included?
faqs.answer: Standard packages include non-prime tickets. Custom upgrades available.

faqs.question: What’s the currency in Dubai?
faqs.answer: AED – Arab Emirates Dirham.

faqs.question: Can I drink alcohol in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Only in licensed restaurants, bars & hotels. Public drinking is illegal.

faqs.question: Is vegetarian food available?
faqs.answer: Yes, Indian and vegetarian meals are easily available.

faqs.question: Can I customize my Dubai itinerary?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. All packages on TripDekhoo.com are customizable.

faqs.question: Is Desert Safari safe for children and elderly?
faqs.answer: It’s safe, but dune bashing may not be suitable for all. Choose soft safari options.

faqs.question: Are theme park tickets included in the package?
faqs.answer: No, but we can add them on request (IMG, Ferrari World, etc.).

faqs.question: Do hotels charge additional fees?
faqs.answer: Yes, Tourism Dirham (5-20 AED per night) is payable directly.

faqs.question: What language is spoken in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Arabic is official; English is widely spoken.

faqs.question: What kind of clothes should I wear in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Modest and respectful clothing. Swimwear only at beaches/pools.

faqs.question: Are credit/debit cards accepted?
faqs.answer: Yes, widely accepted. Carry some cash for small vendors.

faqs.question: Can I travel from Dubai to Abu Dhabi in this package?
faqs.answer: It can be added as an optional day trip.

faqs.question: What are the COVID-19 requirements?
faqs.answer: Currently, no restrictions. Check updates before travel.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get a Dubai visa?
faqs.answer: 3–5 working days with all documents in order.

faqs.question: What’s the legal drinking age in Dubai?
faqs.answer: 21 years and above.

faqs.question: Is tipping compulsory in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not compulsory but customary in the hospitality industry.

faqs.question: Can I use WhatsApp calling in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, most VoIP calls are blocked. Use Zoom or Skype with VPN if needed.

know_before_you_go: Dubai is a part of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and follows Islamic cultural values — dress modestly in public areas.
The official currency is the UAE Dirham (AED). Credit and debit cards are widely accepted.
Dubai is GST (5%) applicable on purchases; tax refunds are available for tourists on eligible shopping.
Tap water is generally safe, but bottled water is recommended for visitors.
The best time to visit is November to March when the weather is cooler.
Summer (June–September) can be extremely hot, with temperatures above 40°C — plan outdoor tours early morning or late evening.
Friday is the weekly holiday, so some attractions and shops may open later in the day.
Public display of affection is prohibited; hand-holding is generally fine for married couples.
Alcohol is served only in licensed restaurants, hotels, and bars; drinking in public is illegal.
Always carry your ID or a copy of your passport when going out.
Taxis are metered, and ride-hailing apps like Careem & Uber are widely used.
Public transport includes metro, buses, and water taxis — all require a Nol card.
Photography of government buildings, military sites, and locals without consent is prohibited.
During Ramadan, eating, drinking, or smoking in public during daylight is not allowed.
Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated (5–10% in restaurants).
Some attractions have strict dress codes (e.g., Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque requires modest clothing).
Carry sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat for daytime sightseeing.
Dubai’s malls often have extended hours until late night.
ATMs are easily available across the city.
Bargaining is acceptable in traditional souks, but fixed prices apply in malls.

dos: Respect local culture, traditions, and laws at all times.
Dress modestly in public areas — cover shoulders and knees.
Use licensed taxis or official ride-hailing apps for travel.
Carry small change for local markets and taxis.
Visit major attractions like Burj Khalifa, Dubai Frame, and Dubai Fountain.
Take a desert safari for a traditional Arabian experience.
Try local Emirati cuisine along with international dining options.
Stay hydrated, especially in summer.
Shop at both luxury malls and traditional souks.
Take advantage of the metro for affordable city travel.
Ask permission before taking photos of people.
Respect prayer times in mosques.
Keep your accommodation’s address and contact details handy.
Explore cultural sites like Al Fahidi Historical District.
Carry a shawl or light jacket for cooler evenings in winter.
Follow safety instructions at theme parks and water activities.
Try dhow cruises for a scenic evening experience.
Enjoy Global Village and Miracle Garden during seasonal openings.
Be polite and patient in queues and public transport.
Use official currency exchange counters for better rates.
donts: Do not engage in public displays of affection beyond hand-holding.
Avoid wearing revealing or see-through clothing in public.
Do not consume alcohol in public places or outside licensed venues.
Avoid using offensive gestures or language.
Do not photograph government buildings, military areas, or locals without consent.
Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking in public during Ramadan daylight hours.
Do not carry drugs — penalties are extremely severe.
Avoid littering; fines apply.
Do not use or possess e-cigarettes/vapes where prohibited.
Avoid loud behavior or arguments in public.
Do not cross streets outside designated pedestrian crossings.
Avoid making hand gestures considered rude in local culture.
Do not bring pork products into the country.
Avoid political discussions or criticism of the UAE government.
Do not stay in the same hotel room with an unrelated opposite-sex companion unless married.
Avoid gambling — it’s illegal in the UAE.
Do not feed wild animals or birds in public areas.
Avoid excessive bargaining in malls where prices are fixed.
Do not chew gum loudly in formal settings.
Avoid leaving valuables unattended in public places.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Dubai | Evening at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Dubai! Upon arrival at Dubai International Airport, meet your driver and transfer to your hotel. After check-in, you can relax or step out for a gentle evening walk along Jumeirah Beach, enjoy dinner at a nearby restaurant, or simply admire the illuminated city skyline. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Half-Day Dubai City Tour | Desert Safari with BBQ Dinner
activities: After breakfast, explore the city’s iconic highlights — Dubai Museum, Jumeirah Mosque, Burj Al Arab (photo stop), Atlantis The Palm, and Sheikh Zayed Road. Visit the bustling Gold & Spice Souks. In the afternoon, head for an exhilarating Desert Safari with dune bashing, camel rides, henna painting, and a BBQ dinner with live entertainment. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Abu Dhabi City Tour | Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
activities: Enjoy breakfast before heading to Abu Dhabi. Visit the majestic Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, drive along the Corniche, explore Heritage Village, and capture photos at Emirates Palace & Qasr Al Watan (outside). Return to Dubai in the evening for leisure time. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Miracle Garden | Global Village
activities: After breakfast, step into a world of vibrant blooms at Dubai Miracle Garden. Later, visit Global Village — an international extravaganza of culture, shopping, and entertainment. Return to the hotel and relax for the night. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Dubai Frame | Burj Khalifa & Dubai Mall
activities: Start the day with a visit to the Dubai Frame for panoramic views of the city’s past and future. Head to Dubai Mall for luxury shopping, visit Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo, and in the evening enjoy the magical Dubai Fountain show. Cap the day with a visit to Burj Khalifa’s observation deck for breathtaking skyline views. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Atlantis the Palm | Aquaventure Waterpark & Lost Chambers Aquarium
activities: After breakfast, spend the day at Atlantis The Palm. Splash around at Aquaventure Waterpark with thrilling slides and a private beach, then explore the enchanting marine life at Lost Chambers Aquarium. Return to your hotel in the evening. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 7: Free Day for Shopping or Optional Tours
activities: Today is free for you to relax or indulge in optional activities — visit IMG Worlds of Adventure, Ski Dubai, or take a yacht cruise along Dubai Marina. You can also spend the day shopping at Dubai’s malls and souks for souvenirs and luxury items. Overnight stay in Dubai.

itinerary.day: Day 8: Departure from Dubai
activities: Enjoy breakfast, check out, and transfer to Dubai International Airport for your departure flight — carrying memories of golden deserts, glittering skylines, and unforgettable experiences.

packages.fagHeading: Top FAQs for Maldives Tour Package

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa for Maldives?
faqs.answer: No, visa on arrival is free for up to 90 days.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Maldives?
faqs.answer: November to April is the dry season – ideal for beach and water activities.

faqs.question: What’s the difference between speedboat, domestic flight, and seaplane transfers?
faqs.answer: It depends on the resort’s location – seaplanes are faster but costlier.

faqs.question: Are water villas safe for families with kids?
faqs.answer: Yes, but beach villas are often recommended for families with young children.

faqs.question: Can I choose an all-inclusive plan?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Many resorts offer all-inclusive packages with meals and drinks.

faqs.question: What is the Maldives currency?
faqs.answer: Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR), but USD is accepted at all resorts.

faqs.question: Is alcohol allowed in Maldives?
faqs.answer: Only in private resort islands, not in local inhabited islands.

faqs.question: Is Maldives good for solo travelers or only couples?
faqs.answer: It’s ideal for both. Some resorts also cater to families and solo travelers.

faqs.question: Are Indian meals available in the Maldives?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially at larger resorts and international chains.

faqs.question: Is Wi-Fi available in resorts?
faqs.answer: Yes, most resorts offer free or paid Wi-Fi.

faqs.question: What activities are included in the package?
faqs.answer: Non-motorized water sports and snorkeling are usually included. Others are optional.

faqs.question: Is it safe to swim in the sea?
faqs.answer: Yes, the lagoons are calm and monitored, but always follow resort safety guidelines.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for extra expenses?
faqs.answer: It depends – around USD 50–150 per day for drinks, excursions, or spa.

faqs.question: Can I book my own flights?
faqs.answer: Yes. Just share your arrival/departure timings for transfer coordination.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance necessary?
faqs.answer: Strongly recommended in case of flight delays or medical emergencies.

faqs.question: Can I visit Male city during my trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your resort is close to Male or during layover before/after check-in.

faqs.question: Are Maldives packages customizable?
faqs.answer: Yes! TripDekhoo offers fully personalized itineraries.

faqs.question: What’s the average travel time from airport to resort?
faqs.answer: 20–60 minutes by speedboat, 25–40 mins by seaplane or domestic flight + boat.

faqs.question: Are there honeymoon or anniversary specials?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many resorts offer free cake, wine, or upgrades for special occasions.

faqs.question: How early should I book my Maldives trip?
faqs.answer: At least 2–3 months in advance, especially for peak season (Dec–Feb).

know_before_you_go: Visa-on-arrival is available for most nationalities for 30 days; ensure your passport is valid for at least 6 months.
Seaplane transfers operate only between 6:00 AM and 4:00 PM, so late arrivals may require overnight stays in Malé.
The local currency is Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR), but USD is widely accepted in resorts.
Alcohol is prohibited on local islands but served freely at resorts.
When visiting inhabited islands, modest clothing is mandatory; swimwear is only for resorts and designated beaches.
Wi-Fi may be slow or intermittent due to remote island locations — download entertainment in advance.
Electric sockets are mostly UK-style (Type G); carry a universal adapter.
The Maldives has a tropical climate — sunny year-round with occasional showers; pack light, breathable clothing.
Bottled or filtered water is recommended for drinking.
Reef-safe sunscreen is essential to protect marine life and your skin.
Medical facilities are limited on remote islands; carry basic medicines and first-aid.
Marine life is protected — do not touch corals, fish, or turtles.
Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated; many resorts add a service charge.
Travel insurance is strongly recommended for medical emergencies and cancellations.
Drone use may require resort permission; always check rules before flying.
Most resorts offer cashless transactions — charges are billed to your room.
The Maldives is 1–5 hours ahead of GMT depending on the resort's island time (some use 'island time' to give longer daylight hours).
Local SIM cards are available at Malé airport for cheaper internet if needed.
Fresh seafood is abundant — try tuna, reef fish, and Maldivian curries.
Book excursions early to secure your preferred activities, as spots can be limited.

dos: Respect local culture — dress modestly when outside resort areas.
Book seaplane/speedboat transfers in advance to match your flight timings.
Try Maldivian cuisine such as mas huni (tuna & coconut breakfast).
Support eco-friendly resorts that practice sustainable tourism.
Snorkel or dive — the Maldives is a world-class underwater paradise.
Use biodegradable sunscreen to protect coral reefs.
Carry light, quick-dry clothing for tropical weather.
Hydrate often — the tropical sun can cause dehydration quickly.
Take part in cultural activities offered by resorts, like Boduberu drumming shows.
Pack a waterproof bag for boat trips and excursions.
donts: Don’t bring alcohol into the Maldives — it will be confiscated at the airport.
Don’t touch or step on corals — they are fragile and protected.
Don’t collect shells or sand — it’s illegal to take natural items from the Maldives.
Don’t engage in PDA (public display of affection) in local communities.
Don’t litter — always dispose of waste responsibly.
Don’t feed fish or marine animals — it disrupts the ecosystem.
Don’t expect nightlife like big cities — the Maldives is more about relaxation.
Don’t forget travel insurance — emergencies are costly on remote islands.
Don’t ignore safety instructions for water sports and excursions.
Don’t rely solely on resort Wi-Fi if you need strong internet — carry a local SIM.

itinerary.day: DAY 1: Arrival in the Maldives | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to the Maldives! Upon arrival at Malé International Airport, you will be greeted and transferred to your resort via speedboat or seaplane (depending on the package). As you check in, the warm ocean breeze and turquoise waters will set the tone for your holiday. Spend the day relaxing on the beach, sipping tropical cocktails, and soaking in panoramic views of the Indian Ocean. In the evening, enjoy a gentle stroll along the shoreline before indulging in a delicious dinner under the stars.

itinerary.day: DAY 2: Snorkeling & Water Adventures | Sunset Cruise
activities: Start your day with a hearty breakfast before heading out for an exciting snorkeling adventure. Swim alongside colorful coral reefs, tropical fish, and—if you’re lucky—majestic sea turtles. Return to the resort for lunch and some leisure time. Later in the afternoon, set sail on a romantic sunset cruise aboard a traditional Dhoni boat, where the sky transforms into a masterpiece of gold, orange, and pink hues. End the day with a beachfront BBQ or candlelight dinner.

itinerary.day: DAY 3: Island Hopping & Cultural Experience
activities: After breakfast, embark on an island-hopping excursion. Visit nearby inhabited and uninhabited islands, where you can experience local Maldivian culture, shop for handicrafts, and taste authentic Maldivian snacks. Relax on pristine sandbanks, swim in crystal-clear lagoons, and take unforgettable photos. Return to your resort for a rejuvenating spa session in the evening, followed by a peaceful night gazing at the star-lit sky.

itinerary.day: DAY 4: Departure from the Maldives
activities: Wake up to your last morning in paradise. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast with a view of the endless ocean before preparing for your departure. Depending on your flight time, take a final swim or walk on the beach. You’ll then be transferred back to Male International Airport, carrying with you memories of turquoise waters, white sands, and unmatched serenity.

packages.fagHeading: Top FAQs for Maldives Tour Package

faqs.question: Do Indians need a visa for Maldives?
faqs.answer: No, visa on arrival is free for up to 90 days.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Maldives?
faqs.answer: November to April is the dry season – ideal for beach and water activities.

faqs.question: What’s the difference between speedboat, domestic flight, and seaplane transfers?
faqs.answer: It depends on the resort’s location – seaplanes are faster but costlier.

faqs.question: Are water villas safe for families with kids?
faqs.answer: Yes, but beach villas are often recommended for families with young children.

faqs.question: Can I choose an all-inclusive plan?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Many resorts offer all-inclusive packages with meals and drinks.

faqs.question: What is the Maldives currency?
faqs.answer: Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR), but USD is accepted at all resorts.

faqs.question: Is alcohol allowed in Maldives?
faqs.answer: Only in private resort islands, not in local inhabited islands.

faqs.question: Is Maldives good for solo travelers or only couples?
faqs.answer: It’s ideal for both. Some resorts also cater to families and solo travelers.

faqs.question: Are Indian meals available in the Maldives?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially at larger resorts and international chains.

faqs.question: Is Wi-Fi available in resorts?
faqs.answer: Yes, most resorts offer free or paid Wi-Fi.

faqs.question: What activities are included in the package?
faqs.answer: Non-motorized water sports and snorkeling are usually included. Others are optional.

faqs.question: Is it safe to swim in the sea?
faqs.answer: Yes, the lagoons are calm and monitored, but always follow resort safety guidelines.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for extra expenses?
faqs.answer: It depends – around USD 50–150 per day for drinks, excursions, or spa.

faqs.question: Can I book my own flights?
faqs.answer: Yes. Just share your arrival/departure timings for transfer coordination.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance necessary?
faqs.answer: Strongly recommended in case of flight delays or medical emergencies.

faqs.question: Can I visit Male city during my trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your resort is close to Male or during layover before/after check-in.

faqs.question: Are Maldives packages customizable?
faqs.answer: Yes! TripDekhoo offers fully personalized itineraries.

faqs.question: What’s the average travel time from airport to resort?
faqs.answer: 20–60 minutes by speedboat, 25–40 mins by seaplane or domestic flight + boat.

faqs.question: Are there honeymoon or anniversary specials?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many resorts offer free cake, wine, or upgrades for special occasions.

faqs.question: How early should I book my Maldives trip?
faqs.answer: At least 2–3 months in advance, especially for peak season (Dec–Feb).

know_before_you_go: Visa-on-arrival is available for most nationalities for 30 days; ensure your passport is valid for at least 6 months.
Seaplane transfers operate only between 6:00 AM and 4:00 PM, so late arrivals may require overnight stays in Malé.
The local currency is Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR), but USD is widely accepted in resorts.
Alcohol is prohibited on local islands but served freely at resorts.
When visiting inhabited islands, modest clothing is mandatory; swimwear is only for resorts and designated beaches.
Wi-Fi may be slow or intermittent due to remote island locations — download entertainment in advance.
Electric sockets are mostly UK-style (Type G); carry a universal adapter.
The Maldives has a tropical climate — sunny year-round with occasional showers; pack light, breathable clothing.
Bottled or filtered water is recommended for drinking.
Reef-safe sunscreen is essential to protect marine life and your skin.
Medical facilities are limited on remote islands; carry basic medicines and first-aid.
Marine life is protected — do not touch corals, fish, or turtles.
Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated; many resorts add a service charge.
Travel insurance is strongly recommended for medical emergencies and cancellations.
Drone use may require resort permission; always check rules before flying.
Most resorts offer cashless transactions — charges are billed to your room.
The Maldives is 1–5 hours ahead of GMT depending on the resort's island time (some use 'island time' to give longer daylight hours).
Local SIM cards are available at Malé airport for cheaper internet if needed.
Fresh seafood is abundant — try tuna, reef fish, and Maldivian curries.
Book excursions early to secure your preferred activities, as spots can be limited.

dos: Respect local culture — dress modestly when outside resort areas.
Book seaplane/speedboat transfers in advance to match your flight timings.
Try Maldivian cuisine such as mas huni (tuna & coconut breakfast).
Support eco-friendly resorts that practice sustainable tourism.
Snorkel or dive — the Maldives is a world-class underwater paradise.
Use biodegradable sunscreen to protect coral reefs.
Carry light, quick-dry clothing for tropical weather.
Hydrate often — the tropical sun can cause dehydration quickly.
Take part in cultural activities offered by resorts, like Boduberu drumming shows.
Pack a waterproof bag for boat trips and excursions.
donts: Don’t bring alcohol into the Maldives — it will be confiscated at the airport.
Don’t touch or step on corals — they are fragile and protected.
Don’t collect shells or sand — it’s illegal to take natural items from the Maldives.
Don’t engage in PDA (public display of affection) in local communities.
Don’t litter — always dispose of waste responsibly.
Don’t feed fish or marine animals — it disrupts the ecosystem.
Don’t expect nightlife like big cities — the Maldives is more about relaxation.
Don’t forget travel insurance — emergencies are costly on remote islands.
Don’t ignore safety instructions for water sports and excursions.
Don’t rely solely on resort Wi-Fi if you need strong internet — carry a local SIM.

itinerary.day: DAY 1: Arrival in the Maldives | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to the Maldives! Upon landing at Malé International Airport, you’ll be greeted and transferred to your resort via speedboat or seaplane. As you check in, the soothing sound of waves and panoramic ocean views welcome you to your island escape. Spend the rest of the day unwinding on the beach, sipping tropical cocktails, or taking a dip in the pool. In the evening, enjoy a starlit dinner as the gentle ocean breeze sets the mood for the days ahead.

itinerary.day: DAY 2: Snorkeling & Water Sports Adventure
activities: Begin your day with a delicious breakfast before heading out to explore the Maldives’ famous coral reefs. Snorkel with vibrant marine life — from playful reef fish to graceful sea turtles. Later, try your hand at exciting water sports such as kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding. Spend the afternoon relaxing by the pool or indulging in a beach massage. As the day ends, enjoy a seafood feast by the water’s edge.

itinerary.day: DAY 3: Island Hopping & Sandbank Picnic
activities: Set off after breakfast for an unforgettable island-hopping excursion. Visit a mix of inhabited islands, where you can interact with locals and shop for souvenirs, and uninhabited islands, where untouched nature awaits. A highlight of the day is a sandbank picnic, where you’ll dine with your feet in the water while surrounded by endless turquoise seas. Return to the resort for a relaxing evening with live music or a Maldivian cultural show.

itinerary.day: DAY 4: Sunset Dolphin Cruise & Leisure Day
activities: Spend the morning at leisure — perhaps book a rejuvenating spa treatment or take a yoga session by the beach. In the afternoon, board a traditional Dhoni boat for a sunset dolphin cruise. Watch playful pods of dolphins leap and dance in the golden waters as the sun dips below the horizon. This magical moment, paired with the gentle sea breeze, is the perfect way to end your last full day in paradise.

itinerary.day: DAY 5: Departure from the Maldives
activities: Wake up to your final Maldivian sunrise and savor a leisurely breakfast with ocean views. Depending on your departure time, take a last stroll along the beach or a dip in the lagoon. You’ll then be transferred to Malé International Airport, carrying home memories of crystal-clear waters, tropical sunsets, and the warm Maldivian hospitality.

packages.fagHeading: Tamil Nadu Things to Do – FAQs

faqs.question: What all things can be done in Tamil Nadu?
answer: Relaxing at Marina Beach in Chennai – India’s longest urban beach
Temple hopping – Visit Meenakshi Temple (Madurai), Brihadeeswarar Temple (Thanjavur), Rameswaram Temple
Cruises and amusement parks – Especially in Chennai and Coimbatore
Cultural exploration – Classical music, Bharatanatyam dance, handicrafts
Festive experiences during Navratri (Sep–Oct) and post-harvest festivals (Mar–Jun)

faqs.question: What adventure activities can be done in Tamil Nadu?
answer: Trekking: Anamalai Hills (Topslip), Yelagiri (Jalagamparai Waterfalls), Nilgiris & Kolli Hills
Surfing: Covelong/Kovalam (near Chennai), Mahabalipuram (Bay of Life, Mumu Surf School)
Rock Climbing & Paragliding: Yelagiri (state tourism supported)
Hang Gliding: St. Thomas Mount (Chennai outskirts)

faqs.question: Which are famous treks in Tamil Nadu?
answer: Nilgiri Hills – Located at the tri-junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. Ooty and Kotagiri are prime spots. Best time: September–December and April–June
Kolli Hills (Namakkal District) – Known for 70 hairpin bends and untouched natural beauty. Ideal for serious hikers and meditation seekers

faqs.question: Which are the best places for camping in Tamil Nadu?
answer: Nagalapuram & Tada Falls – Waterfalls + forest camping
Yercaud & Yelagiri – Hill station vibe, great for families
Pichavaram – Unique mangrove camping experience
Mahabalipuram & Pondicherry (TN border) – Coastal camping
Hogenakkal – River camping near waterfalls

faqs.question: Which are the best places for wildlife safari in Tamil Nadu?
answer: Mudumalai Wildlife Sanctuary (near Ooty)
Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary & Topslip (near Coimbatore)
Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary (near Mahabalipuram)
Avalanche Sanctuary (Ooty), Point Calimere (Thanjavur)
Arignar Anna Zoological Park (Chennai), Amirthi Zoo (Vellore)

faqs.question: Which are some famous sites for surfing in Tamil Nadu?
answer: Covelong (Kovalam): Bay of Life Surf School, Ocean Delight Surf School
Mahabalipuram: Mumu Surf School
Neyveli (Pirates): Smaller surf spot attracting local surfers

faqs.question: Which are the best water sports destinations in Tamil Nadu?
answer: Surfing & Windsurfing: Mahabalipuram, Covelong Beach
Scuba Diving: Rameswaram Beach
Boating & Angling: Muttukadu Backwaters (near Chennai), Pykara Lake (near Ooty), Aradha Puzha, Peemund, Kalkundi, Kodi Lake
Aerosports & Hang Gliding: Practiced in Ooty, Kodaikanal, and Yercaud
Paragliding: Kodaikanal

itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Chennai | Chennai Sightseeing Tour
activities: Welcome to Chennai! Upon your arrival at Chennai Airport or Railway Station, you will be transferred to your hotel for check-in. Later, begin your city exploration with a visit to the Kapaleeshwarar Temple in Mylapore, a stunning example of Dravidian architecture. Continue to Fort St. George and the Government Museum, delving into the city’s rich history and heritage. In the evening, take a leisurely stroll along Marina Beach and relax at Elliot’s Beach before returning to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Transfer to Kanchipuram | Temple & Silk Heritage Tour
activities: After breakfast, check out from your hotel and drive to Kanchipuram, famously known as the “City of a Thousand Temples.” Upon arrival, check in at your hotel and later visit the Kanchi Kamakshi Temple, dedicated to Goddess Kamakshi, one of the revered Shakti Peeths. Continue to Ekambareswarar Temple and Kailasanathar Temple, both celebrated for their historical and architectural significance. End the day by exploring Kanchipuram’s renowned silk saree shops before returning to your hotel for the night.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – Transfer to Mahabalipuram | UNESCO Heritage Exploration
activities: After breakfast, check out and proceed to Mahabalipuram. On arrival, check in to your hotel and rest for a while. Later, visit the Shore Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, followed by the Pancha Rathas and the fascinating rock relief of Arjuna’s Penance. Spend some time unwinding at Mahabalipuram Beach and browsing through local handicraft shops before heading back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Transfer to Thanjavur | Temple & Palace Tour
activities: Today, check out and travel to Thanjavur. Upon arrival, check in at your pre-booked hotel and begin your sightseeing tour. Visit the magnificent Brihadeeswarar Temple (Big Temple), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, followed by the Thanjavur Royal Palace and Art Gallery. Continue to Gangaikonda Cholapuram, the Thanjavur Maratha Palace, Schwartz Church, and the Vijayanagar Fort. Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Thanjavur.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 – Return to Chennai | Departure
activities: After breakfast, check out from your hotel in Thanjavur and begin your journey back to Chennai Airport or Railway Station for your onward travel, taking with you cherished memories of your Tamil Nadu adventure.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Madurai | Madurai Sightseeing
activities: Welcome to Madurai, Tamil Nadu's cultural capital! Upon arrival in Madurai, get transferred to your hotel for check-in. Later, you’ll be driven for a sightseeing tour which includes the sacred Meenakshi Amman Temple, an architectural masterpiece. Explore the temple's majestic halls before heading to the stunning Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace. Further, visit the Gandhi Memorial Museum, the Koodal Azhagar Temple and the historic Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam. Later, get driven back to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Transfer to Rameswaram | Visit the Ramanathaswamy Temple and Dhanushkodi
activities: In the morning, you’ll check out from the hotel and get transferred to Rameswaram. Enjoy the scenic journey, passing through picturesque landscapes of Tamil Nadu. Upon arrival, settle into your hotel. Later, you'll be driven to the sacred Ramanathaswamy Temple. Marvel at its impressive corridors adorned with intricately carved pillars. Afterward, explore the ruins of Dhanushkodi, a historic town known for its mythical past and tragic history. Later, get driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Rameswaram Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, you’ll be driven to explore the sacred city of Rameswaram starting with a visit to the iconic Pamban Bridge. Walk along this architectural marvel that connects Rameshwaram to the mainland of India. Next, visit Gandhamadhana Parvatham, a hilltop site believed to have the footprint of Lord Rama. From here, you can enjoy panoramic views of the island. Conclude your tour with a visit to the ancient Kothandaramaswamy Temple before being transferred back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer from Rameswaram to Kodaikanal | Kodaikanal Sightseeing Tour
activities: In the morning, check out from the hotel and get driven to Kodaikanal, also known as the “Princess of Hills”. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel. Later, you'll be driven to visit Kodaikanal Lake, a picturesque man-made lake nestled amidst lush hills. Next, explore the Coaker's Walk, a pathway built on the edge of a cliff. Explore other sites such as Bryant Park and Guna Caves. Lastly, admire the majestic Pillar Rocks, 3 towering rocks standing at 400 feet. Later, get driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Half Day Kodaikanal Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today will be your second day of exploring Kodaikanal. First, you’ll be driven to Bear Shola Falls, a scenic waterfall set amidst lush green hills. Next, visit Green Valley Viewpoint to admire panoramic views of a 500 ft deep valley. Then, head to Pine Forest to capture stunning photos of tall, dense trees. Conclude your tour with a visit to the sacred Kurinji Andavar Temple and learn about the mystery behind the temple’s name. Lastly, get transferred back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Departure
activities: Today, check out from your hotel and get transferred to Coimbatore Airport/Railway Station. From there, you can embark on your journey back home.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival in Bangalore | Transfer to Mysore | Mysore Sightseeing
activities: Upon arrival at Bangalore Airport/Railway Station, embark on a scenic drive to the City of Palaces, Mysore. After checking in to your hotel and relaxing for a while, set out for a captivating sightseeing tour. Visit the sacred Chamundeshwari Temple perched atop the Chamundi Hills, and explore the grandeur of the Mysore Palace. Continue to the Mysore Zoo and Wax Museum before heading to the illuminated Brindavan Gardens for a mesmerizing musical fountain show. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Mysore.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Mysore to Coorg
activities: After breakfast, check out and travel to the picturesque “Scotland of India” – Coorg. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and enjoy the rest of the day at leisure. You may explore the charming town at your own pace, visit the cascading Mallalli Falls, or spot exotic bird species at Pushpagiri Wildlife Sanctuary. For a unique experience, try the popular elephant rides at Nisargadhama before returning to your hotel for the night.

itinerary.day: Day 3 – Coorg Sightseeing
activities: Today, discover the highlights of Coorg on a full-day sightseeing tour. Begin with a visit to Talacauvery and Bhagamandala, two revered pilgrimage sites. Continue to Brahmagiri Hills for stunning views, then stroll through lush coffee plantations. Witness the beauty of Abbey Falls, soak in the peaceful ambience at Raja’s Seat, and admire the historic architecture of Omkareshwar Temple. After your tour, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 – Coorg to Ooty
activities: After breakfast, check out and drive to the enchanting hill station of Ooty, famously known as the “Queen of Hills.” Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and spend the day at leisure. You can explore the colonial charm of the Stone House, relax by Pykara Lake, or visit Deer Park to spot wildlife. Evening at leisure before your overnight stay in Ooty.

itinerary.day: Day 5 – Ooty Sightseeing
activities: After breakfast, embark on a sightseeing tour of Ooty. Visit the vibrant Botanical Gardens and enjoy panoramic views from Doddabetta Peak. Continue to the Tea Garden and Museum to learn about the art of tea-making, followed by a stroll through the beautiful Rose Garden. End your day with a visit to Ooty Lake, where you can opt for boating (at your own expense). Return to your hotel for your final night’s stay.

itinerary.day: Day 6 – Departure from Ooty
activities: After breakfast, check out from your hotel and travel back to Bangalore Airport/Railway Station for your onward journey, carrying fond memories of your Mysore, Coorg, and Ooty tour.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Bangalore | Transfer to Coorg | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Bangalore! Upon arrival at the Bangalore Airport or Railway Station, you will be transferred to Coorg where you will check in at your hotel. Later, you can head out and explore Coorg on your own. You can visit Mallalli Falls, known for its stunning surroundings, or Pushpagiri Wildlife Sanctuary, famous for its variety of birds. Alternatively, you can visit Nisargadhama, known for its elephant rides, among other attractions. Later, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Coorg Sightseeing Tour
activities: In the morning, board the transfer from your hotel for the Coorg sightseeing tour. During the day, you will visit the sacred Talacauvery and Bhagamandala temples, followed by a hike up Bramhagiri Hills. You will also explore the lush coffee plantations of Coorg and visit the stunning Abbey Falls. Conclude your tour with a visit to the historic Omkareshwar Temple and the famous Raja's Seat before being driven back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Ooty | Day at Leisure
activities: Today, you will check out from the hotel and board your transfer to Ooty,`The Queen of the Hill Stations`; Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and enjoy the rest of the day at leisure, exploring the city on your own. You can visit the stunning Stone House, popular as the first house constructed in Ooty, or visit Pykara Lake situated in Pykara village. You can also explore Deer Park. Later, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Ooty Sightseeing Tour
activities: In the morning, get driven from your hotel to explore the city on a sightseeing tour. Begin with a visit to the Botanical Garden, known for a diverse range of plant species. Next, head to Doddabetta Peak, the highest point in the Nilgiris. Wander through the scenic Tea Garden and learn about the tea-making process at the Tea Factory and Museum. Visit the beautiful Rose Garden and the stunning Ooty Lake. Later, get transferred back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer to Kodaikanal | Day at Leisure
activities: Bid adieu to Ooty as you check out from the hotel and get driven to Kodaikanal. Enjoy the scenic views of lush green valleys along the way. Once you reach Kodaikanal, check in to your hotel. You can either relax at your hotel or head out to explore Kodaikanal on your own by visiting places like Berijam Lake, a natural freshwater lake, or the stunning Kumbakkarai Falls, located in the foothills of Kodaikanal hills. Later, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Kodaikanal Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, you will embark on a Kodaikanal sightseeing tour. First, get transferred to Kodaikanal Lake, where you can even opt for boating (at an additional cost). Next, head to the Pillar Rocks viewpoint to admire these three rocks standing tall at the height of 400 ft. Further, walk along Coaker's Walk, a scenic walkway. Also, explore Bryant Park, Guna Caves, Pine Forests, and Bear Shola Falls among other attractions. Later, get transferred back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Departure
activities: Today, check out from the hotel and get transferred to the Bangalore Airport/Railway Station. From there, you can begin your journey back home, marking the end of the trip.
