itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Bangalore | Bangalore Sightseeing Tour
activities: Welcome to Bangalore! Upon arrival at Bangalore Airport/Railway Station, get transferred to your hotel for check-in and rest. Later, get driven on your Bangalore Sightseeing Tour. Begin at Lalbagh Botanical Garden, showcasing historic structures and lush landscapes. Next, move on to Cubbon Park, where nature meets urban charm and visit ISKCON Temple, an architectural marvel. Finally, behold Vidhana Soudha, representing South India’s governance before getting driven to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – Transfer to Coorg | Leisure Day
activities: Post check-out from your hotel, get driven to Coorg. En route, make a stop at Bylukuppe Tibetan Settlement and Kaveri Nisargadhama in Kushalanagar for serene landscapes and cultural insights. Upon arrival in Coorg, check into your hotel and spend the day at leisure. You can trek to Tadiandamol Peak, the highest in Coorg, offering stunning views of the Western Ghats. Next, you can enjoy the soothing sound of cascading water at Mallalli Falls and later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Coorg Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, get driven on a scenic day tour in Coorg! Begin at Talacauvery Temple, where the River Cauvery begins its journey from Bramhagiri hills. Next, visit Bhagamandala Temple nearby, known for the Triveni Sangama. Explore lush coffee plantations, then marvel at Abbey Falls. Later, experience the unique architecture of Omkareshwara Temple and delve into history at Madikeri Fort's museum. Conclude with a serene sunset at Raja Seat and get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Mysore | Day trip to Mysore Palace and Chamundeshwari Temple
activities: In the morning, check-out from your hotel and get driven to Mysore. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and rest for some time. Later, get transferred to Mysore Palace, a stunning example of Indo-Saracenic architecture. Explore its opulent halls and vibrant artworks reflecting royal splendor. Next, visit Chamundeshwari Temple atop Chamundi Hill, and experience the spiritual ambiance and intricate craftsmanship of this ancient temple. Afterwards, get driven to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer to Ooty | Leisure Day
activities: Post check-out, get transferred to Ooty. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and spend the day at leisure. You can visit the historic Stone House, one of the oldest buildings in the town, offering a glimpse into its colonial past. Then, head to the serene Emerald Lake, surrounded by lush greenery, perfect for a leisurely stroll or boating. Finally, explore the Deer Park, home to various species of deer amidst natural surroundings. Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Half Day Ooty Sightseeing Tour | Trip to Coonoor
activities: Today, embark on a delightful Ooty tour by getting driven to Ooty Lake, perfect for serene walks. Next, explore the Botanical Gardens for diverse flora and ascend Doddabetta Peak. Then, visit Rose Garden and get driven to Coonoor for a half day trip. There, explore the botanical wonders of Sim's Park and enjoy the stunning view from Dolphin's Nose. Next, marvel at the cascading Catherine Falls, and take in the scenic views from Lamb’s Rock. Afterwards, get driven to Ooty for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Departure Day
activities: In the morning, check out from your hotel and get driven to Bangalore. Upon arrival at Bangalore Airport/Railway Station, continue your journey towards home, marking an end to this trip.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Kerala?
faqs.answer: The ideal time to visit Kerala is between September and March, just after the monsoon season. The weather is pleasant, making it perfect for exploring backwaters, beaches, and hill stations. The peak tourist season is from October to February, while June to August is preferred by those seeking Ayurvedic treatments during the monsoons.

Honeymooners (5-6 days): Romantic and scenic experiences including hill stations and houseboats.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Kochi | Transfer to Munnar & Sightseeing
activities: Prepare for an unforgettable journey with Tripdekhoo’s special experiences. Upon arrival in Kochi, get driven to Munnar, savoring a traditional Kerala feast along the way. Cross the Neriamangalam Bridge over the Periyar River & marvel at the stunning seven-tiered Cheeyappara Waterfall. At Pottas Fun Farm, enjoy activities (at an extra cost) such as ziplining, a giant swing, and a fish spa. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel, and cap off the day with Kathakali and martial arts performances.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Munnar Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, get driven for a city tour. Begin at the Tata Tea Museum and learn about the tea-making process. Visit the Macofa Chocolate Factory and enjoy an elephant ride at the Carmelagiri Elephant Park (at an extra cost). Admire the scenic views of Mattupetty Dam and visit Echo Point, known for its mesmerizing sound reflections. Take a walk through the vast, rolling Yellapatty Grasslands, and enjoy the boat rides at Kundala Lake (at extra costs). Later, unwind with a rejuvenating Ayurvedic massage.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Alleppey | Houseboat Stay
activities: In the morning, check out from your hotel and get driven to Alleppey. Upon arrival, step aboard a traditional houseboat. As you glide along peaceful waterways, admire the picturesque views of paddy fields & coconut groves. You’ll also have the chance to learn about the traditional lifestyle of the local communities as you pass by their homes. You can also try steering the houseboat yourself as you sail through these calm and scenic waters.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Kochi | Departure
activities: Deboard the houseboat & travel to Kochi. Upon arrival, visit the Dutch Palace, renowned for its intricate murals showcasing scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Next, explore the Jewish Synagogue, famous for its dazzling chandeliers & exquisite hand-painted blue tiles from China. Cap off your day with a romantic stroll along Marine Drive, where you’ll watch the sunset cast a golden glow over the Arabian Sea. Afterwards, get driven to Kochi Airport/ Railway Station for your onward journey.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Kerala?
faqs.answer: The ideal time to visit Kerala is between September and March, just after the monsoon season. The weather is pleasant, making it perfect for exploring backwaters, beaches, and hill stations. The peak tourist season is from October to February, while June to August is preferred by those seeking Ayurvedic treatments during the monsoons.

faqs.question: How many days are required to explore Kerala?
answer: Short trip(4–5 days): Covers top spots like Munnar, Thekkady, and Alleppey.
Family holiday (7-8 days): Ideal for covering Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey, Kovalam, and Kochi at a relaxed pace.
Honeymooners (5-6 days): Romantic and scenic experiences including hill stations and houseboats.

faqs.question: Which is the nearest airport for Kerala?
answer: Cochin International Airport (COK) – Best connected, ideal for central Kerala.
Trivandrum International Airport (TRV) – Ideal for southern Kerala and beaches like Kovalam.
Calicut International Airport (CCJ) – Suitable for northern Kerala (Wayanad, Kozhikode).

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Kochi | Transfer to Munnar | En route Sightseeing || Athirapally Waterfall
activities: Upon arrival, board your transfer to Munnar. Make a stop to savour a traditional Kerala feast bursting with local flavours. En route, visit the majestic 7-tiered Cheeyappara Waterfalls. At Pottas Fun Farm, try activities (extra cost) such as ziplining and giant swing. Later, head to Pettimudi View Point for scenic views of tea estates. Afterwards, check in at the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Munnar Sightseeing Tour
activities: Start your day with Tripdekhoo’s exclusive itinerary, including top attractions as well as hidden gems. Visit the Tata Tea Museum and learn about Munnar's rich tea heritage, then head to Macofa Chocolate Factory to sample chocolates and buy your favourite ones. At Mattupetty Dam, soak in the scenic views and try jet skiing (extra cost). Unwind on the beautiful meadows of Yellapatty Grasslands, relishing sunset views. You can choose to go for an Ayurvedic massage before concluding your day.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Thekkady | En route Sightseeing | Thekkady Sightseeing Tour
activities: Check out and board your transfer to Thekkady. En route stop at the Chunayammakkal Waterfalls and enjoy a toy train ride and ziplining (extra cost). Relish an unparalleled view of the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border from Aruvikkuzhi Viewpoint. Upon arrival, enjoy a boat safari on Periyar Lake, spotting wildlife at Periyar National Park. Later return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Alleppey | En route Sightseeing | Houseboat Stay Experience
activities: After check out, travel to Alleppey, taking a stop at Parunthumpara Hill, famous for its 360-degree views and as a film shooting location. Upon arrival, visit Alleppey Beach and Marari Beach, known for their pristine golden sands and stunning views. Explore the historic Alleppey Lighthouse. Later, board your houseboat for a serene cruise through the backwaters, taking in the surrounding views. You can even take a turn to steer the houseboat, the experience of which will stay with you forever.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Kochi Sightseeing Tour | Departure Day
activities: Deboard the houseboat and head to Kochi. Visit the Dutch Palace, where vibrant murals intricately depict royal history and mythology bringing Kerala’s royal history to life. Marvel at the Jewish Synagogue’s ornate chandeliers & historic blue tiles. Visit St. Francis Church, Vasco da Gama’s original burial site. Cap off your day with a stroll along Marine Drive and observe the age-old Chinese Fishing Nets, a local fishing method still in practice. Get driven to Kochi Airport/Railway Station.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Kerala?
faqs.answer: The ideal time to visit Kerala is between September and March, just after the monsoon season. The weather is pleasant, making it perfect for exploring backwaters, beaches, and hill stations. The peak tourist season is from October to February, while June to August is preferred by those seeking Ayurvedic treatments during the monsoons.

how_to_reach: By Air: The only international airport in Bhutan is Paro International Airport (PBH), with flights from cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Kathmandu, and Bangkok via Druk Air or Bhutan Airlines. Alternatively, you can fly to Bagdogra Airport (IXB) in West Bengal, India—about 170 km from Bhutan's border town Phuentsholing—and continue by road.

By Rail: Bhutan has no railway network. The nearest Indian railway stations are Hasimara (17 km from Phuentsholing), New Alipurduar, and New Jalpaiguri (NJP) near Siliguri. From these stations, taxis or buses can take you to the Bhutan border.

By Road: Bhutan is accessible by road through key border towns like Phuentsholing, Gelephu, and Samdrup Jongkhar. The Phuentsholing entry point is most commonly used, especially when coming from Siliguri or Bagdogra in India. Indian citizens can enter with a valid ID (voter ID or passport) and require an entry permit.
highlight: Enjoy a blend of tradition and nature as you explore Phuntsholing’s gateways, Thimphu’s sacred monasteries, and Paro’s scenic valleys on an amazing journey to Bhutan.
Marvel at the magnificent Buddha Dordenma, a towering statue built to promote world peace, offering a serene retreat amidst the Himalayan landscape.
Hike to the legendary Tiger’s Nest Monastery, where legend says Guru Rinpoche meditated, making it one of the most revered pilgrimage destinations of Bhutan.
Explore the National Memorial Chorten, one of Bhutan’s most important landmarks, where spinning prayer wheels and murmured mantras create a peaceful ambience.
Visit the Motithang Takin Preserve, a conservation centre dedicated to protecting Bhutan’s national animal, offering a rare chance to see these legendary creatures up close.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.
Travellers aren't expected to wear the traditional kira, but you should make sure your clothing covers your arms and legs when entering a Dzong.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Paro | Transfer to Thimphu | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Paro! Upon your arrival at Paro Airport, head to the immigration office for your travel permit. Then, get driven to your hotel in Thimphu. Check in & spend the day at leisure. You can explore Ludrong Memorial Garden, featuring 50 species of native Bhutanese plants & herbs. Experience Bhutanese culture at Simply Bhutan & witness live demonstrations of traditional crafts. You can also relax in Deer Park, modeled after India’s Deer Park. Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, you'll be driven to explore Thimphu. Visit the National Memorial Chorten & admire its religious paintings. Next, admire the 51.5-meter-tall Buddha Dordenma, housing the world’s largest Buddha statue. At Motithang Preserve, you might spot Bhutan's national animal. Then, explore Tashichho Dzong, a stunning fortress housing government offices, & Simtokha Dzong, the oldest dzong in Bhutan. Later, you can shop for souvenirs at the Handicrafts Emporium before getting driven to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Paro | Paro Sightseeing Tour
activities: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be driven to Paro. Upon arrival, explore Drukgyel Dzong, which served as a stronghold against Tibetan invasions. Next, gaze at the majestic Mt. Jhomolhari, Bhutan’s second-highest peak at 7,314 meters, known for its stunning beauty and cultural significance. Visit Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples, dating back to the 7th century, believed to hold spiritual power. Afterward, check in at your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
activities: Today, begin your journey at Ta Dzong, a watchtower that serves as a national museum.Next, visit Rinpung Dzong. Then, visit Tiger’s Nest parking lot, where your 7 km hike to the Taktsang Monastery. As you ascend through lush pine forests adorned with colorful prayer flags, take in the views of the Paro Valley. Upon arrival at the monastery, explore its prayer wheels, meditation caves, and intricate murals dedicated to Guru Rinpoche. Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Departure Day
activities: In the morning, get ready and check out of your hotel in Paro. Then, board your transfer and get driven to Paro Airport for your flight back home. This marks the end of your Bhutan Trip!

about_the_tour: Embark on a soulful journey with our Bhutan Tour Package, where every moment is wrapped in peace, discovery, and wonder. Walk through serene monasteries like the iconic Tiger’s Nest, breathe in the crisp Himalayan air of Paro and Thimphu, and let the vibrant local markets and traditional architecture charm every member of the family. From nature walks to cultural encounters, Bhutan offers more than a holiday—it’s a gentle adventure that brings hearts closer in a land where happiness truly matters.
how_to_reach: By Air: The only international airport in Bhutan is Paro International Airport (PBH), with flights from cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Kathmandu, and Bangkok via Druk Air or Bhutan Airlines. Alternatively, you can fly to Bagdogra Airport (IXB) in West Bengal, India—about 170 km from Bhutan's border town Phuentsholing—and continue by road.

By Rail: Bhutan has no railway network. The nearest Indian railway stations are Hasimara (17 km from Phuentsholing), New Alipurduar, and New Jalpaiguri (NJP) near Siliguri. From these stations, taxis or buses can take you to the Bhutan border.

By Road: Bhutan is accessible by road through key border towns like Phuentsholing, Gelephu, and Samdrup Jongkhar. The Phuentsholing entry point is most commonly used, especially when coming from Siliguri or Bagdogra in India. Indian citizens can enter with a valid ID (voter ID or passport) and require an entry permit.

Explore the National Memorial Chorten, one of Bhutan’s most important landmarks, where spinning prayer wheels and murmured mantras create a peaceful ambience.
Visit the Motithang Takin Preserve, a conservation centre dedicated to protecting Bhutan’s national animal, offering a rare chance to see these legendary creatures up close.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
activities: Upon your arrival at Siliguri Railway Station or Bagdogra Airport, get driven to your hotel in Phuntsholing. Check in and spend your time at leisure. You can visit Bhutan Gate, a striking traditional gateway that beautifully marks the entry into Bhutan. If you wish, you can also visit Amo Chhu Crocodile Breeding Centre lets you witness Bhutan’s wildlife conservation efforts up close, among other famous attractions.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
activities: Today, check out from the hotel and visit the immigration office to obtain your travel permit. Next, get driven to your hotel in Thimphu. After checking in, take the day to explore at your own pace. You can visit Clock Tower Square to admire the beautiful Bhutanese architecture, or immerse yourself in the nation’s history at Simply Bhutan. If you’re a nature lover, you can explore the Royal Botanical Garden to see the variety of plant life. Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Thimphu Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Paro
activities: In the morning, check out and get driven for a sightseeing tour of Thimphu. First, admire the National Memorial Chorten, a stupa that celebrates Bhutan's third king. Visit the Motithang Takin Preserve to catch a glimpse of Bhutan’s national animal. Marvel at the enormous golden Buddha Dordenma statue & later, explore the Tashichho Dzong, a fortress-monastery that houses several temples and chapels. After visiting other places, get driven to Paro & upon arrival, check in to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery
activities: Today, check out and get transferred to the base of Tiger’s Nest Monastery. Begin your hike, which takes you through lush pine forests adorned with colourful prayer flags fluttering in the breeze. The trek offers stunning views of the surrounding valley and the monastery perched high on a cliff, at 3,120 meters above sea level. Once at the monastery, step inside & explore its prayer wheels, intricate murals, and stunning artwork. Afterwards, get driven back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
activities: After you check out in the morning, get driven to Phuntsholing. After you arrive, check in at the hotel. Later, you can spend your time exploring places like Zangto Pelri, a replica of Guru Rinpoche’s celestial abode. Alternatively, you may admire stunning views from Karbandi Monastery, where lush gardens & prayer flags create a peaceful escape. While exploring the town, you can try Bhutanese dishes like Ema Datshi (chilli cheese) & momos at local eateries, before returning back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Transfer to Siliguri | Departure Day
activities: In the morning, check out of the hotel and get transferred to New Jalpaiguri Railway Station/Bagdogra International Airport. En route, make a stop at the immigration office. Continue your journey onward and this marks the end of your trip.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Paro | Transfer to Thimphu | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Bhutan! Upon arrival at Paro Airport, head to the immigration office for your travel permit. Then, get driven to your hotel in Thimphu. Check in & spend the day at your leisure. You can visit places like the Royal Botanical Garden & the National Institute for Zorig Chusum, housing the Bhutanese arts & crafts. Also, visit Zilukha Anim Dratshang & learn about the nuns' lifestyles & experiences through interactive sessions. Later, return to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, get transferred to explore Thimphu. Visit the National Memorial Chorten, a stupa built in honour of Bhutan’s third king. Next, visit Tashichho Dzong, a fortress monastery that serves as Bhutan’s government’s seat. Continue to Simtokha Dzong & also witness the Buddha Dordenma statue. Head to the Motithang Takin Preserve to see Bhutan's national animal, the takin. Conclude your tour at the Handicrafts Market before getting driven to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Nubding | Gangtey Sightseeing Tour
activities: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be driven to Nubding. En route stop at Dochula Pass & the historic Wangdue Phodrang Dzong, admired for its architecture. Upon arrival in Nubding, check in to your hotel and later embark on a sightseeing tour of Gangtey. Explore the peaceful Phobjikha Valley, famous for its beautiful landscapes and the winter home of the endangered blacknecked cranes. After visiting other such attractions, get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Punakha | Half-Day Punakha Sightseeing Tour
activities: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be transferred to Punakha. Upon arrival, check in and relax for a while. Later, get driven to explore Punakha. Start by visiting Punakha Dzong, a fortress located at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers, renowned for its architecture. Next, visit Chimi Lhakhang Temple, famously known as the Fertility Temple. Afterward, admire the serene beauty of the Mo Chhu River before getting driven to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer to Paro | Paro Sightseeing Tour
activities: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be driven to Paro. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and then embark on a sightseeing tour of Paro. Start with a visit to Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest and most sacred temples. Next, explore the ruins of Drukgyel Dzong, a historic fortress that offers views of the Paro Valley. Continue to the base of Mount Jhomolhari, Bhutan’s second-highest peak, revered as a sacred site. Later, get driven to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Hike To Tiger's Nest Monastery
activities: Today, you'll be driven to Ta Dzong, an ancient watchtower housing the National Museum of Bhutan. Next, explore the Rinpung Dzong, renowned for its impressive architecture. Afterward, proceed to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang, the starting point for a scenic hike to the Taktsang Monastery, or Tiger’s Nest. Trek through lush pine forests, soaking in the surrounding views before reaching the monastery to explore the sacred site. Later, get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Departure Day
activities: Today, check out of the hotel and get transferred to the Paro International Airport to board your flight for the onward journey. This is where your trip comes to an end.

about_the_tour: Embark on a soulful journey with our Bhutan Tour Package, where every moment is wrapped in peace, discovery, and wonder. Walk through serene monasteries like the iconic Tiger’s Nest, breathe in the crisp Himalayan air of Paro and Thimphu, and let the vibrant local markets and traditional architecture charm every member of the family. From nature walks to cultural encounters, Bhutan offers more than a holiday—it’s a gentle adventure that brings hearts closer in a land where happiness truly matters.
how_to_reach: By Air: The only international airport in Bhutan is Paro International Airport (PBH), with flights from cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Kathmandu, and Bangkok via Druk Air or Bhutan Airlines. Alternatively, you can fly to Bagdogra Airport (IXB) in West Bengal, India—about 170 km from Bhutan's border town Phuentsholing—and continue by road.

By Rail: Bhutan has no railway network. The nearest Indian railway stations are Hasimara (17 km from Phuentsholing), New Alipurduar, and New Jalpaiguri (NJP) near Siliguri. From these stations, taxis or buses can take you to the Bhutan border.

By Road: Bhutan is accessible by road through key border towns like Phuentsholing, Gelephu, and Samdrup Jongkhar. The Phuentsholing entry point is most commonly used, especially when coming from Siliguri or Bagdogra in India. Indian citizens can enter with a valid ID (voter ID or passport) and require an entry permit.
highlight: Enjoy a blend of tradition and nature as you explore Phuntsholing’s gateways, Thimphu’s sacred monasteries, and Paro’s scenic valleys on an amazing journey to Bhutan.

Hike to the legendary Tiger’s Nest Monastery, where legend says Guru Rinpoche meditated, making it one of the most revered pilgrimage destinations of Bhutan.
Explore the National Memorial Chorten, one of Bhutan’s most important landmarks, where spinning prayer wheels and murmured mantras create a peaceful ambience.
Visit the Motithang Takin Preserve, a conservation centre dedicated to protecting Bhutan’s national animal, offering a rare chance to see these legendary creatures up close.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Day at Leisure
activities: Welcome to Siliguri! Upon arrival at the Bagdogra Airport/New Jalpaiguri Railway Station, board your transfer to the beautiful Phuntsholing Border Town. After checking in to your hotel, spend the rest of the day at leisure, where you can visit the Amo Chhu Crocodile Breeding Centre and witness the rare and endangered crocodiles up close. Also, you can stroll along the serene Torsa Riverside and soak-in its amazing atmosphere. Later, return to your hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Transfer to Thimphu | Day at Leisure
activities: After check-out, proceed to the immigration office & obtain your travel permit. Then, enjoy a scenic drive to Thimphu, & upon arrival, check in to your hotel and spend the rest of your day at leisure. You can visit Clock Tower Square and marvel at its intricate carvings with artistic designs. Also, you can explore Simply Bhutan and immerse yourself in Bhutan’s rich heritage through exhibits or visit the Royal Botanical Garden showcasing Bhutan’s diverse flora. Later, return to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, explore Thimphu on a sightseeing tour. Start with a visit to the National Memorial Chorten & admire its intricate design stupa. Continue to the iconic Buddha Dordenma Statue, one of the world's largest Buddha statues, and witness Bhutan’s unique national animal, the Takin, at the Motithang Takin Preserve. Also, visit Tashichho Dzong before heading to Simtokha Dzong, the oldest dzong in Bhutan. Later, explore the Handicrafts Market for traditional souvenirs & get transferred to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Punakha via Dochula Pass | Punakha Sightseeing Tour
activities: Post check out, board your transfer, & get driven to Punakha. En route, take a stop at the Dochula Pass and soak-in the stunning views of the Himalayan mountains. Once in Punakha, explore Punakha and visit Chimi Lhakhang, also called 'The Temple of Fertility.' Then, explore the Punakha Dzong, located between the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers. Also, admire its vibrant murals and intricate designs. Later, get transferred to your hotel for check-in and enjoy your comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Day Trip to Gangtey
activities: Today, enjoy a scenic drive to Gangtey, known for its natural beauty. Start with a visit to the Phobjikha Valley, a stunning glacial valley, home to the rare Tibetan black-necked cranes. Next, visit the iconic Gangtey Gompa Monastery and soak-in the views of the Phobjikha Valley. Continue to Wangdiphodrang Dzong, a fortress that stands at the confluence of the Mo Chhu and Tang Chhu rivers. Also, admire its stunning Bhutanese architecture before getting transferred to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Transfer to Paro | Paro Sightseeing Tour
activities: In the morning, check out and get transferred to Paro, passing through charming Bhutanese villages. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and later, enjoy a sightseeing tour. Start with a visit to the Drukgyel Dzong, an iconic fortress offering a glimpse into Bhutan's military past. Next, pay your respects at the Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples, dating back to the 7th century. After an amazing day, get transferred to your hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 – Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
activities: Today, visit Ta Dzong, a former watchtower now a National Museum showcasing Bhutan’s rich cultural heritage. Next, explore Rinpung Dzong, an iconic fortress with stunning Bhutanese architecture. Then, hike to the legendary Taktsang Monastery (Tiger’s Nest), perched on a cliffside. As you ascend through pine forests adorned with prayer flags, enjoy the breathtaking views. Upon reaching the temple, explore sacred meditation caves & murals. Afterwards, descend the trail & get driven to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 8 - Departure Day
activities: After checking out of the hotel, you will be driven to the Bhutan Immigration Office. Complete your formalities and get transferred to Paro International Airport for your journey back home. This marks the end to your amazing Bhutan trip!

From Guwahati, you can hire a taxi or take a shared cab to Shillong. Shillong Airport (SHL) in Umroi also operates limited domestic flights.

By Rail: Meghalaya does not have a railway network. The closest railhead is Guwahati Railway Station, well connected to major Indian cities. From there, road travel is required to reach Shillong or other parts of Meghalaya.

By Road: Meghalaya is easily accessible by road from Guwahati via NH6. Regular state-run and private buses, shared sumos, and taxis operate between Guwahati and Shillong, making the journey scenic and comfortable.
highlight: Discover the breathtaking beauty of Shillong, Cherrapunji, and Dawki as you explore misty hills, cascading waterfalls, and pristine rivers in the Abode of Clouds.
Trek through dense forests to witness Meghalaya’s famous Double Decker Living Root Bridge, a marvel of bio-engineering made entirely of natural roots.
Stand in awe of NohKaLikai Falls, India’s tallest plunge waterfall, where water dramatically plunges 1,115 feet into a misty pool below.
Visit Dawki and marvel at the crystal-clear waters of the Umngot River, often called the cleanest river in India, with boats appearing to float on air.
Experience panoramic views of verdant valleys and dramatic cliffs at Laitlum Canyon, a hidden gem offering one of Meghalaya’s best vistas.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Meghalaya?
faq.answer: The best time to visit Meghalaya is from October to April, when the weather is pleasant and ideal for sightseeing, trekking, and river activities. Monsoon (June to September) enhances the waterfalls but may cause roadblocks or heavy rainfall delays.

faq.question: Is Meghalaya safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Yes, Meghalaya is considered safe for tourists, including solo travelers and families. The locals are warm and welcoming. Still, always travel with a guide in remote areas and avoid night travel in lesser-known regions.

faq.question: How do I reach Meghalaya?
faq.answer:
By Air: Nearest airport is Guwahati (GAU), 100 km from Shillong. Shillong has a small airport (Umroi) with limited connectivity.

By Rail: No rail station in Meghalaya. The nearest is Guwahati Railway Station.

By Road: Meghalaya is well connected to Guwahati by NH6; taxis and buses are readily available.

faq.question: What kind of accommodation is available in Meghalaya?
faq.answer: Meghalaya offers a range of accommodations from budget guesthouses to deluxe and luxury hotels. In places like Shillong and Cherrapunji, options are plenty, while in remote areas, stays may be basic.

faq.question: Do I need any permits to travel in Meghalaya?
faq.answer: Indian citizens generally do not require permits. However, you may need entry permits for certain eco-sensitive or tribal areas, and your tour operator usually arranges these.

faq.question: What are must-do activities in Meghalaya?
faq.answer:
Trek to Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)

Boating on the Umngot River at Dawki

Visit NohKaLikai and Seven Sisters waterfalls

Explore Mawsmai and Arwah caves

Sunset at Laitlum Canyon

Visit Mawlynnong (Asia’s cleanest village)

faq.question: Is the Nongriat trek suitable for all age groups?
faq.answer: The trek to the Double Decker Root Bridge involves over 3,000 steep steps, so it is not advisable for elderly travelers or those with mobility issues. Good fitness and hiking shoes are essential.

faq.question: Is mobile network and internet available across Meghalaya?
faq.answer: Yes, BSNL, Jio, and Airtel have decent coverage in major towns like Shillong and Cherrapunji. However, connectivity may be poor or unavailable in remote areas like Dawki or Nongriat.

faq.question: What should I pack for the Meghalaya trip?
faq.answer:
Rain gear (umbrella/raincoat) – sudden rain is common

Warm clothing – evenings can be chilly

Good hiking shoes – for treks and walks

Torch, power bank, and personal medications

Government-issued photo ID (except PAN card)

faq.question: Are ATMs and cards accepted in Meghalaya?
faq.answer: ATMs are available in major towns like Shillong and Cherrapunji. However, remote areas may have limited ATM access and some shops may not accept cards—carry enough cash.

faq.question: Are boating and adventure activities included in the package?
faq.answer: No, activities like boating in Dawki, kayaking, zip-lining, and cave exploration are chargeable extras, payable on the spot. Prices may vary based on location and season.

faq.question: Can Meghalaya be visited with kids and elderly people?
faq.answer: Yes, Meghalaya is suitable for families. However, avoid strenuous treks like Nongriat with very young children or elderly people. Most sightseeing spots are easily accessible by vehicle.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Guwahati | Transfer to Cherrapunji | Cherrapunji Sightseeing Tour
activities: Welcome to Adobe of Clouds, Meghalaya! Upon reaching Guwahati Airport/railway station/bus stand, you'll be taken to Cherrapunji, "the land of oranges." After reaching, explore the city on a city sightseeing tour and visit popular attractions such as the Arwah Caves and witness the natural wonders inside the caves. Continue to the Seven Sisters Falls, NohKaLikai Falls, and more. Afterwards, you'll be driven to your hotel in Cherrapunji for check-in, followed by an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Trekking at Nongriat
activities: Today, you'll be taken to the stunning Tyrna Village for your adventurous Nongriat Trek. Begin your trek, exploring the Tyrna Village while learning about the vibrant culture of Meghalaya from the local guide. Continue your trek through lush forests, crossing rivers, to visit the famous Double Decker Root Living Bridge. Post-trek, you'll be transferred back to your hotel from Tyrna village and enjoy your comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Mawlynnong Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Dawki
activities: After check-out, you'll be driven towards Dawki. En route, you'll visit a small village, Mawlynnong, known as the cleanest village in Asia. Also, explore the unique Balancing Rock and experience the rich Khasi culture at Riwai village. Next, continue your journey to Dawki, and upon arrival, check-in to your hotel, followed by a comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Shillong
activities: Check-out from your hotel and begin your journey towards Shillong, the "Scotland of the East." Upon your arrival, check-in at your pre-booked hotel and spend the rest of the day at leisure. You can explore the city at your own pace by visiting attractions such as the Air Force Museum, All Saints Cathedral, and more. Later, return to your hotel on your own for an comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Departure Day
activities: Today, check-out from your hotel, and you'll be taken to the famous Kamakhya Devi Temple. Pay your respects to the temple deity and witness the temple architecture reflecting indigenous Assamese styles. Later, you will be driven to Guwahati Airport / Railway Station / bus station for your journey back home, marking the end of your trip.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Guwahati | Transfer to Shillong | Leisure Day
activities: Upon arrival in Guwahati, you will be transferred to Shillong, passing by cascading waterfalls and lush landscapes. En route, visit Umiam Lake for a peaceful retreat. After spending some time at the lake, continue your journey to Shillong, and upon arrival, check in at the hotel. You can relax for the day or explore the city on your own. Phan Nonglait Park and Spread Eagle Falls are key attractions that we recommend, among others. Later, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Transfer to Cherrapunji | Cherrapunji Sightseeing Tour
activities: Check out and get driven to Cherrapunji. En route, stop at the stunning Elephant Falls, a beautiful three-tiered waterfall. On arrival in Cherrapunji, embark on a city sightseeing tour. Admire the breathtaking Seven Sisters Waterfall and the towering NohKaLikai Falls, the tallest in India. Explore the Mawsmai and Arwah Caves, known for their impressive limestone formations. Later, check into your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Trek to Nongriat Double Decker Living Root Bridge
activities: In the morning, you will be driven to Tyrna Village from the hotel for an exciting Nongriat Trek. Along the journey, enjoy the vibrant landscapes of Meghalaya. After reaching Tyrna Village, you will ascend 3,500 steps to Nongriat and visit the awe-inspiring Double Decker Living Root Bridge. Afterwards, you can also extend your hike to the Rainbow Falls at an extra cost. Later, get driven back from Tyrna village to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Dawki via Mawlynnong | Trek to Single Decker Living Root Bridge
activities: After checking out of the hotel, get driven to Dawki with a stop at Mawlynnong, famed as the ‘Cleanest Village of Asia.’ Trek to the Single Decker Living Root Bridge in Riwai Village, and take time to marvel at the fascinating Balancing Rock. After your trek, continue toward Dawki. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel, and later, you can explore the town at your own pace, visiting the pristine Umngot River, known as one of the cleanest rivers in India.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer to Shillong | En route Sightseeing
activities: Check out and board your transfer to the Shnongpdeng Village, where you can indulge in adventure activities (extra cost) like kayaking, and boating. After this, continue your journey to Shillong. En route, visit the beautiful Krang Shuri Waterfalls, set amidst lush forests. Also, enjoy a hike on the stunning trails of Laitlum Canyon, offering stunning views of the surrounding hills and valleys. Once you reach your hotel in Shillong, check in for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Transfer to Guwahati | Visit to Kamakhya Devi Temple | Departure
activities: In the morning, check out of the hotel and board your transfer to Guwahati. Upon arrival, visit the Kamakhya Devi Temple, one of the oldest and most revered centres of Tantric practices, dedicated to the goddess Kamakhya. After the visit, continue your journey to Guwahati Airport/Railway Station for your departure. This is where your trip comes to an end.

faq.question: Is Meghalaya safe for tourists?

faq.question: How do I reach Meghalaya?
faq.answer:
By Air: Nearest airport is Guwahati (GAU), 100 km from Shillong. Shillong has a small airport (Umroi) with limited connectivity.

By Rail: No rail station in Meghalaya. The nearest is Guwahati Railway Station.

By Road: Meghalaya is well connected to Guwahati by NH6; taxis and buses are readily available.

faq.question: What kind of accommodation is available in Meghalaya?
faq.answer: Meghalaya offers a range of accommodations from budget guesthouses to deluxe and luxury hotels. In places like Shillong and Cherrapunji, options are plenty, while in remote areas, stays may be basic.

faq.question: Do I need any permits to travel in Meghalaya?
faq.answer: Indian citizens generally do not require permits. However, you may need entry permits for certain eco-sensitive or tribal areas, and your tour operator usually arranges these.

faq.question: What are must-do activities in Meghalaya?

Trek to Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)

Boating on the Umngot River at Dawki

Explore Mawsmai and Arwah caves

Sunset at Laitlum Canyon

Visit Mawlynnong (Asia’s cleanest village)

faq.question: Is the Nongriat trek suitable for all age groups?
faq.answer: The trek to the Double Decker Root Bridge involves over 3,000 steep steps, so it is not advisable for elderly travelers or those with mobility issues. Good fitness and hiking shoes are essential.

faq.question: Is mobile network and internet available across Meghalaya?
faq.answer: Yes, BSNL, Jio, and Airtel have decent coverage in major towns like Shillong and Cherrapunji. However, connectivity may be poor or unavailable in remote areas like Dawki or Nongriat.

faq.question: What should I pack for the Meghalaya trip?
faq.answer:
Rain gear (umbrella/raincoat) – sudden rain is common

Warm clothing – evenings can be chilly

Good hiking shoes – for treks and walks

Torch, power bank, and personal medications

Government-issued photo ID (except PAN card)

faq.question: Are ATMs and cards accepted in Meghalaya?
faq.answer: ATMs are available in major towns like Shillong and Cherrapunji. However, remote areas may have limited ATM access and some shops may not accept cards—carry enough cash.

faq.question: Are boating and adventure activities included in the package?
faq.answer: No, activities like boating in Dawki, kayaking, zip-lining, and cave exploration are chargeable extras, payable on the spot. Prices may vary based on location and season.

faq.question: Can Meghalaya be visited with kids and elderly people?
faq.answer: Yes, Meghalaya is suitable for families. However, avoid strenuous treks like Nongriat with very young children or elderly people. Most sightseeing spots are easily accessible by vehicle.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Guwahati | Transfer to Kaziranga
activities: Welcome to Guwahati! Upon arrival at Guwahati Airport, you'll be transferred to your camp/lodge in Kaziranga. En route, enjoy stunning views of Assam’s lush tea plantations stretching across the landscape. Upon arrival, check in and relax for a while. Later, you can explore nearby tribal villages, where you can interact with the locals and experience their unique culture. Afterward, return to your camp/lodge for an overnight stay amidst nature.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Kaziranga National Park Safari | Transfer to Shillong | Day at Leisure
activities: In the morning, get ready for a jeep safari at Kaziranga National Park, where you can spot the one-horned rhinoceros, elephants, tigers, wild buffalo, & various birds. Afterward, return to your hotel to check out. Then, drive to Shillong, enjoying views of Umiam Lake along the way. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and spend the day at your leisure. You can explore local attractions like Sweet Falls, Bishop Falls, and All Saints Cathedral. Later, head back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Cherrapunji | Elephant Falls Visit | Cherrapunji Sightseeing Tour
activities: After checking out, you'll be transferred to Elephant Falls, a three-tiered waterfall surrounded by greenery. Next, visit Cherrapunji, known for its heavy rainfall and lush landscapes. Witness the Seven Sisters Waterfalls, a collection of seven falls that flow down the hills. Then, visit NohKaLikai Falls, the tallest waterfall in India at 1,115 feet. Afterward, explore Mawsmai and Arwah caves, famous for their limestone formations. Later, get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Trek to Nongriat Double Decker Living Root Bridge
activities: In the morning, board your transfer to Tyrna Village for an exciting trek. Immerse yourself in the rich culture of the village and start ascending towards the Double Decker Living Root Bridge. Upon reaching, marvel at the structure of the bridge, crafted by Khasi people over several years, using roots of Banyan trees. You can choose to extend your hike to the Rainbow Falls (extra cost). Afterwards, you will be driven back to your hotel in Cherrapunji for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer to Dawki via Mawlynnong | Trek to Single Decker Root Bridge
activities: After checking out of your hotel get transferred to Dawki. En route, visit Mawlynnong, the ‘Cleanest Village of Asia,’ and witness the Khasi culture. Then, trek to the Single Decker Living Root Bridge in Riwai Village. Also, witness the unique Balancing Rock. Afterward, continue your journey towards Dawki, where you will admire the beauty of the Umngot River, with the water so clear that the riverbed can be seen. Upon arrival at the hotel, check-in to enjoy an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Transfer to Shillong | Visit Krang Shuri Falls & Laitlum Canyon
activities: After checking out of your hotel, you'll be driven to the Shnongpdeng Village. Here, you can enjoy thrilling adventure activities (extra cost) like kayaking, and boating. Then, continue your journey to Shillong. En route, visit Krang Shuri Waterfalls, set amidst lush forests. Also, enjoy hiking on the trails of Laitlum Canyon and witness stunning views of the surrounding hills and valleys. Afterward, you will be transferred to your hotel in Shillong. Check-in for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Visit to Kamakhya Devi Temple | Departure Day
activities: In the morning, check out and get transferred to the Kamakhya Devi Temple in Guwahati, one of the oldest and most revered temples, dedicated to Goddess Kamakhya. After the visit, continue your journey to Guwahati Airport/Railway Station for your departure. This is where your trip ends.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Guwahati | Transfer to Shillong | Stopover at Umiam Lake
activities: Welcome to Guwahati, the Gateway to Northeast India! Upon your arrival at the Guwahati airport/ railway station, you will be driven to Shillong. En route, you will make a brief stop at Umiam Lake, a stunning man-made lake known for its scenic landscape. Afterwards, continue your journey towards Shillong. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel in Shillong and spend the day at your leisure. You can visit the Lady Hydari Park, or shop at the bustling police bazar before returning to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Transfer to Cherrapunji | Trip to Elephant Falls | Cherrapunji Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, you will check-out from the hotel and board the transfer for your journey to Cherrapunji. En route, you will visit the beautiful Elephant Falls in Shillong. Continue your journey towards Cherrapunji. En route, you will also explore Masami Caves and the mesmerizing Arwah Caves. Witness the stunning Nohkalikai Falls and the breathtaking Seven Sister Falls. Later, you will be driven to your hotel in Cherrapunji for check-in and an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Trek to Double Decker Root Bridge
activities: Wake up early today and enjoy the views of Cherrapunji at sunrise before you board the transfer and proceed to Tyrna village. Begin your trek to the iconic Double Decker Root Bridge (Nongriat) with a local guide. Optionally, you can extend your hike to the Rainbow Falls for an extra cost. Conclude the trek by climbing 3500 steps back to Tyrna village by evening. Afterwards, you will be driven to the hotel in Cherrapunji for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Day Trip to Mawphlang | Trek to David Scott Trail
activities: In the morning, you will be starting your adventure to Mawphlang. You will be driven to this small village, where you will begin the David Scott Trail with a local guide, crossing valleys and small streams. Experience a 5-hour trek through beautiful landscapes, before being driven back to your hotel in Cherrapunji.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Trek to Single Decker Living Root Bridge | Transfer to Dawki
activities: Post check out, you will be transferred to Mawlynnong, the cleanest village in Asia. From here, you will trek to the Single Decker Living Root Bridge in Riwai village and visit the Balancing Rock. Continue to Dawki and en route make a stop to see the pristine Umngot River, known as the cleanest river in Asia. Upon arrival, you will check in at your hotel and enjoy an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Transfer to Shillong | Visit Krang Shuri Waterfalls and Laitlum Canyon
activities: After checking out from your hotel in Dawki, you'll be driven to Shnongpdeng, where you can indulge in adventure activities like kayaking and boating (at your own expense). Then, you'll be transferred to Shillong. En route, make a brief stop at the breathtaking Krang Suri Waterfalls and also at the scenic trails of Laitlum Canyon. Upon arrival in Shillong, you will check in at your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Transfer to Guwahati | Guwahati Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, check out from the hotel and get transferred to Guwahati. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel and head out for sightseeing. You will be driven to visit the Assam State Museum to learn about the rich culture and history. Explore the Assam State Zoo, home to exotic animals and take a boat ride to Umananda Island to visit the Umananda Temple. In the evening, you can enjoy a cruise on the Brahmaputra River (at your own expense), before getting transferred back to the hotel for the night.

itinerary.day: DAY 8 - Departure Day
activities: In the morning, check-out from the hotel and get transferred to the beautiful Kamakhya Devi Temple. Later, you will be driven to the Guwahati Airport/ Railway Station for your journey back home, marking an end of your trip.

faqs.question: What are the best things to do in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: Visit Namdapha National Park – Explore lush forests and spot rare wildlife like the red panda in this biodiversity hotspot.
Trek in Dirang – A scenic hill town ideal for trekking, hot springs, and learning about tribal cultures.
Watch the Sunset in Roing – Enjoy a serene sunset by the Dibang River surrounded by greenery.
Relax at Glow Lake – A secluded spot in Tezu surrounded by hills, perfect for nature lovers and couples.
Admire Nuranang Falls – Visit this spectacular 100-meter waterfall near Tawang for breathtaking views.
Drive to Sela Pass – A high-altitude mountain pass known for its sacred lake and stunning snow-covered scenery.
Raft on the Kameng River – Experience thrilling white-water rafting surrounded by untouched nature.
Trek to Talle Valley – Discover remote forest trails and interact with the Apatani tribe near Ziro.
Explore Upper Dibang Valley – Visit India’s largest district with lush valleys, gorges, and rivers.
Visit Ziro Valley – Known for the Ziro Music Festival, pine-clad hills, and unique tribal life.

faqs.question: What are the best adventure activities to do in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: River Rafting – On rivers like Brahmaputra, Subansiri, Siang, and Lohit.
Trekking and Hiking – Across pristine mountains, forests, and tribal villages.
Fishing and Angling – Popular in many river systems; great for peaceful nature experiences.
Bird Watching – With hotspots like Dirang, Sangti Valley, and Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary.

faqs.question: Which are the best places for river rafting in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: Brahmaputra River – Starts at Dibrugarh and offers Grade IV+ rapids through remote forests.
Subansiri River – Offers intense rapids and scenic tribal surroundings.
Siang River – Has both calm and challenging sections with amazing landscape views.
Lohit River – Known for Grade V rapids in some of the country’s remotest areas.

faqs.question: Which are the most adventurous places for trekking in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: Talley Valley Trek – Lush forests and biodiversity make this a top trek.
Bailey Trail – Follows a historic route with views of the highest Himalayan peaks.
Ziro Trek – Great for nature walks, tribal interaction, and scenic views.
Mechuka Trek – A challenging, offbeat trek through valleys, rivers, and untouched nature.

faqs.question: Where can I enjoy kayaking in Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Kayaking is best experienced on the Brahmaputra River, offering scenic routes and calm to challenging water stretches for paddling.

faqs.question: Where can I enjoy paragliding in Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Tawang is the top spot for paragliding, providing panoramic views of snow-capped mountains, valleys, and monasteries.

faqs.question: Where can I go skiing in Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Head to Pankang Teng Tso Lake near Tawang during winter when the lake and surrounding areas turn into a snowy paradise ideal for skiing.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit is between October and April, when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing, adventure sports, and attending cultural festivals.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Guwahati | Transfer to Bhalukpong | Leisure Day
activities: Welcome to Guwahati, the gateway to the Northeast. Upon arrival at Guwahati Airport, you will be transferred to Bhalukpong, a medieval town renowned for its thrilling activities. The Kameng River flows through the town, offering numerous opportunities for adventure. Check in to the hotel and take the rest of the day at your own pace. You can indulge in some adventurous activities like river rafting or canoeing on the banks of River Kameng. Return to the hotel at your convenience.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Transfer from Bhalukpong to Dirang | Explore the hubs of tribes and diverse culture
activities: Check out and start your journey to Dirang. En route, stop at Tippi Orchid Research Centre, known as the orchid paradise, housing over 500 orchid species. Following this, head to Nag Mandir to honour the snake deity and take in the calm atmosphere. Proceed with your journey, check into the hotel in Dirang and rest before starting Dirang's city tour. Later, visit the apple and Kiwi farms (seasonal), Dirang Monastery, and Kalachakra Monastery. Get transferred back to the hotel to spend the night.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer from Dirang to Tawang | Embrace the Himalayan Heights
activities: Check out from the hotel and get transferred to Tawang, located at an elevation of 10,000 ft. Along the journey, marvel at the stunning views of Sela Pass, adorned with snow-capped peaks and the pristine Sela Lake sparkling below. Visit the Jaswant Garh War Memorial to learn about the history of the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Continue your journey to Nuranang Falls and be amazed by the pristine waters and lush green surroundings. Later, get transferred to the hotel for check-in and relax for the day.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Tawang Local Sightseeing with Bum La Pass (optional) | Visit the biggest Buddhist Monastery in India
activities: Today is the day of local sightseeing in Tawan. Before this, you can opt for a short visit to Bum La Pass, the state's highest mountain pass. Continuing your journey, explore Tawang's famous Shonga-tser Lake or Madhuri Lake named after Madhuri Dixit. Also, visit Taktsang Gompa for its serene atmosphere. Lastly, proceed to Tawang Monastery, India's largest Buddhist monastery. After the sightseeing, get transferred back to your hotel and rest.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer from Tawang to Bomdila | Get the views of West Kameng Valley eloped in the clouds
activities: In the morning, check out and begin your drive to Bomdila. Upon arrival in Bomdila, check into the hotel and relax for a while before starting your visit to Gontse Rabgyaling Monastery (Upper Gonpa) and Thub-Chog Gatsel Ling Monastery (Lower Gonpa). After exploring the monasteries, get transferred back to the hotel. In the evening, you can take a short stroll around the town on your own to glimpse its unique culture and traditions.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Journey from Bomdila to Guwahati
activities: Check out from the hotel and embark on your journey to Guwahati. Experience a scenic drive through the diverse terrains of Arunachal Pradesh, passing charming towns and soaking in natural beauty. Upon reaching Guwahati, check into your hotel and enjoy the rest of the day at your leisure. You can explore some vibrant markets like Fancy Market and Paltan Market for shopping delights. Return to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Departure
activities: Check out from your hotel and get transferred to the Guwahati Airport or railway station for your journey back home. On the way, visit Kamakhya Temple, an important Hindu pilgrimage site where you can seek blessings from Goddess Kamakhya and get immersed in the peaceful experience of it.

faqs.question: What are the best things to do in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: Visit Namdapha National Park – Explore lush forests and spot rare wildlife like the red panda in this biodiversity hotspot.
Trek in Dirang – A scenic hill town ideal for trekking, hot springs, and learning about tribal cultures.
Watch the Sunset in Roing – Enjoy a serene sunset by the Dibang River surrounded by greenery.
Relax at Glow Lake – A secluded spot in Tezu surrounded by hills, perfect for nature lovers and couples.
Admire Nuranang Falls – Visit this spectacular 100-meter waterfall near Tawang for breathtaking views.
Drive to Sela Pass – A high-altitude mountain pass known for its sacred lake and stunning snow-covered scenery.
Raft on the Kameng River – Experience thrilling white-water rafting surrounded by untouched nature.
Trek to Talle Valley – Discover remote forest trails and interact with the Apatani tribe near Ziro.
Explore Upper Dibang Valley – Visit India’s largest district with lush valleys, gorges, and rivers.
Visit Ziro Valley – Known for the Ziro Music Festival, pine-clad hills, and unique tribal life.

faqs.question: What are the best adventure activities to do in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: River Rafting – On rivers like Brahmaputra, Subansiri, Siang, and Lohit.
Trekking and Hiking – Across pristine mountains, forests, and tribal villages.
Fishing and Angling – Popular in many river systems; great for peaceful nature experiences.
Bird Watching – With hotspots like Dirang, Sangti Valley, and Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary.

faqs.question: Which are the best places for river rafting in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: Brahmaputra River – Starts at Dibrugarh and offers Grade IV+ rapids through remote forests.
Subansiri River – Offers intense rapids and scenic tribal surroundings.
Siang River – Has both calm and challenging sections with amazing landscape views.
Lohit River – Known for Grade V rapids in some of the country’s remotest areas.

faqs.question: Which are the most adventurous places for trekking in Arunachal Pradesh?
answer: Talley Valley Trek – Lush forests and biodiversity make this a top trek.
Bailey Trail – Follows a historic route with views of the highest Himalayan peaks.
Ziro Trek – Great for nature walks, tribal interaction, and scenic views.
Mechuka Trek – A challenging, offbeat trek through valleys, rivers, and untouched nature.

faqs.question: Where can I enjoy kayaking in Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Kayaking is best experienced on the Brahmaputra River, offering scenic routes and calm to challenging water stretches for paddling.

faqs.question: Where can I enjoy paragliding in Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Tawang is the top spot for paragliding, providing panoramic views of snow-capped mountains, valleys, and monasteries.

faqs.question: Where can I go skiing in Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Head to Pankang Teng Tso Lake near Tawang during winter when the lake and surrounding areas turn into a snowy paradise ideal for skiing.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit is between October and April, when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing, adventure sports, and attending cultural festivals.

activities: Today, get driven for a city tour. Start with Sahastradhara, known for its stunning waterfalls, and visit the mysterious Robbers Cave. Next, visit the sacred Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple, creating a serene spiritual atmosphere. Conclude your city tour by admiring the Forest Research Institute, renowned for its grand colonial architecture and role in forestry research. Later, get transferred to Mussoorie. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Mussoorie Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, board your transfer for a city tour. Begin with the serene Kempty Falls, where cascading water amidst lush greenery creates a tranquil escape. Next, take a trip to Gun Hill for breathtaking views of the Himalayan range. Explore the beautiful Company Garden, then enjoy the bustling atmosphere of Mall Road with its vibrant shops. Then, visit Lal Tibba, and finally, take a scenic walk along Clouds End and Camels Back Road. Afterward, get driven to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Departure Day
activities: In the morning, check-out from your hotel and get driven to the Dehradun/Railway Station. Continue your journey forward, marking the end of this trip.

about_the_tour: Explore the enchanting land of Uttarakhand, a state that beautifully blends spirituality, adventure, and natural beauty. From the holy towns of Rishikesh, Haridwar, Kedarnath, and Badrinath, to the tranquil lakes of Nainital and the snowy slopes of Auli, this tour offers something for every kind of traveler.

Whether you’re looking to seek blessings at ancient temples, embark on Himalayan treks, or unwind at yoga retreats, Uttarakhand will mesmerize you at every step. Enjoy heart-pounding adventure sports like white-water rafting, bungee jumping, zip-lining, and skiing, or unwind in serene forest camps under the stars.

Spot wildlife at Jim Corbett National Park, walk across iconic suspension bridges in Rishikesh, or breathe in the crisp mountain air at Mussoorie. This tour offers the perfect mix of spiritual rejuvenation, natural serenity, and high-altitude adventure.
highlight: Explore the spiritual charm of Uttarakhand with visits to ancient temples, holy rivers, and sacred towns like Rishikesh, Haridwar, Badrinath, and Kedarnath.
Trek through stunning Himalayan trails, featuring snow-capped peaks, alpine meadows, and tranquil forests.
Witness the confluence of faith and nature at the origin points of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers.
Enjoy scenic camping experiences under the starlit skies in remote Himalayan settings.
Visit popular hill stations like Mussoorie, Nainital, and Auli, known for their lakes, colonial charm, and panoramic views.
Experience thrilling adventure activities such as river rafting, bungee jumping, zip-lining, and skiing (seasonal).
Discover the peaceful atmosphere of yoga and wellness retreats in the spiritual capital of Rishikesh.
Spot diverse flora and fauna in Jim Corbett National Park — India’s oldest national park and a haven for wildlife lovers.
Walk across hanging bridges, explore charming mountain villages, and enjoy warm local hospitality.
inclusions: Accommodation in clean and comfortable hotels/guesthouses/camps as per itinerary
Daily breakfast and dinner throughout the trip (or as specified)
Guided trek (if applicable) with experienced trek leaders
Transportation by private/shared vehicle for all intercity and local transfers
Permits and entry passes (e.g., Inner Line Permits)
Support staff for trek: porters/helpers (if included in itinerary)
Airport/railway station transfers (if mentioned)
All applicable taxes and service charges
exclusions: Meals not mentioned in the itinerary (e.g., lunch)
Personal expenses such as laundry, phone calls, tips, etc.
Entrance fees or camera charges at temples, parks, or sightseeing points
Cost of optional tours, adventure activities, or additional sightseeing
Any kind of emergency evacuation charges due to weather or health conditions
Anything not specifically mentioned in the “Inclusions” section
know_before_you_go: Valid government-issued ID is mandatory for all travelers. PAN Card is not accepted. Foreign nationals must carry a valid passport.
Weather in the mountains can change rapidly. Always carry warm clothing, even in summer.
Some areas exceed 2,500m+ altitude. If you have respiratory or heart conditions, consult your doctor before the trip.
Dress modestly in religious places. Carry layers for high-altitude or cold areas.
Internet and phone signals may be weak or absent in remote areas. Inform someone of your plans before you travel.
ATMs are limited in remote areas. Keep cash handy along with cards.
Carry comfortable, sturdy footwear, especially for treks and walks.
Travel insurance is highly recommended, especially for trekking or adventure packages.
Some areas like Valley of Flowers, Hemkund Sahib, or border regions may require special permits.
Vehicles are allotted based on group size and route type. AC may be turned off in hilly areas to preserve engine power.
In case of landslides, heavy snow, or political unrest, the itinerary may change for your safety.
Emergency evacuation (if required) will be chargeable to the traveler.
The operator reserves the right to alter or reschedule services based on local conditions.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Uttarakhand?
answer: Summer (March to June): Ideal for sightseeing, treks, and hill stations.
Winter (October to February): Perfect for snow lovers and skiing in Auli.
Monsoon (July to September): Lush greenery but risk of landslides in some areas.

faqs.question: Are religious destinations like Kedarnath and Badrinath included in the itinerary?
faqs.answer: These can be included on request as part of Char Dham Yatra or a separate spiritual itinerary. Access is seasonal and subject to weather.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation will be provided?
faqs.answer: Clean and comfortable hotels, guesthouses, or camps will be provided as per the itinerary. In remote trekking locations, accommodations may be more basic.

faqs.question: Are meals included in the tour?
faqs.answer: Yes, daily breakfast and dinner are included unless stated otherwise. Lunch is generally not included to allow flexibility during sightseeing.

faqs.question: What type of transportation will be provided?
faqs.answer: Transportation will be provided in a private or shared vehicle, depending on the group size and itinerary.

faqs.question: Is the tour suitable for kids and senior citizens?
faqs.answer: Yes, with itinerary customizations. However, high-altitude treks or remote areas might be challenging for very young children or seniors with health conditions.

faqs.question: Are adventure activities included in the package?
faqs.answer: No, but activities like rafting, bungee jumping, zip-lining, and skiing can be arranged at an extra cost depending on location and season.

faqs.question: Do I need permits for trekking or high-altitude areas?
faqs.answer: Yes, permits may be required for certain treks or protected regions. These are usually arranged by your tour operator.

faqs.question: Will mobile networks and internet work in all places?
faqs.answer: Network availability is good in major towns but may be limited or unavailable in remote or high-altitude areas.

faqs.question: Are there medical facilities en route?
faqs.answer: Basic medical facilities are available in towns, but limited in trekking zones. Carry a basic first-aid kit and any prescribed medications.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Transfer from Delhi to Haridwar | Haridwar Sightseeing
activities: Board your transfer from the meeting point in Delhi and begin your journey to Haridwar. Upon arrival in Haridwar, check into your hotel. Later, you will be driven to explore Haridwar. Visit its famous temples, including Chanda Devi Temple, Mansa Devi Temple, Daksheshwar Mahadev Temple, and Vaishno Devi Temple, a replica of the famous temple in Jammu. In the evening, experience the spiritual aura of the Ganga Aarti ritual at the renowned Har Ki Pauri ghat. Later, get driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Haridwar to Rishikesh | Rishikesh Sightseeing
activities: In the morning, check out from the hotel and get driven to Rishikesh. Upon arrival, check into your hotel. Later, you will be taken to Ram Jhula, where you can walk over the bridge and enjoy fantastic mountain views. Visit Shivanand Ashram, a hub for yoga and meditation, followed by Parmarth Niketan. Then, explore Geeta Bhawan, dedicated to Hindu religious studies and literature. End your day by witnessing the peaceful Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat before being driven back to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer from Rishikesh to Mussoorie | Mussoorie Sightseeing
activities: Today, you will check out from the hotel and then, be driven to Mussoorie, the Queen of Hill Stations. Upon arrival, check into your hotel. Later, visit the stunning Kempty Falls, where you can enjoy the refreshing waters and picturesque surroundings. Next, trek through the dense trees to Gun Hill, Mussoorie's second highest point, or take a cable car ride to the top to enjoy the panoramic views. Conclude your day with a visit to the bustling Mall Road before being driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer from Mussoorie to Dhanaulti | Dhanaulti Sightseeing
activities: In the morning, board your transfer to Dhanaulti. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and relax before starting your sightseeing tour. Start by visiting Eco Park, where you can indulge in thrilling activities such as sky walking, flying fox, and rock climbing. Next, explore Dhanaulti Adventure Park, offering more adventure opportunities. Finally, visit Sukhanda Devi Temple to seek blessings and enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding Himalayas before being driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Departure from Dhanaulti
activities: Bid adieu to the scenic town of Dhanaulti and board your transfer back to Delhi. Enjoy the scenic views along the way. Once you reach Delhi, the tour comes to an end.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Delhi | Transfer to Haridwar | Haridwar Sightseeing
activities: Begin your journey from Delhi to Haridwar, where spirituality meets the Himalayan backdrop. Enjoy the scenic 4-hour drive, and upon arrival in Haridwar, check in at your hotel. You will be driven for a sightseeing tour, paying your respects at Chanda Devi, Daksheshwar Mahadev, and other temples. In the evening, you can experience the charm of Har Ki Pauri Ghat, where the Ganga Aarti casts a spell with its sacred chants and shimmering diyas. Afterwards, return to the hotel for overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Transfer from Haridwar to Rishikesh | Day at leisure
activities: In the morning, board your transfer to Rishikesh, just a short 1-hour journey away. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and relax. Spend the day at your leisure, exploring the city on foot, taking in the serene riverside views, or indulging in yoga and meditation at local ashrams. In the evening, don't miss the mesmerizing Ganga Aarti ceremony at Triveni Ghat, where the rhythmic chants and flickering lamps create a peaceful ambiance. Afterward, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Rishikesh Sightseeing
activities: Get ready to embark on a full-day sightseeing tour of Rishikesh. Visit the city's iconic landmarks like Ram Jhula, the Beatles Ashram, and Neelkanth Temple. After spending the day exploring the sacred temple and other attractions, you will be driven to Shivpuri Adventure Zone where you can opt for various adventure activities (at your own cost). If time permits, you can also choose to witness the holy Ganga Aarti ceremony as the sun begins to set. Later, get transferred back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer from Rishikesh to Mussoorie via Dehradun
activities: Check out from the hotel and board the transfer for your journey to Mussoorie, with a stop in Dehradun along the way. In Dehradun, refresh your mind in the peaceful atmosphere of the Mindrolling Monastery or seek blessings at Shiv Mandir. You can explore the heart of Dehradun by visiting the iconic Clock Tower and enjoy shopping in the local markets. After exploring Dehradun, continue your journey to Mussoorie. Upon arrival, check-in at your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Mussoorie Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, get driven to the cascading Kempty Waterfalls, a popular tourist attraction and the first stop in your Mussoorie sightseeing tour. You can trek through the tall, dense trees to Gun Hill or take a cable car ride to the top, soaking in the panoramic views of the majestic Himalayas and the charming town of Mussoorie. You will also visit Lal Tibba, the highest peak in Mussoorie, the Company Garden and Camel's Back Road. Later, you will get transferred back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Departure from Mussoorie
activities: Post check-out from the hotel, you will bid farewell to the beautiful hill station in the Himalayas and begin your 6-hour journey back to Delhi. Upon arrival in Delhi, you will continue your journey back home on your own.
