testimonals.review: I booked a solo backpacking package for Spiti with Tripdekhoo and it was so affordable yet well managed. Shared cabs, community stays, and local food experiences made this trip authentic and budget-friendly. Every turn on the road was picture-worthy.

testimonals.name: Divyansh & Tara
testimonals.review: Yes, Spiti is remote, but Tripdekhoo managed to give us luxury wherever possible. Boutique camps in Chandratal, curated food at homestays, and private jeeps made it a blend of comfort and wild terrain. It was adventurous, but never rough.

testimonals.name: Ankita
testimonals.review: If you want to escape the noise of life, go to Spiti. Tripdekhoo planned a perfect route with no internet, limited calls, and lots of stars. I journaled, read books, and connected with nature. They even gave me a checklist of things to carry.

testimonals.name: Verma Family
testimonals.review: We were fascinated by Spiti’s Tibetan roots and Tripdekhoo ensured we explored that fully. Monastery tours, local meals with villagers, and visits to schools made our kids appreciate a new way of life. It was educational, adventurous, and deeply touching.

testimonals.name: Ritesh & Nandita
testimonals.review: We didn’t want a beach or city trip for our anniversary—Spiti was our surprise pick, and it was unforgettable. Tripdekhoo arranged a small celebration at our guesthouse in Kaza and even got us a cake! Sitting under the stars, wrapped in blankets, sipping tea—it was a simple yet unforgettable memory.

testimonals.name: Jatin & Colleagues
testimonals.review: We did a work-from-the-hills week followed by a trekking extension. Tripdekhoo arranged stable homestays with power backup and internet in Tabo and Kaza. After work hours, we explored nearby villages, and over the weekend we hiked to remote lakes.

testimonals.name: Priya
testimonals.review: I had seen Spiti in reels but the real thing was far beyond! The colors, the silence, and the kindness of locals—it hits you differently. Tripdekhoo created a safe, mindful itinerary with scenic stays and no hectic rush.

testimonals.name: Nakul & Ishita
testimonals.review: Many avoid Spiti in monsoon but it was green and serene in the valleys. Tripdekhoo gave us updates on road conditions, flexible plans, and helpful local guides. We avoided landslide-prone areas and still saw everything on our list.

testimonals.name: Manav
testimonals.review: As a student traveler, I had limited money but big dreams. Tripdekhoo gave me a shared-group tour, dorm-style stays, and a real taste of Spiti. It wasn’t luxurious, but it was honest and adventurous.

about_the_tour: Explore the enchanting land of Uttarakhand, a state that beautifully blends spirituality, adventure, and natural beauty. From the holy towns of Rishikesh, Haridwar, Kedarnath, and Badrinath, to the tranquil lakes of Nainital and the snowy slopes of Auli, this tour offers something for every kind of traveler.

Whether you’re looking to seek blessings at ancient temples, embark on Himalayan treks, or unwind at yoga retreats, Uttarakhand will mesmerize you at every step. Enjoy heart-pounding adventure sports like white-water rafting, bungee jumping, zip-lining, and skiing, or unwind in serene forest camps under the stars.

Spot wildlife at Jim Corbett National Park, walk across iconic suspension bridges in Rishikesh, or breathe in the crisp mountain air at Mussoorie. This tour offers the perfect mix of spiritual rejuvenation, natural serenity, and high-altitude adventure.
highlight: Explore the spiritual charm of Uttarakhand with visits to ancient temples, holy rivers, and sacred towns like Rishikesh, Haridwar, Badrinath, and Kedarnath.
Trek through stunning Himalayan trails, featuring snow-capped peaks, alpine meadows, and tranquil forests.
Witness the confluence of faith and nature at the origin points of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers.
Enjoy scenic camping experiences under the starlit skies in remote Himalayan settings.
Visit popular hill stations like Mussoorie, Nainital, and Auli, known for their lakes, colonial charm, and panoramic views.
Experience thrilling adventure activities such as river rafting, bungee jumping, zip-lining, and skiing (seasonal).
Discover the peaceful atmosphere of yoga and wellness retreats in the spiritual capital of Rishikesh.
Spot diverse flora and fauna in Jim Corbett National Park — India’s oldest national park and a haven for wildlife lovers.
Walk across hanging bridges, explore charming mountain villages, and enjoy warm local hospitality.

know_before_you_go: Valid government-issued ID is mandatory for all travelers. PAN Card is not accepted. Foreign nationals must carry a valid passport.
Weather in the mountains can change rapidly. Always carry warm clothing, even in summer.
Some areas exceed 2,500m+ altitude. If you have respiratory or heart conditions, consult your doctor before the trip.
Dress modestly in religious places. Carry layers for high-altitude or cold areas.
Internet and phone signals may be weak or absent in remote areas. Inform someone of your plans before you travel.
ATMs are limited in remote areas. Keep cash handy along with cards.
Carry comfortable, sturdy footwear, especially for treks and walks.
Travel insurance is highly recommended, especially for trekking or adventure packages.
Some areas like Valley of Flowers, Hemkund Sahib, or border regions may require special permits.
Vehicles are allotted based on group size and route type. AC may be turned off in hilly areas to preserve engine power.

Emergency evacuation (if required) will be chargeable to the traveler.
The operator reserves the right to alter or reschedule services based on local conditions.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Uttarakhand?
answer: Summer (March to June): Ideal for sightseeing, treks, and hill stations.
Winter (October to February): Perfect for snow lovers and skiing in Auli.
Monsoon (July to September): Lush greenery but risk of landslides in some areas.

faqs.question: Are religious destinations like Kedarnath and Badrinath included in the itinerary?
faqs.answer: These can be included on request as part of Char Dham Yatra or a separate spiritual itinerary. Access is seasonal and subject to weather.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation will be provided?
faqs.answer: Clean and comfortable hotels, guesthouses, or camps will be provided as per the itinerary. In remote trekking locations, accommodations may be more basic.

faqs.question: Are meals included in the tour?
faqs.answer: Yes, daily breakfast and dinner are included unless stated otherwise. Lunch is generally not included to allow flexibility during sightseeing.

faqs.question: What type of transportation will be provided?
faqs.answer: Transportation will be provided in a private or shared vehicle, depending on the group size and itinerary.

faqs.question: Is the tour suitable for kids and senior citizens?
faqs.answer: Yes, with itinerary customizations. However, high-altitude treks or remote areas might be challenging for very young children or seniors with health conditions.

faqs.question: Are adventure activities included in the package?
faqs.answer: No, but activities like rafting, bungee jumping, zip-lining, and skiing can be arranged at an extra cost depending on location and season.

faqs.question: Do I need permits for trekking or high-altitude areas?
faqs.answer: Yes, permits may be required for certain treks or protected regions. These are usually arranged by your tour operator.

faqs.question: Will mobile networks and internet work in all places?
faqs.answer: Network availability is good in major towns but may be limited or unavailable in remote or high-altitude areas.

faqs.question: Are there medical facilities en route?
faqs.answer: Basic medical facilities are available in towns, but limited in trekking zones. Carry a basic first-aid kit and any prescribed medications.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Nainital | Trip to Naina Devi Temple and Naini Lake
activities: Head to the pickup point in Delhi and board your transfer to Nainital. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel & then, get driven for city tour. Start by visiting the sacred Naina Devi Temple, believed to be the spot where the eyes of Goddess Sati fell. Then, see the serene Naini Lake, where you can enjoy a boat ride (at an extra cost). Later, explore the vibrant Mall Road, known for its local shops before being driven back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Nainital Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, get driven for Nainital sightseeing tour. Start with a visit to the Eco Cave Garden, where you can wander through a network of natural caves. Then, visit the Snow View Point to take in breathtaking panoramic views of the snow-clad peaks. Continue to other scenic spots like Tiffin Top, also known as Dorothy's Seat and Lovers Point, a spot known for its romantic views of the Naini lake.Afterward, you’ll be driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Kausani | Kausani Sightseeing Tour
activities: Post check-out, get driven to Kausani, often referred to as the “Switzerland of India”. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and relax for a while. Later, you'll be driven for a city tour, starting with the Anasakti Ashram, a retreat once visited by Mahatma Gandhi. Next, marvel at the natural beauty of Rudradhari Falls, nestled amidst lush forests and wrap up your day with a visit to the Kausani Tea Estate, where you can stroll through lush plantations. Later, get driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Joshimath
activities: In the morning, check out and get transferred to Joshimath, a quaint hill town nestled in the Garhwal Himalayas. En route, enjoy the stunning views of snow-capped peaks, winding mountain roads and charming villages dotting the landscape. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and unwind amidst the scenic views.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Excursion to Auli
activities: Today, get driven to the Joshimath-Auli Ropeway Lower Station, where you’ll board the Chair Lift (tickets not included) for an unforgettable ride to Auli. Enjoy stunning views of snow-clad peaks and lush landscapes as you ascend. Once you arrive at the Joshimath-Auli Ropeway Upper Terminal, visit the Auli Artificial Lake, one of the world’s highest man-made lakes & take a peaceful walk along its picturesque shores. Later, ride the chair lift back to Joshimath. Then, get driven to your hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Transfer to Rishikesh | Day at Leisure
activities: Post check-out, get driven to Rishikesh, famously known as the `Yoga Capital of the World.` Enjoy picturesque views of lush hills and winding rivers during the journey. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and relax for the day. In the evening, you can head to the Triveni Ghat & witness the Ganga Aarti by the sacred river. If time permits, you can explore other attractions like the iconic Lakshman Jhula or the Beatles Ashram.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Transfer to Delhi | Departure Day
activities: Check out from your hotel & get driven back to Delhi, enjoying scenic views along the way. Upon arrival at Majnu Ka Tilla or Kashmere Gate, bid farewell to your memorable trip as you continue your journey back home.

about_the_tour: Goa, located on the western coast of India, is a popular destination known for its unique blend of Indian and Portuguese cultures, scenic beaches, vibrant nightlife, and relaxed lifestyle. Despite being one of India’s smallest states, it attracts visitors from around the world thanks to its rich heritage, diverse attractions, and laid-back charm.The state features a long coastline dotted with a variety of beaches that cater to all kinds of travelers—from quiet, serene spots to lively, party-centric shores. Its cuisine, especially seafood, is a major draw, as are its numerous restaurants, beach shacks, bars, and nightclubs.Goa’s colonial history is reflected in its architecture, with old churches, forts, and traditional houses that add to its cultural appeal. Whether you’re looking for relaxation, adventure, history, or entertainment, Goa offers something for everyone.
how_to_reach: By Air: Goa’s main airport, Manohar International Airport (Mopa) in North Goa and Dabolim Airport in South Goa, are well-connected to major cities across India like Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, and Hyderabad. Regular domestic and limited international flights make air travel the fastest way to reach Goa.

By Rail: Goa has two major railway stations — Madgaon (Margao) in South Goa and Vasco-da-Gama. They are connected to most Indian cities via Konkan Railway routes, offering scenic coastal and Western Ghats views during the journey.

By Road: Goa is accessible by well-maintained highways. State-run and private buses connect it to nearby states like Maharashtra and Karnataka. Self-drive trips from Mumbai, Pune, or Bangalore via NH66 and NH748 are also popular among travelers.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Goa?
faqs.answer: The ideal time to visit Goa is from November to February when the weather is pleasant and perfect for beaches and sightseeing. Avoid the monsoon season (June to September) unless you're seeking off-season solitude and discounts.

faqs.question: Is Goa safe for solo travelers and families?
faqs.answer: Yes, Goa is generally safe for solo travelers, couples, and families. Like any tourist destination, exercise standard precautions—avoid isolated beaches at night and keep your belongings secure.

faqs.question: What are the top things to do in Goa?
answer: Beach hopping (Baga, Calangute, Palolem, Anjuna)
Exploring forts (Aguada, Chapora)
Water sports (jet skiing, parasailing, banana boat rides)
Visiting churches and temples
Enjoying vibrant nightlife and beach parties
Shopping at flea markets (Anjuna, Mapusa)

faqs.question: What kind of cuisine can I expect in Goa?
faqs.answer: Goa offers a mix of seafood-rich Goan cuisine, Indian, and international dishes. Must-tries include prawn curry, xacuti, vindaloo, and bebinca (dessert). Beach shacks and cafés serve everything from local thalis to continental platters.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit to visit Goa?
faqs.answer: No permits are required for Indian or foreign tourists to visit Goa. Just carry a valid government-issued ID (passport, Aadhaar, driving license). PAN cards are not accepted as valid ID proof.

faqs.question: What are the popular ways to get around in Goa?
faqs.answer: You can rent scooters, motorbikes, or cars (must carry valid license), use taxis or auto-rickshaws, or book private cabs or guided tours. Self-drive options are popular and economical for beach-hopping and local exploration.

faqs.question: Are there any dress code restrictions in Goa?
faqs.answer: Goa is liberal and tourist-friendly. Beachwear is fine on beaches, but modest attire is recommended when visiting churches, temples, and local markets.

faqs.question: What should I carry while visiting Goa?
answer: Light cotton clothes & swimwear
Sunscreen (SPF 40+), sunglasses, hat/cap
Comfortable shoes or flip-flops
Valid ID proof
Power bank, reusable water bottle, basic medicines

faqs.question: Is alcohol permitted in Goa?
faqs.answer: Yes, alcohol is legal and widely available in Goa. You must be 18 years or older to purchase or consume alcohol. Be mindful of drinking in public places or beaches, as it’s discouraged and sometimes penalized.

faqs.question: Are there ATMs and mobile networks available throughout Goa?
faqs.answer: Yes, major towns and tourist areas have plenty of ATMs, though rural areas may have limited access. All major mobile networks work well in Goa, though some beach and remote areas may have weak signals.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 – Arrival in Goa | Leisure Day
activities: Welcome to Goa! Upon your arrival at the airport or railway station, you will be greeted by our representative and transferred to your hotel for check-in. Spend the rest of the day at leisure—explore the nearby beaches, soak in the laid-back vibe, or simply relax at the hotel. Overnight stay in Goa.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 – North Goa Sightseeing Tour
activities: After breakfast, embark on a full-day sightseeing tour of North Goa. Begin with the historic Aguada Fort, offering panoramic views of the Arabian Sea. Visit Sinquerim Beach and Candolim Beach before heading to the vibrant Calangute Beach, known for its water sports and lively atmosphere. Continue to Baga Beach, famous for nightlife and the bustling Tito’s Lane, and then explore the happening Anjuna Beach. End the day at Vagator Beach, framed by the scenic Chapora Fort. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Goa.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 – South Goa Sightseeing Tour
activities: Enjoy breakfast and set out for a South Goa sightseeing tour. Start with a visit to Shri Manguesh Temple, followed by the UNESCO-listed Basilica of Bom Jesus and the grand Se Cathedral in Old Goa. Stroll along Miramar Beach, then visit the picturesque Dona Paula Beach, where the Mandovi and Zuari rivers meet. In the evening, shop for souvenirs at the Panjim flea market before returning to your hotel for an overnight stay in Goa.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 – Departure from Goa
activities: After breakfast, complete the check-out formalities and transfer to the airport or railway station for your onward journey, taking with you beautiful memories of your Goa getaway.

about_the_tour: Explore the pristine beauty of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, a tropical paradise nestled in the Bay of Bengal. This tour offers a perfect blend of white-sand beaches, crystal-clear turquoise waters, rich marine biodiversity, and colonial-era history, making it ideal for honeymooners, families, nature lovers, and adventure seekers.The journey takes you through the top attractions of the islands—Port Blair, Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep), Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep), and more. Witness the famed Radhanagar Beach, known as one of Asia’s most beautiful beaches, enjoy water sports at Elephant Beach, and delve into history with a visit to the Cellular Jail. The itinerary balances relaxation, exploration, and activities like snorkeling, scuba diving, and glass-bottom boating.With seamless inter-island transfers, cozy beachfront accommodations, daily breakfast, and guided sightseeing, the Andaman tour ensures a smooth and rejuvenating escape from the mainland hustle
how_to_reach: By Air (Recommended): The quickest and most convenient way to reach the Andaman Islands is by air. Veer Savarkar Airport (Port Blair Airport) is the main airport in the islands.
Flights from Major Indian Cities:
Delhi → Port Blair: Approx. 4–5 hours direct flight
Mumbai → Port Blair: Approx. 4.5–5 hours direct flight
Chennai → Port Blair: Approx. 2.5–3 hours direct flight
Kolkata → Port Blair: Approx. 2.5–3 hours direct flight
Airlines operating: IndiGo, Air India, SpiceJet, GoAir
By Sea: Although slower, traveling by ship can be an adventurous option. Neil, Havelock, and other islands are accessible via sea from Port Blair.
Ships from Chennai, Kolkata, or Visakhapatnam: Passenger ships operate once or twice a week.
Travel time by ship: Approximately 3–4 days depending on port of departure.
Inter-island ferries: Regular ferries connect Port Blair to Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), Neil (Shaheed Dweep), and other islands.
Ferry durations: Port Blair → Havelock: 1.5–3 hours, Port Blair → Neil: 1–2 hours.
How to Reach Individual Islands: Most tourists fly into Port Blair first, then take a ferry or private boat.
Havelock Island is the most popular for beaches and water activities, reachable by ferry from Port Blair.
Tip: Flights are recommended for a time-efficient trip, while ferries offer scenic views of the Bay of Bengal.

packages.fagHeading: Basic FAQ for Andaman and Nicobar Tour

faq.question: What is the best time to visit the Andaman Islands?
faq.answer: The best time to visit is between October and May, when the weather is pleasant, ideal for sightseeing, beach hopping, and water sports. The monsoon season (June–August) may bring heavy rains, but the islands remain lush and beautiful.

faq.question: Do I need a visa or any permit to visit Andaman?
faq.answer: Indian Nationals do not need any visa or special permit to visit most islands. Foreign Nationals need a valid Indian visa and must obtain a Restricted Area Permit (RAP), usually available upon arrival at the airport or harbor.

faq.question: Are there direct flights to the Andaman Islands?
faq.answer: Yes. Port Blair (Veer Savarkar International Airport) is the main airport, well-connected with direct flights from cities like Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Bangalore.

faq.question: What kind of accommodations are available?
faq.answer: Andaman offers a range of accommodations – from budget hotels to luxury resorts and beachfront cottages – mainly in Port Blair, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), and Neil Island.

faq.question: What water sports can I enjoy in Andaman?
faq.answer: You can enjoy snorkeling, scuba diving, jet skiing, sea walking, kayaking, and glass-bottom boat rides, especially at Elephant Beach, North Bay, and Havelock Island.

faq.question: Are ferries and cruises included in the tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Inter-island travel is typically arranged by government ferries or private cruises based on availability. Private cruises are subject to availability and may be substituted with ferries if necessary.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel in Andaman?
faq.answer: Yes, Andaman is very safe for tourists, including solo travelers and families. However, it’s advisable to follow safety instructions during water activities and respect local guidelines.

faq.question: Is internet connectivity good in Andaman?
faq.answer: Internet and mobile connectivity can be spotty, especially on Neil and Havelock Islands. BSNL and Airtel tend to work better, but speed and signal may vary.

faq.question: What should I pack for the trip?
faq.answer: Carry light cotton clothes, swimwear, sunscreen, insect repellent, power banks, and a raincoat (if visiting during the monsoon). Don’t forget your government-approved ID.

faq.question: Are COVID-19 guidelines still applicable?
faq.answer: Yes, travelers are expected to follow local COVID-19 regulations, including wearing masks, sanitizing hands, and maintaining social distancing, as per government advisories.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival in Port Blair | Begin your tropical island adventure
activities: Welcome to the Andaman Islands! Upon arrival at Port Blair Airport, you will be greeted by our representative and transferred to your hotel for check-in. Spend the day at leisure exploring the surroundings or relaxing at your hotel. In the evening, enjoy a visit to Cellular Jail, followed by the Light & Sound Show, where the history of the freedom struggle comes alive. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Port Blair.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Havelock Island | Relax on the pristine sands of Radhanagar Beach
activities: After breakfast, board the ferry to Havelock Island. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and get ready to explore the island. Spend the day at the famous Radhanagar Beach, renowned for its white sands and turquoise waters. You can indulge in beach activities or simply relax and soak in the scenic beauty. Optional water sports and snorkeling activities are also available. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Havelock.

itinerary.day: Day 3 – Havelock & Elephant Beach Excursion | Adventure and underwater fun
activities: Wake up to a tropical morning and have breakfast. Proceed to Elephant Beach, known for its coral reefs and vibrant marine life. Enjoy snorkeling, swimming, or just relaxing on the pristine sands. Later, explore local markets and enjoy the island ambiance. In the evening, return to your hotel in Havelock for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 – Departure | Return with memories of paradise
activities: After breakfast, check out from your hotel and take the ferry back to Port Blair. Depending on your flight schedule, you may visit Chidiya Tapu for bird watching and a stunning sunset. Finally, transfer to Port Blair Airport for your onward journey, carrying with you the unforgettable memories of the Andaman Islands.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival in Port Blair | Visit to Corbyns Cove Beach & Cellular Jail
activities: Welcome to Port Blair! Upon arriving at the airport, get transferred to the hotel. After you relax for some time, board the transfer for a sightseeing tour of Port Blair. Begin the journey by exploring Corbyns Cove Beach, a spot ideal for relaxation and water sports. Also, you can relax on its shores and admire the scenic surroundings. Following that, visit Cellular Jail, showcasing the struggles of Indian freedom fighters. Later, get driven back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Transfer to Havelock | Visit to Radhanagar Beach
activities: After you check out from the hotel, get driven to Phoenix Bay Harbour for a ferry ride to Havelock Island. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel. Later, you'll be driven to Radhanagr Beach, famous for its stunning views and serene atmosphere. While you are there, you can enjoy swimming or simply sun bathe around its beautiful shores. After spending a wonderful day, board the transfer back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 3 – Leisure Day at Havelock Island
activities: Make the most of your day on the stunning Havelock Island at your own pace. Visit the picturesque Elephant Beach, a top destination for underwater adventures. Dive into thrilling water sports like snorkelling and surfing, or simply unwind on the beach. Alternatively, explore Vijaynagar Beach, where you can swim in its tranquil waters and enjoy the serene views of the surrounding landscape. After a day of exploration and relaxation, return to your hotel at your leisure for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 – Kalapathar Beach Tour | Transfer to Port Blair
activities: In the morning, get ready for a visit to Kalapathar Beach, renowned for its striking black rocks and beautiful sunrise views over the Indian Ocean. Enjoy a peaceful walk along the shore, creating a stunning contrast against the dark rocks and turquoise waters. After that, return to the hotel to check out and then get transferred to Havelock Jetty to board the ferry to Port Blair. Upon arrival, get driven to the hotel and check in for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 5 – Departure Day
activities: After you check out from your hotel, you will be transferred to the airport for your flight back home. This marks the end of your trip.

packages.fagHeading: Basic FAQ for Andaman and Nicobar Tour

faq.question: What is the best time to visit the Andaman Islands?
faq.answer: The best time to visit is between October and May, when the weather is pleasant, ideal for sightseeing, beach hopping, and water sports. The monsoon season (June–August) may bring heavy rains, but the islands remain lush and beautiful.

faq.question: Do I need a visa or any permit to visit Andaman?
faq.answer: Indian Nationals do not need any visa or special permit to visit most islands. Foreign Nationals need a valid Indian visa and must obtain a Restricted Area Permit (RAP), usually available upon arrival at the airport or harbor.

faq.question: Are there direct flights to the Andaman Islands?
faq.answer: Yes. Port Blair (Veer Savarkar International Airport) is the main airport, well-connected with direct flights from cities like Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Bangalore.

faq.question: What kind of accommodations are available?
faq.answer: Andaman offers a range of accommodations – from budget hotels to luxury resorts and beachfront cottages – mainly in Port Blair, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), and Neil Island.

faq.question: What water sports can I enjoy in Andaman?
faq.answer: You can enjoy snorkeling, scuba diving, jet skiing, sea walking, kayaking, and glass-bottom boat rides, especially at Elephant Beach, North Bay, and Havelock Island.

faq.question: Are ferries and cruises included in the tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Inter-island travel is typically arranged by government ferries or private cruises based on availability. Private cruises are subject to availability and may be substituted with ferries if necessary.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel in Andaman?
faq.answer: Yes, Andaman is very safe for tourists, including solo travelers and families. However, it’s advisable to follow safety instructions during water activities and respect local guidelines.

faq.question: Is internet connectivity good in Andaman?
faq.answer: Internet and mobile connectivity can be spotty, especially on Neil and Havelock Islands. BSNL and Airtel tend to work better, but speed and signal may vary.

faq.question: What should I pack for the trip?
faq.answer: Carry light cotton clothes, swimwear, sunscreen, insect repellent, power banks, and a raincoat (if visiting during the monsoon). Don’t forget your government-approved ID.

faq.question: Are COVID-19 guidelines still applicable?
faq.answer: Yes, travelers are expected to follow local COVID-19 regulations, including wearing masks, sanitizing hands, and maintaining social distancing, as per government advisories.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival in Port Blair | Trip to Corbyn Cove Beach and Cellular Jail
activities: Welcome to Andaman! Upon arrival at the airport, get transferred to your hotel. Once you have checked in, take some time to relax. Later, get driven to Corbyn Cove Beach, where you can enjoy stunning ocean views and the peaceful environment. Then, experience the rich history of the Cellular Jail through an engaging light and sound show. After the show, board your transfer back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Transfer to Havelock Island | Radhanagar Beach Tour
activities: Post check out, get transferred to Phoenix Bay Harbour. Next, board your ferry to the picturesque Havelock Island. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and take some time to settle in. Later, get driven to the renowned Radhanagar Beach, famous for its pristine white sands and turquoise waters. Spend the afternoon basking in the sun and enjoying the serene beach environment. Afterward, return to your hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 3 – Visit to Elephant Beach
activities: In the morning, get transferred for a captivating day trip to the Elephant Beach. Upon arrival, take your time to explore the vibrant underwater world at Neemo Reef with a range of water sports available (additional cost). Enjoy the stunning coastal views and the crystal-clear waters that make this beach a tropical paradise. After a day filled with adventure and relaxation, get driven to your hotel for a relaxing overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 – Visit to Kalapathar Beach | Transfer to Neil Island
activities: Today, check out from your hotel and get transferred to the serene Kalapathar Beach. There, you can enjoy a leisurely stroll along the pristine shoreline and take in the breathtaking natural beauty. After soaking in the serene atmosphere, get driven to the Havelock Island Harbour for your ferry ride to Neil Island. Upon arrival, you'll be transferred to your hotel. Check in and rest for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 5 – Neil Island Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Port Blair
activities: Post check out, you’ll get transferred to explore Neil Island. Visit the picturesque Laxmanpur Beach, the serene Sitapur Beach, and the vibrant Bharatpur Beach. There, you can also indulge in various water sports and activities. Following your island exploration, get driven to Neil Island Jetty and board your ferry to Port Blair. Upon arrival, get transferred to your hotel. Check in and rest for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 6 – Departure Day
activities: After checking out from your hotel, you will be driven to Veer Savarkar International Airport for your flight back home. This marks the end of your trip.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival in Port Blair | Port Blair Sightseeing Tour
activities: Welcome to Andaman, the Garden of Eden! Upon arrival at the airport, you'll be transferred to your hotel. Check in and relax for a while. Then, you'll be transferred to Corbyn Cove Beach, renowned for its stunning coastal views and scenic atmosphere. Next, explore the historical Cellular Jail, where you'll experience a captivating light and sound show depicting the struggles of Indian freedom fighters. Later, you'll be driven back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Transfer to Havelock Island | Radhanagar Beach Tour
activities: After checking out, you'll be transferred to Phoenix Bay Harbour for your ferry ride to Havelock Island. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel and relax for a while. Then, start your exploration by getting driven to Radhanagar Beach, renowned for its pristine waters and powdery white sands. This stunning beach is perfect for swimming and sunbathing. After a day of relaxation and exploration, you'll be transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 3 – Excursion to Elephant Beach
activities: Start your day with a transfer to the jetty point, where you’ll board a speedboat for a thrilling ride to Elephant Beach. Upon arrival, you can take part in water sports at Neemo Reef, where vibrant marine life awaits (at additional cost). On Elephant Beach, enjoy a serene walk along the pristine sandy shores and take in the breathtaking ocean views. Later, return to the jetty point by speedboat and you'll be driven to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 – Excursion to Kalapathar Beach | Transfer to Neil Island
activities: In the morning, you will be driven to Kalapathar Beach, known for its stunning white sands and turquoise waters. Take time to stroll along the shore and soak in the vibrant scenery. Afterward, you will be transferred to the hotel for check-out. Next, transfer to the jetty point on Havelock Island Harbour for a scenic ferry ride to Neil Island Port. Upon arrival, you will be driven to your hotel on Neil Island, where you can relax and enjoy an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 5 – Transfer to Port Blair | Enroute sightseeing in Neil Island
activities: After checking out, board your transfer to Port Blair. En route, make a stop at Neil Island. You can enjoy the natural beauty of Laxmanpur Beach, known for its scenic beauty and coral formations. Continue to Sitapur Beach, where golden sands and serene waters await. Visit Bharatpur Beach, perfect for snorkeling and other water activities. You can opt for water sports (at your own cost). Later, continue to Port Blair. Check in at your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 6 – Ross and North Bay Island Tour
activities: Begin your day with a ferry ride to the stunning Ross and North Bay Islands. At North Bay Island, you can enjoy a range of water activities, including snorkeling, glass-bottom boat rides, and scuba diving, to discover the underwater world. Continue your adventure on Ross Island, where you can explore the intriguing ruins of the Penal Colony. After a full day of excitement and exploration, you'll be transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 7 – Departure Day
activities: After checking out, you will be driven to Veer Savarkar International Airport for your onward journey. This marks the end of your trip.

itinerary.day: Day 1 Arrival at Jaipur | Half-Day Jaipur Sightseeing Tour
activities: Welcome to Jaipur! Upon arrival, you'll be taken to visit the City Palace, a stunning blend of Mughal and Rajput architecture. Continue to Jantar Mantar, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to the world’s largest sundial & marvel at the intricate latticework windows of the Hawa Mahal. Later, pay your respects at the Govind Dev Ji Temple and head to Tripolia Bazar and Johari Bazaar, renowned for their traditional handicrafts and jewelry. After an amazing time, get driven to your hotel & check-in.

itinerary.day: Day 2 Jaipur Forts Tour with Jal Mahal & Birla Mandir
activities: Today, explore Jaipur on a sightseeing tour and visit Nahargarh Fort, perched on the Aravalli Hills, offering panoramic views of the city. Continue to Jaigarh Fort, home to the world’s largest cannon on wheels, Jaivana, a symbol of Rajput strength. Next, step into the grand Amer Fort & marvel at the beauty of Sheesh Mahal’s magical mirror work. Also, visit the Jal Mahal, a stunning palace floating on the Man Sagar Lake and conclude with a visit to the Birla Temple, a masterpiece of white marble.

itinerary.day: Day 3 Transfer to Pushkar | En Route Ajmer Sightseeing Tour | Half-Day Pushkar Sightseeing Tour
activities: Post-checkout, get driven to Pushkar. En route, make a stop at Ajmer and visit the Ajmer Sharif Dargah, home to the tomb of Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. Next, visit Adhai-Din-Ka Jhonpra, one of India’s oldest surviving Islamic structures and visit the scenic Ana Sagar Lake. Later, upon reaching Pushkar, check in and relax. Afterwards, get driven to visit the Brahma Temple, one of the rare temples dedicated to Lord Brahma. Also, stroll along Pushkar Lake and explore the local markets.

itinerary.day: Day 4 Departure Day
activities: In the morning, get ready and check-out from your hotel in Pushkar. Then, board your transfer and get driven to Jaipur for your journey back home, marking the end to your amazing journey in Rajasthan.

itinerary.day: Day 1 Arrival in Udaipur | Udaipur Sightseeing Tour
activities: Welcome to Udaipur! Upon arriving at Udaipur, you'll be transferred to the hotel for check-in. After you relax for some time, board the transfer for the sightseeing tour of the city. During this day trip, enjoy a walk through the Sahelio-ki-Bari and take-in the beauty of the Fateh Sagar Lake, which looks scenic in the monsoon season. Also, explore Under the Sun Aquarium, home to various exotic marine species. Later, get transferred back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 Visit to City Palace | Day at Leisure
activities: Prepare yourself for an amazing experience and get transferred to the stunning City Palace, set on the scenic banks of Lake Pichola. Explore the Crystal Gallery within the palace and marvel at its stunning collection of crystal artifacts. Later, get transferred back to the hotel. Afterward, you can make time to see some other attractions in the city at your own pace, like Jagdish Temple and Bagore ki Haveli, among other famous spots. Later, return to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 3 Excursion to Kumbhalgarh
activities: Enjoy a wonderful day trip from Udaipur as you get transferred from the hotel to Kumbhalgarh. Upon arriving, explore the ancient temples and the grand Badal Mahal palace. While you are there, also admire the stunning views from Kumbhalgarh Fort's expansive walls, second-longest continuous wall in the world. After an amazing day of exploration, board the transfer back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 Day Trip to Chittorgarh
activities: Get ready to explore the historical Chittorgarh Fort on an amazing excursion. Board the transfer from the hotel to Chittorgarh. Upon arriving, pass through seven grand gates along a scenic road to reach the fort. Afterwards, climb upstairs to see the Vijay Stambh, adorned with Arabic engravings and admire the grandeur of the beautiful Padmini Palace. After a memorable day, you'll get transferred back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 5 Departure Day
activities: As your memorable vacation in Udaipur Airport/Railway Station comes to a close, you'll get transferred from your hotel to Udaipur to board the transfer back home.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival in Jaipur | Welcome to the ‘Pink City’
activities: Upon arrival in Jaipur, meet a representative who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. After check-in and some relaxation, head out to explore the city. Begin with a quick stop at the Hawa Mahal, followed by a visit to the Jantar Mantar observatory and the City Palace & Museum, home to royal artifacts. In the evening, seek blessings at Govind Dev Ji Temple and enjoy the vibrant local market before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Jaipur Sightseeing | Explore the Majestic Forts
activities: After breakfast, set out for a full day of sightseeing. Visit the grand Amer Fort, famous for its Sheesh Mahal, followed by the Jaigarh Fort, which houses one of the largest cannons. Continue to Nahargarh Fort for stunning city views, and take a photogenic stop at Jal Mahal. Later, visit the beautiful Birla Temple, built in white marble, before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay in Jaipur.

itinerary.day: Day 3 – Jaipur to Jodhpur | The Blue City’s Marvels
activities: Post breakfast, check out and drive towards Jodhpur. On arrival, check in to your hotel and relax for a while. Later, visit the towering Mehrangarh Fort, one of the most magnificent forts in India, and the marble memorial of Jaswant Thada, often called the “Taj Mahal of Marwar.” In the evening, explore the lively Ghanta Ghar market before returning to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 – Jodhpur to Jaisalmer | Enter the Golden City
activities: After breakfast, begin your journey towards Jaisalmer, the “Golden City of Rajasthan.” En route, stop at the Jaisalmer War Memorial to learn about the valor of Indian soldiers. Upon reaching Jaisalmer, check in to your hotel and rest for a while. Later, visit the Jaisalmer Fort, a living fort where locals still reside and markets thrive. Spend some time exploring the vibrant streets and leather shops before returning for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 5 – Jaisalmer Sightseeing & Desert Adventure
activities: After breakfast, start with a peaceful walk at Gadisar Lake, followed by visits to the intricately designed Patwon Ki Haveli, Nathmal Ki Haveli, and Salim Singh Ki Haveli. In the afternoon, head towards the Sam Sand Dunes, where the desert experience begins. Enjoy dune bashing, a camel ride, and witness the sunset over the golden sands. In the evening, indulge in folk performances, a bonfire, and a traditional Rajasthani dinner at your desert camp, where you’ll spend the night.

itinerary.day: Day 6 – Departure from Jodhpur | Memories of Rajasthan
activities: After breakfast, check out from the desert camp and proceed towards Jodhpur Airport/Railway Station for your onward journey. This marks the end of your royal Rajasthan adventure with memories of forts, palaces, deserts, and vibrant culture.

itinerary.day: Day 1 Arrival in Jaipur | Half-Day Sightseeing Tour
activities: Welcome to Jaipur! Upon arrival, explore City Palace, still home to Jaipur’s royal family. Explore Jantar Mantar, an astronomical marvel featuring the world’s largest stone sundial. Next, visit the Hawa Mahal, known for its stunning latticework windows. Visit the sacred Govind Dev Ji Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna. Later, explore Tripolia & Johari Bazaars, where you can shop for handicrafts, Bandhej sarees, & Mojaris. You can also try Dahi Vade at LMB before checking into your hotel.

itinerary.day: Day 2 Jaipur Forts Tour with Jal Mahal & Birla Mandir
activities: Today, begin your tour at Nahargarh Fort & enjoy panoramic views of the city & the Aravalli Hills. Then, visit Amer Fort, known for its Sheesh Mahal, where thousands of mirrors create a magical effect. Continue to Jaigarh Fort, housing world's largest cannon on wheels. Stop at Panna Meena ka Kund, a place worthy to be on your Instagram feed. Next, visit Jal Mahal & Birla Mandir before getting driven to the hotel. In the evening, visit Chokhi Dhani & enjoy Rajasthani cuisine & folk performances.

itinerary.day: Day 3 Transfer to Udaipur via Nathdwara | Udaipur Sightseeing Tour
activities: After checking out of your hotel & get driven to Udaipur. En route make a stop at Nathdwara & visit Shri Nath Ji temple, famous for its 12th-century idol of Krishna. Upon arrival, get driven to the hotel & check in. Later, visit Lake Pichola, where you can enjoy a scenic boat ride. Explore the nearby local cafes at Ambrai Ghat and enjoy the traditional dance and music of Rajasthan at the Bagore ki haveli. Spend some peaceful time at Gangaur Ghat.

itinerary.day: Day 4 Visit to City Palace | Trip to Rayta Hills
activities: Start your day with a visit to the City Palace, known for its stunning Crystal Gallery and impressive sculpture collection. Next, visit the peaceful Ubeshwar Ji Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Drive to the Rayta Hills, enjoying breathtaking views of the lush green Aravalli Hills. Afterward, return to the city and visit the Maharana Pratap Smarak, which honors a great warrior. Then visit Fateh Sagar Lake, where you can enjoy a relaxing boat ride & savor delicious treats at the nearby Chopati.

itinerary.day: Day 5 Transfer to Jodhpur | En route Sightseeing Tour
activities: Check out and get driven to Jodhpur. En route, visit Ranakpur Temple, famous for its intricate marble design. Next stop at Om Banna Temple, where you can offer alcohol to Bullet Baba for blessings. Continue your journey to Jodhpur, and upon arrival, check in to your hotel. Later, visit Mehrangarh Fort, which offers panoramic views of the blue city. Stroll through Navchowkiya to immerse yourself in the charm of Jodhpur. Before wrapping up the day, be sure to savor the city's famous mirchi vada.

itinerary.day: Day 6 Visit to Umaid Bhawan Palace | Transfer to Jaisalmer
activities: Check out of your hotel, & get driven to Umaid Bhawan Palace, one of the largest private residences. Afterward, get driven to Jaisalmer. En route, visit The Date Farm, also known as Mini Dubai, home to over 15,000 dates. Upon arrival in Jaisalmer, check into your hotel & relax for a while. In the evening, get driven to Gadisar Lake, a manmade lake surrounded by temples & ghats. Here, you can enjoy a boat ride and soak in the golden hues of Jaisalmer's skyline. Later, get driven to the hotel.

itinerary.day: Day 7 Jaisalmer Sightseeing Tour | Desert Camping & Adventure Activities
activities: Check out and visit the iconic Jaisalmer Fort, a vibrant 'living fort' where residents still live. Next, visit Patwon Ki Haveli, Nathmal Ki Haveli, and Salim Singh Ki Haveli, a perfect spot to capture Instaworthy pictures. Explore the ghost village of Khuldhara and uncover the mystery behind the villagers' sudden disappearance. Later, get driven to your camp. Upon arrival, enjoy a warm Rajasthani welcome. Enjoy a camel ride, Jeep safari, & watch Rajasthani folk performances.

itinerary.day: Day 8 Transfer to Jodhpur | En route Sightseeing | Departure Day
activities: After checking out of your hotel, get transferred to Jodhpur. En route, stop at the Jaisalmer War Memorial, a tribute to the Indian Soldiers, where you can view war trophies and vintage military vehicles. Next, explore the impressive Bhadariya Library, Asia's largest underground library, housing over 900,000 books and ancient manuscripts. Later, get driven to Jodhpur. Upon arrival, get driven to Jodhpur Airport/Railway Station to continue your onward journey.

about_the_tour: Explore the raw beauty and rugged charm of Spiti Valley, a high-altitude desert nestled deep within the Himalayas of Himachal Pradesh. Often called “Little Tibet” for its stark landscapes and ancient monasteries, Spiti is a paradise for travelers seeking solitude, spiritual experiences, and thrilling adventures.

This tour takes you on a soul-stirring journey through winding mountain roads, centuries-old gompas, crystal-clear rivers, and charming villages that seem untouched by time. Visit iconic destinations like Kaza, Key Monastery, Hikkim (home to the world's highest post office), Komic (one of the world’s highest villages), and the surreal Chandratal Lake.
Perfect for adventure lovers, photographers, bikers, and explorers, Spiti offers offbeat travel, stargazing, nature walks, and cultural immersion—far from the crowds and chaos of city life.

testimonals.name: Sahil & Meera
testimonals.review: Driving through the barren beauty of Spiti felt like being on another planet. Tripdekhoo helped us rent a well-maintained SUV and planned halts perfectly. The stay at Tabo and the views from Langza still give us goosebumps. It wasn’t just a trip—it was a soul journey. We wouldn’t have managed such a remote region without their guidance.

testimonals.name: Rohit Sharma
testimonals.review: I did the Spiti circuit solo on a rented bike and Tripdekhoo helped me with route planning, homestays, and emergency support. The ride from Kaza to Chicham bridge was insane! Their local contact even helped me fix a puncture in Losar. I felt secure even while off-grid. This was the most thrilling trip of my life.

testimonals.name: Joshi Family
testimonals.review: We wanted something offbeat but safe for our teenage kids, and Tripdekhoo recommended Spiti in summer. The monasteries fascinated my son and the night sky amazed us all. Every stay was clean, warm, and scenic. Even in the remote villages, we never felt disconnected. A truly enriching family experience.

testimonals.name: Arushi & Raghav
testimonals.review: Spiti was a photographer’s dream—minimalist landscapes, ancient monasteries, and star-studded skies. Tripdekhoo ensured we stayed in properties with great views and gave us time for golden-hour shoots. They even arranged a local to guide us to a secret lake near Dhankar. We came back with memory cards full of magic!

testimonals.name: Sana
testimonals.review: Tripdekhoo created a soulful itinerary with slow travel in Spiti. I spent time meditating at Key Monastery and walking through the peaceful village of Lhalung. My homestay hosts were kind and welcoming. Disconnecting from the digital world and reconnecting with myself was exactly what I needed.

testimonals.name: Kabir & College Friends
testimonals.review: We did a 9-day Spiti circuit with Tripdekhoo and it was packed with adventure—camping in Chandratal, hiking to Dhankar Lake, and off-roading near Mudh village. Our tempo traveler had a fun driver who doubled as our storyteller. Spiti tested us, thrilled us, and united us. Best college trip ever!

testimonals.name: Neha Bansal
testimonals.review: I booked a solo backpacking package for Spiti with Tripdekhoo and it was so affordable yet well managed. Shared cabs, community stays, and local food experiences made this trip authentic and budget-friendly. Every turn on the road was picture-worthy. Would totally do it again!

testimonals.name: Divyansh & Tara
testimonals.review: Yes, Spiti is remote, but Tripdekhoo managed to give us luxury wherever possible. Boutique camps in Chandratal, curated food at homestays, and private jeeps made it a blend of comfort and wild terrain. It was adventurous, but never rough. That’s what stood out the most.

testimonals.name: Ankita
testimonals.review: If you want to escape the noise of life, go to Spiti. Tripdekhoo planned a perfect route with no internet, limited calls, and lots of stars. I journaled, read books, and connected with nature. They even gave me a checklist of things to carry. Peace like I’ve never known.

testimonals.name: Verma Family
testimonals.review: We were fascinated by Spiti’s Tibetan roots and Tripdekhoo ensured we explored that fully. Monastery tours, local meals with villagers, and visits to schools made our kids appreciate a new way of life. It was educational, adventurous, and deeply touching. Truly eye-opening.

testimonals.name: Ritesh & Nandita
testimonals.review: We didn’t want a beach or city trip for our anniversary—Spiti was our surprise pick, and it was unforgettable. Tripdekhoo arranged a small celebration at our guesthouse in Kaza and even got us a cake! Sitting under the stars, wrapped in blankets, sipping tea—it was a simple yet unforgettable memory.

testimonals.name: Jatin & Colleagues
testimonals.review: We did a work-from-the-hills week followed by a trekking extension. Tripdekhoo arranged stable homestays with power backup and internet in Tabo and Kaza. After work hours, we explored nearby villages, and over the weekend we hiked to remote lakes. It was productive and refreshing!

testimonals.name: Priya
testimonals.review: I had seen Spiti in reels but the real thing was far beyond! The colors, the silence, and the kindness of locals—it hits you differently. Tripdekhoo created a safe, mindful itinerary with scenic stays and no hectic rush. Even the drive was meditative. Highly recommend for nature lovers.

testimonals.name: Nakul & Ishita
testimonals.review: Many avoid Spiti in monsoon but it was green and serene in the valleys. Tripdekhoo gave us updates on road conditions, flexible plans, and helpful local guides. We avoided landslide-prone areas and still saw everything on our list. It felt raw, real, and deeply personal.

testimonals.name: Manav
testimonals.review: As a student traveler, I had limited money but big dreams. Tripdekhoo gave me a shared-group tour, dorm-style stays, and a real taste of Spiti. It wasn’t luxurious, but it was honest and adventurous. I met great people, saw unreal landscapes, and came back stronger.

packages.fagHeading: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Spiti Valley Tour from Delhi

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Spiti Valley?
answer: The ideal time to visit is May to October when the roads are open and weather is pleasant.
Winters (November to April) bring heavy snow and many routes become inaccessible.

faqs.question: What is the starting point of this trip?
answer: The tour begins and ends in Delhi.
You can reach Delhi by air, train, or road, depending on your location.

faqs.question: Is this trip suitable for beginners or families?
answer: Spiti is a high-altitude, offbeat destination best suited for travelers with moderate fitness levels.
Families with kids or elderly members should consult a doctor beforehand and be cautious about altitude sickness.

faqs.question: What is the altitude in Spiti Valley? Will I face altitude sickness?
answer: Spiti lies at elevations ranging from 3,000 to 4,500 meters.
Altitude sickness is a real concern — ensure gradual acclimatization, drink water frequently, and avoid overexertion.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodations are provided?
answer: You’ll stay in clean and hygienic hotels, guesthouses, or camps on a double/triple-sharing basis depending on availability and group size.

faqs.question: Are meals included in the package?
answer: Yes, daily buffet breakfast and dinner are included.
Lunch and snacks are not included, allowing flexibility during travel stops.

faqs.question: What type of vehicle will be used for the trip?
answer: Depending on group size, you’ll travel in SUVs or Tempo Travellers.
All vehicles are non-AC and non-heated due to the terrain and climate.

faqs.question: Is there network and internet connectivity in Spiti?
answer: Connectivity is limited.
Basic mobile networks like BSNL may work in some towns (e.g., Kaza), but there is no internet or network in remote regions like Hikkim, Dhankar, or Chandratal.

faqs.question: Is a permit required for Spiti Valley?
answer: Yes, permits such as the Inner Line Permit and Manali Green Tribunal Permit are required and included in your package.

faqs.question: What should I carry for the trip?
answer: Warm clothes & thermals
Trek/hiking shoes
First-aid kit & medicines
Daypack (20–30L)
Reusable water bottle
Valid ID proof (not PAN)
Sunglasses, sunscreen, moisturizer
A complete checklist is included under “Things To Carry” in your itinerary.

faqs.question: Are adventure activities included?
answer: The trip includes sightseeing and cultural experiences, but activities like river crossings, trekking, or monastery visits may have entry fees or be optional (not included in base cost).

faqs.question: Can I join this tour solo?
answer: Yes, solo travelers are welcome but minimum group size is 2 to operate the tour.
Solo travelers may be placed with another group or asked to join a different date if numbers are not met.

faqs.question: Will there be a guide?
answer: Yes, an experienced driver-cum-guide will accompany you, familiar with local routes and terrain.

faqs.question: Are there ATMs in Spiti?
answer: ATMs are very limited (mainly in Kaza or Reckong Peo) and often non-functional.
It's recommended to carry sufficient cash from Delhi or Manali.

faqs.question: What if I want to leave the tour midway?
answer: If you choose to exit the tour early, all subsequent expenses will be borne by you.
No refunds are provided for unused services.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance included?
answer: No, travel insurance is not included, but it is highly recommended for high-altitude destinations like Spiti.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Explore Manali – Gateway to the Himalayas
activities: Begin your journey with sightseeing in Manali. Visit the serene Hadimba Temple amidst cedar forests, the ancient Manu Temple, and enjoy shopping at Mall Road. Adventure lovers can opt for paragliding, trekking, or river rafting against the backdrop of stunning Himalayan landscapes.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Manali to Kaza via Kunzum Pass – Witness Bara-Sigri Glacier
activities: Drive through Atal Tunnel and ascend to Kunzum Pass (14,931 ft). On the way, marvel at the Bara-Sigri Glacier, the second-longest in the Himalayas. The scenic route offers rugged mountain vistas and the raw beauty of Spiti Valley before reaching Kaza.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Kaza Sightseeing – Key Monastery & Spiti Exploration
activities: Discover the spiritual charm of Key Monastery, known for its vibrant murals and hilltop location with sweeping views of Spiti Valley. Explore the cultural richness and traditional lifestyle of the region.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Kaza to Chandratal via Kunzum La – The Enchanting Moon Lake
activities: Travel through Kunzum La to reach Chandratal, the “Moon Lake.” Famous for its crystal-clear waters that shift colors with the sun, the lake is a magical highlight of Spiti, surrounded by dramatic Himalayan peaks.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Chandratal to Manali via Rohtang Pass – Scenic Himalayan Drive
activities: Return to Manali via Rohtang Pass, soaking in breathtaking views of the Geypan Peaks. The scenic drive with winding roads and snow-capped mountains completes your unforgettable Himalayan adventure.

Often called “Little Tibet” for its stark landscapes and ancient monasteries, Spiti is a paradise for travelers seeking solitude, spiritual experiences, and thrilling adventures.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Shimla | Transfer to Chitkul – The Last Village on the Indo-Tibetan Border
activities: Arrive in Shimla and drive towards Chitkul, a charming hamlet nestled in Baspa Valley. Known as the last inhabited village on the Indo-Tibetan border, Chitkul greets you with snow-clad peaks, wooden houses, and tranquil surroundings—an ideal start to your Himalayan journey.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Chitkul to Nako | Experience the Ancient Yak-Skin Prayer Wheel
activities: Proceed to Nako, a picturesque village by a high-altitude lake. Visit the ancient monastery and spin the 500-year-old prayer wheel crafted from yak skin—a rare and spiritual encounter that connects you with the deep-rooted Buddhist traditions of the valley.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Nako to Kaza | Explore Key Monastery’s Artistic Heritage
activities: Travel to Kaza, the lively hub of Spiti Valley. Visit the iconic Key Monastery, famed for its artistically painted walls, intricate frescoes, and treasured Buddhist scriptures. The hilltop monastery also offers breathtaking views of the vast Spiti landscapes.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Excursion Around Kaza | World’s Highest Post Office at Hikkim
activities: Set out to explore nearby villages including Hikkim, home to the highest post office in the world. Post a letter from here as a one-of-a-kind travel memory. Visit Komik and Langza villages, soaking in Spiti’s unmatched charm and high-altitude beauty.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Kaza to Kalpa via Dhankar | Witness Kinnaur Kailash Peak
activities: En route to Kalpa, stop at the cliffside Dhankar Monastery, a historic gem overlooking confluence valleys. On arrival in Kalpa, marvel at the stunning Kinnaur Kailash Peak, which dominates the skyline with its spiritual and majestic presence.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Kalpa to Shimla | Farewell to the Enchanting Spiti Valley
activities: Drive back to Shimla, bidding adieu to the magical valleys, monasteries, and towering peaks of Spiti. Return with unforgettable memories of this soul-stirring Himalayan adventure.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Delhi to Manali | Scenic Drive Through the Himalayas
activities: Depart from Delhi for an overnight journey to Manali. Nestled in the Beas River Valley, Manali welcomes you with snow-clad peaks, pine forests, and riverside charm—an enchanting prelude to your Himalayan adventure.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Arrival in Manali | Local Sightseeing & Himalayan Vibes
activities: On reaching Manali, explore Hadimba Devi Temple, Manu Temple, and the bustling Mall Road. Enjoy the serene riverside, soak in the beauty of cedar forests, and prepare for the adventures that lie ahead in the high Himalayas.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Manali to Kaza via Kunzum Pass | Gateway to Spiti Valley
activities: Travel across the spectacular Kunzum Pass (14,931 ft), a high-altitude gateway to Spiti. The journey unfolds barren valleys, glaciers, and rugged mountain terrain before arriving at Kaza, the heart of dramatically on a cliff with views of river confluences. Later, explore Pin Valley—famed for rare wildlife, lush meadows, and contrasting landscapes.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Kaza Sightseeing | Highest Post Office, Monasteries & Villages
activities: Discover Hikkim, home to the world’s highest post office, and post a letter from 14,567 ft. Visit Key Monastery with its vibrant murals and scriptures, then explore the quaint villages of Langza and Komic—known for fossils, culture, and panoramic views.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Excursion to Tabo, Dhankar & Pin Valley | Monasteries & Hidden Charms
activities: Visit Tabo Monastery, over 1,000 years old and renowned as the “Ajanta of the Himalayas” for its caves and murals. Continue to Dhankar Monastery, perched dramatically on a cliff with views of river confluences. Later, explore Pin Valley—famed for rare wildlife, lush meadows, and contrasting landscapes.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Kaza to Chandratal Lake | The Moon Lake Experience
activities: Drive to Chandratal, the magical “Moon Lake.” Known for its crystal-clear waters that shift colors with the sun, the lake is a jewel of Spiti surrounded by soaring peaks—perfect for reflection, photography, and stargazing.

itinerary.day: Day 7: Chandratal to Manali & Departure to Delhi | Farewell Spiti
activities: Return to Manali via Lahaul Valley, enjoying spellbinding views of the Geypan Peaks. After some leisure time in Manali, board your return journey to Delhi, carrying unforgettable memories of Spiti’s rugged beauty and timeless culture.

about_the_tour: Explore the raw beauty and rugged charm of Spiti Valley, a high-altitude desert nestled deep within the Himalayas of Himachal Pradesh. Often called “Little Tibet” for its stark landscapes and ancient monasteries, Spiti is a paradise for travelers seeking solitude, spiritual experiences, and thrilling adventures.

This tour takes you on a soul-stirring journey through winding mountain roads, centuries-old gompas, crystal-clear rivers, and charming villages that seem untouched by time. Visit iconic destinations like Kaza, Key Monastery, Hikkim (home to the world's highest post office), Komic (one of the world’s highest villages), and the surreal Chandratal Lake.
Perfect for adventure lovers, photographers, bikers, and explorers, Spiti offers offbeat travel, stargazing, nature walks, and cultural immersion—far from the crowds and chaos of city life.
how_to_reach: By Air: The Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL) in Delhi is well connected to all major cities in India and internationally. It is the most convenient option for travelers flying in.
By Train: You can arrive at New Delhi Railway Station (NDLS) or Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station (NZM). These are major railway hubs with connections from across the country.

By Road: Delhi is well connected by national highways to nearby cities such as Jaipur, Agra, Chandigarh, Dehradun, and even international routes like Kathmandu (Nepal). Frequent state-run and private buses operate to and from Delhi.
highlight: Embark on an epic Himalayan road trip from Delhi to Spiti, weaving through dramatic landscapes, ancient villages, and winding mountain passes.
Conquer Kunzum Pass, one of India’s highest motorable passes, and witness the breathtaking transition from Lahaul to Spiti surrounded by snow-covered peaks.
Mail a memory from Hikkim, home to the world’s highest post office — a truly unique experience that lets you share your journey with loved ones from the top of the world.
Step back in time at Tabo Monastery, the oldest continuously functioning Buddhist enclave in India, rich with ancient murals, scriptures, and a tranquil spiritual aura.
Explore the untamed wilderness of Pin Valley, a high-altitude national park home to rare Himalayan wildlife — keep your eyes open for the elusive snow leopard and other alpine fauna.

packages.fagHeading: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Spiti Valley Tour from Delhi

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Spiti Valley?
answer: The ideal time to visit is May to October when the roads are open and weather is pleasant.
Winters (November to April) bring heavy snow and many routes become inaccessible.

faqs.question: What is the starting point of this trip?
answer: The tour begins and ends in Delhi.
You can reach Delhi by air, train, or road, depending on your location.

faqs.question: Is this trip suitable for beginners or families?
answer: Spiti is a high-altitude, offbeat destination best suited for travelers with moderate fitness levels.
Families with kids or elderly members should consult a doctor beforehand and be cautious about altitude sickness.

faqs.question: What is the altitude in Spiti Valley? Will I face altitude sickness?
answer: Spiti lies at elevations ranging from 3,000 to 4,500 meters.
Altitude sickness is a real concern — ensure gradual acclimatization, drink water frequently, and avoid overexertion.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodations are provided?
answer: You’ll stay in clean and hygienic hotels, guesthouses, or camps on a double/triple-sharing basis depending on availability and group size.

faqs.question: Are meals included in the package?

Lunch and snacks are not included, allowing flexibility during travel stops.

faqs.question: What type of vehicle will be used for the trip?
answer: Depending on group size, you’ll travel in SUVs or Tempo Travellers.
All vehicles are non-AC and non-heated due to the terrain and climate.

faqs.question: Is there network and internet connectivity in Spiti?
answer: Connectivity is limited.
Basic mobile networks like BSNL may work in some towns (e.g., Kaza), but there is no internet or network in remote regions like Hikkim, Dhankar, or Chandratal.

answer: Yes, permits such as the Inner Line Permit and Manali Green Tribunal Permit are required and included in your package.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Arrival in Chandigarh | The Modern Gateway to the Himalayas
activities: Arrive in Chandigarh, India’s first planned city designed by Le Corbusier. Explore the Rock Garden, Sukhna Lake, and other architectural landmarks before beginning your Himalayan expedition.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Chandigarh to Narkanda | Apple Orchards & Himalayan Views
activities: Ride through winding mountain roads to Narkanda, known as the Apple Capital of India. At 8,100 ft, enjoy panoramic Himalayan views, cool mountain air, and lush orchards.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Narkanda to Chitkul | The Last Village on the Indo-Tibetan Border
activities: Head towards Chitkul, the last inhabited village on the Indo-Tibetan border. Surrounded by wooden houses, pristine valleys, and crystal-clear rivers, it offers an authentic Himalayan charm.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Chitkul to Kalpa | Sacred Peaks & Serene Landscapes
activities: Travel to Kalpa, famed for its breathtaking views of Kinnaur Kailash. Spot the revered Shivling Rock formation and soak in the serenity of terraced fields and apple orchards.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Kalpa to Kaza via Tabo | Ancient Monasteries & Heritage
activities: Ride towards Kaza, the hub of Spiti Valley. En route, visit Tabo Monastery—over 1,000 years old and known as the “Ajanta of the Himalayas” for its ancient murals and cave shrines.

itinerary.day: Day 6: Kaza Excursion | Villages & the World’s Highest Post Office
activities: Explore Key Monastery, perched dramatically on a hill, and visit Hikkim to post a letter from the world’s highest post office. Continue to Langza, Komic, and Chicham, immersing yourself in Spiti’s unique culture and landscapes.

itinerary.day: Day 7: Kaza to Chandratal via Kunzum La | The Mesmerizing Moon Lake
activities: Cross Kunzum Pass (14,931 ft) en route to Chandratal, the “Moon Lake.” Known for its ever-changing hues, this high-altitude lake offers an ethereal experience amidst rugged peaks.

itinerary.day: Day 8: Chandratal to Manali via Rohtang Pass | Majestic Himalayan Drive
activities: Ride towards Manali, passing through the scenic Rohtang Pass. Enjoy spectacular views of the Geypan Peaks and dramatic Himalayan landscapes before reaching Manali.

itinerary.day: Day 9: Manali to Chandigarh | End of the Expedition
activities: Conclude your bike expedition with a return ride to Chandigarh. Descend from the mountains with unforgettable memories of pristine valleys, monasteries, and thrilling Himalayan adventures.

about_the_tour: Honeymoon in Kashmir! Explore Srinagar's charming avenues and houseboats on Dal Lake. Stroll hand-in-hand through Mughal gardens and the old city, finding unique souvenirs. Then, drive through stunning landscapes to Gulmarg. Enjoy the Lidder River and nearby valleys. Finally, capture romantic photos in Sonmarg's vibrant meadows - a memory to cherish forever.

testimonals.name: Simran & Karan
testimonals.review: Kashmir was a dream, and Tripdekhoo made it magical. From a private shikara ride on Dal Lake to a candlelight dinner in our Pahalgam resort, everything felt like a romantic movie. The snow in Gulmarg and the pine views from our room left us speechless. We were pampered every day with smooth transfers and personalized service.

testimonals.name: Ravi Mehta & Family
testimonals.review: This was our first trip to Kashmir and we were a bit nervous. Tripdekhoo handled everything—local guides, Kashmiri food, clean hotels, and even snow jackets for my kids! The tulip gardens in Srinagar were in full bloom and Sonmarg was a winter fairytale. Truly a peaceful and memorable experience for our entire family.

testimonals.name: Nisha
testimonals.review: As a solo female traveler, safety was my top concern. Tripdekhoo ensured I stayed in central locations, assigned a local woman guide in Srinagar, and checked in with me regularly. I even explored floating markets and attended a Sufi music evening. It was empowering and soul-refreshing.

testimonals.name: Abhay & Ritu
testimonals.review: We had never seen snowfall before and wanted a white Kashmir experience. Tripdekhoo timed our tour perfectly—fresh snow in Gulmarg, cozy stays with heaters, and snow games that took us back to childhood. Their team even arranged a ski instructor for beginners. It was thrilling and very well organized!

testimonals.name: Shruti & Dinesh
testimonals.review: We didn’t just want sightseeing—we wanted to understand Kashmiri culture. Tripdekhoo added heritage walks, saffron farm visits, and even a day with a local family for a traditional wazwan meal. These touches made the trip so authentic and heartfelt. We returned with stories, not just photos.

testimonals.name: The Bansals
testimonals.review: Travelling with our elderly parents was smooth thanks to Tripdekhoo. They ensured wheelchair-friendly stays, minimal walking, and warm service. The houseboat stay on Dal Lake was a favorite, and the slow pace allowed us to truly soak in Kashmir’s beauty without any rush.

testimonals.name: Tanvi & College Friends
testimonals.review: We wanted an adventurous yet affordable Kashmir tour. Tripdekhoo packed our days with gondola rides, snow biking, pony rides, and even a trek near Aru Valley. The hostels and group stays they chose were super clean and had mountain views. This trip bonded our group like nothing else!

testimonals.name: Aditya
testimonals.review: As a landscape photographer, I wanted a tailored itinerary. Tripdekhoo arranged sunrise shoots at Dal Lake, a private cab for remote spots in Sonmarg, and even connected me with a local fixer for drone permissions. The chinar trees, snowy slopes, and golden evenings gave me the best shots of my career.

testimonals.name: Arjun & Nivedita
testimonals.review: We opted for premium hotels and Tripdekhoo curated a 5-star experience. From boutique resorts in Pahalgam to luxury shikara lounges in Srinagar, the service was flawless. Our guide was knowledgeable, spoke fluent English, and even helped us shop for the best Pashmina.

testimonals.name: Shreya
testimonals.review: I needed a break from the chaos of city life. Tripdekhoo built an introspective itinerary with Sufi shrines, visits to Hazratbal, and a peaceful stay near the Lidder River. I spent hours meditating in nature. Kashmir’s silence was exactly what my soul needed.

testimonals.name: Vikrant & Office Team
testimonals.review: Our company’s offsite to Kashmir was organized by Tripdekhoo and it was a big success. We stayed in a resort with a conference hall, team-building sessions were conducted in the meadows of Gulmarg, and the bonfire evening with local music was the highlight. Everyone returned rejuvenated.

testimonals.name: Divya & Samar
testimonals.review: We traveled in April to witness the tulips and almond blossoms. Tripdekhoo scheduled visits to Mughal Gardens, Nishat Bagh, and lesser-known orchard spots. The air was fragrant, and the colors—unreal. Kashmir in spring is divine, and this trip exceeded every expectation.

testimonals.name: Mihir & Bhavna
testimonals.review: As foodies, we asked Tripdekhoo to make cuisine a focus. They delivered big time—home-cooked wazwan feasts, kahwa tastings, bakery visits in old Srinagar, and a spice shopping tour. Our guide even explained the stories behind each dish. We ate our way through Kashmir happily!

testimonals.name: Rhea
testimonals.review: Being a solo traveler on a tight budget, I was amazed how Tripdekhoo made it work. I stayed in cozy guesthouses with mountain views, took shared cabs, and still got to see Gulmarg, Pahalgam, and the old city of Srinagar. I never once felt unsafe or alone.

testimonals.name: Karan & Dev
testimonals.review: People warned us against visiting in monsoon but it turned out to be an amazing offbeat decision. The hills were lush, crowds were less, and everything felt fresh and untouched. Tripdekhoo managed all logistics even during the rain—flexible and responsive. Highly recommended!
