know_before_you_go: Pick up from the airport is only between 05:00 AM to 07:00 PM as it becomes unsafe for travel on the outskirts. Beyond these timings, you are advised to let Tripdekhoo POC know before booking if you are arriving after 7 PM in Siliguri so that Tripdekhoo can rearrange your Itinerary accordingly as you might have to stay in Siliguri itself.

Govt. Approved Photo ID proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking (to acquire necessary permits), and also upon arrival. PAN card and Driving License will not be considered as a valid address proof.
There is no governing authority (HRACC) to decide the star category of the hotels. Hence, the standards of the room will not be the same as TIER-I/II Cities.
By default, we arrange a standard category room while booking unless you specify to receive a different (upgraded) category of rooms for your stay requirements.

In case of triple sharing rooms, extra mattresses will be provided at the assigned property. Due to infrastructure limitations in the region the rooms in the North-East come with very basic and necessary amenities only.

Senior citizens and travelers younger than 4 years are not recommended to go to Gurudongmar Lake because of low oxygen levels. Permits for the infant under 2 years of age are not granted by North Sikkim tourism. That means if you have an infant traveling with you, you’ll not be allowed to go to North Sikkim.

As per North East guidelines, vehicles are available on point to point basis only (not on disposal), any deviation in the itinerary would cost an additional amount (unless any issue occurs such as bad weather, Political/social disturbances, roadblocks, VVIP movements & state transport rule prohibition). Before changing the itinerary, you are free to consult with us for the charges.

The charges for Nathu La Pass are not included in the package as this is a restricted area and special permits are required to visit the same. Permits are granted only between Wednesday and Sunday and can be canceled anytime for security reasons or weather conditions. Very limited number of vehicles are granted permits for Nathu La therefore the same are subject to availability and are never guaranteed in advance. Thus, you are required to pay the same on spot, depending on the real time conditions. (Applicable even if Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir are included in the package).
Nathu La Pass can be added at an extra cost of INR 4000/- to INR 9000/- per vehicle, depending on the season and availability.

Mt. Katao, Kalapathar, Chopta Valley and Zero Point (in North Sikkim) can be added at an extra cost of INR 4000/- to INR 9000/- per vehicle per spot, depending on the season. Visiting these spots are subject to availability of permits that are mandatory (for both Indian and Foreign Nationals).

Tripdekhoo does not recommend Sumo/ Bolero for its travelers as these vehicles are not allowed in the main market areas of Sikkim. However, if you choose these vehicles then you’ll be dropped at/ picked up from the nearest possible location. You might have to walk or take a union cab (at your own expense) to reach the hotel/ the pickup point.

During season time the vehicle may get delayed during pickup/ drop due to heavy traffic, bad weather, political/ social disturbances, roadblocks, VVIP movements & state transport rule prohibition. Customer discretion is advised.

Due to power shortages in the state, the government does not allow travelers to use electric room heaters. Also, it is possible that hotels may usually not have room heaters installed. However, in some hotels room heaters may be available on a chargeable basis (subject to availability).
As per state guidelines, travelers wearing a turban are not allowed in Lachen.

Foreign Nationals are not allowed to visit Lachen, Baba Mandir & Nathula Pass as per state authority due to security reasons. Foreign Nationals in groups of 2 or above will be allowed to visit Lachung & Tsomgo Lake with an Indian Guide (Mandatory). However, Foreign Nationals traveling solo are not granted permits to visit any part of North Sikkim.
Foreign National with Indian Spouse will be considered as a solo traveler unless the spouse also has an OCI Card.

If your permit for North Sikkim is canceled/ not issued due to adverse weather conditions/ political dispute, etc., Tripdekhoo will arrange alternate sightseeing for the travelers safety. In such cases, cost of alternative accommodation needs to be borne by the customer as the pre-booked hotels execute their cancellation policies & are non-refundable. The same policy applies when you book the hotels yourself as well.
Heavy rainfalls are observed between June – September & real time itinerary changes are possible in case of road blocks due to landslides or any other natural calamity.

Any change in the itinerary is subject to weather conditions, political manifestations, and government restrictions, etc. Tripdekhoo & On Ground Operators reserve the right to rearrange the itinerary in such cases.

Any sightseeing point which is not completed due to time constraints, traffic jams, natural calamity, travelers starting late, permits issued late or any other reason beyond Tripdekhoo’s control are not liable for a refund or a discount.
The entire tour passes through eco-friendly zones and littering is prohibited. Any traveller found guilty might have to face strict charges by the local law enforcing authorities.
Any Health Guidelines issued by the State-Government are to be followed. Social distancing to be maintained. Frequent hand sanitization and use of masks is recommended.

It is advised that the travelers do not consume alcohol or any other intoxicants during the tour as it may cause respiratory problems or dehydration at high altitudes which can lead to serious health conditions and can be fatal as there are limited medical facilities in remote locations.
Air fare / Train fare /Bus fare are not included in the package and the cost mentioned above.
The travelers will have to take care of their international airfare, visa fees, airport tax or any kind of insurance cover.
GST is applicable to the package and not included in the above cost.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Sikkim?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit Sikkim is from March to June (spring-summer) and September to December (autumn-winter). Avoid the monsoon season (July–August) due to landslides and roadblocks.

faqs.question: Is a permit required to visit North Sikkim and Nathula Pass?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Protected Area Permit (PAP) is required to visit North Sikkim (Lachen, Lachung, Yumthang, Gurudongmar Lake) and Nathula Pass. These are arranged by local operators and are issued only to Indian nationals. Foreign nationals are not allowed in some parts of North Sikkim.

faqs.question: Can foreign nationals travel to North Sikkim?
faqs.answer: No, foreign nationals are not permitted to travel to Lachen, Gurudongmar Lake, Nathula Pass, or Baba Mandir. They can visit Lachung and Tsomgo Lake, but only in a group of two or more and with a mandatory Indian guide.

faqs.question: How high is Gurudongmar Lake and is it safe for everyone?
faqs.answer: Gurudongmar Lake is at 17,800 ft. It is not recommended for children under 4 years, infants, or senior citizens due to low oxygen levels. Travelers must be in good health and should consult a doctor before the trip.

faqs.question: What vehicles are used for the trip and are they allowed everywhere?
faqs.answer: Vehicles like Innova, Xylo, or similar are used. However, Sumo/Bolero are not allowed inside main Gangtok city. Point-to-point travel is followed as per local union rules; deviation requires additional charges.

faqs.question: Can I add Nathula Pass, Zero Point, or Katao to my itinerary?
faqs.answer: Yes, these can be added at an extra cost (INR 4000–9000 per vehicle per spot), subject to permit availability and weather. Nathula Pass is open only from Wednesday to Sunday and is not guaranteed in advance.

faqs.question: Is travel to Sikkim suitable for children and elderly travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, Gangtok and moderate elevations are suitable. However, high-altitude areas like Gurudongmar Lake are not advisable for small children, infants, or elderly due to extreme altitude and oxygen deficiency.

faqs.question: What documents are required for the Sikkim tour?
faqs.answer: Each traveler must carry a valid government photo ID (Voter ID or Passport). PAN cards and Driving Licenses are not accepted for permits. Foreigners need valid visas and additional documentation for special permits.

faqs.question: Will I get mobile connectivity and internet access in North Sikkim?
faqs.answer: Mobile connectivity is limited in North Sikkim. BSNL and Jio work in some areas, but internet is weak or unavailable, especially in Lachen and Lachung.

faqs.question: What are the hotel standards in Sikkim, especially North Sikkim?
faqs.answer: In North Sikkim, hotels are basic with minimal amenities due to remote location and limited infrastructure. Power cuts are common and room heaters may not be available unless requested at an extra charge.

faqs.question: What is the policy in case permits are denied or weather disrupts travel?
faqs.answer: If permits are denied or roads are blocked due to weather, political issues, or natural calamities, alternate sightseeing will be arranged. However, hotel costs are non-refundable and travelers bear any extra costs.

faqs.question: Are electric heaters available in hotels?
faqs.answer: Due to government restrictions and power shortages, electric room heaters are not provided by default. Some hotels may offer them at a chargeable rate, subject to availability.

faqs.question: Can I travel to Sikkim by train or air?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Nearest airport: Bagdogra (IXB)
Nearest railway station: New Jalpaiguri (NJP)
From either, you can take a cab to Gangtok (4–5 hours drive).

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Gangtok
activities: Welcome to Gangtok, the Land of Monasteries. Upon your arrival at Bagdogra Airport/NJP Railway Station, get transferred to the hotel in Gangtok. After relaxing for some time, stroll through the city at your own pace by visiting some of the places, like the Seven Sister Water Falls and the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology. Also, you can pray in peace at Do Drul Chorten Stupa and Phodong Monastery. Later, return to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Visit to Baba Mandir & Tsomgo Lake | Transfer to Zuluk
activities: Enjoy a day trip to Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir. Board your transfer from the hotel and spend a wonderful time at the stunning Tsomgo Lake. Then, visit the shrine of Baba Harbhajan Singh, also known as the Baba Mandir, known to protect soldiers in the Eastern Himalayas. If the time permits, you can also visit Nathula Pass, connecting Sikkim to Tibet. Afterward, get transferred to Zuluk and check-in at your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Gangtok | Enroute Sightseeing
activities: Get ready for an amazing journey towards Gangtok. Check-out from the hotel and enjoy an amazing journey passing through rugged lands of various valleys like the Kupup, Tukla, and Nathang. Admire the stunning mountains along the way. Enjoy a short stopover at Thambi View Point and take-in the views of the beautiful curvy roads overseeing Zuluk. Continue the journey to Gangtok, and upon your arrival, check-in at your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Lachen
activities: Enjoy a change of surroundings as you check-out from the hotel. Enjoy a scenic drive to Lachen, and on the way, admire the beauty of the beautiful rivers in the lush green valleys. Also, take-in the views of the surroundings as you pass through various small villages, seeing the Buddhist local culture closely. Upon your arrival, check-in at the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Visit to Gurudongmar Lake | Transfer to Lachung
activities: Today, proceed towards the highest lakes in the world, Gurudongmar Lake. Check-out from the hotel and get transferred to the lake. Take a moment to admire the beauty of the surrounding snow-capped mountains. Explore the area around the lake on foot and see various Himalayan birds and animals in their natural habitat. After spending a peaceful time at the lake, get transferred to Lachung and check-in at your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Excursion to Yumthang Valley | Transfer to Gangtok
activities: Check-out from the hotel and get transferred to explore Yumthang Valley, Sikkim's Valley of Flowers. Upon your arrival, admire the beautiful Primula, Rhododendron, and other alpine flowers. While you are there, also visit Zero Point, where three rivers meet against the snowy mountain view and beautiful surroundings. After that, get transferred back to Lachung to have lunch. Later, get transferred to Gangtok, and upon your arrival, check-in at the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Departure Day
activities: It’s time to say goodbye to all the amazing experiences. Get transferred from the hotel to Bagdogra Airport/NJP Railway Station. This is where your trip ends. Have a safe journey back home.

Permits are granted only between Wednesday and Sunday and can be canceled anytime for security reasons or weather conditions. Very limited number of vehicles are granted permits for Nathu La therefore the same are subject to availability and are never guaranteed in advance. Thus, you are required to pay the same on spot, depending on the real time conditions. (Applicable even if Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir are included in the package).
Nathu La Pass can be added at an extra cost of INR 4000/- to INR 9000/- per vehicle, depending on the season and availability.

Mt. Katao, Kalapathar, Chopta Valley and Zero Point (in North Sikkim) can be added at an extra cost of INR 4000/- to INR 9000/- per vehicle per spot, depending on the season. Visiting these spots are subject to availability of permits that are mandatory (for both Indian and Foreign Nationals).

Tripdekhoo does not recommend Sumo/ Bolero for its travelers as these vehicles are not allowed in the main market areas of Sikkim. However, if you choose these vehicles then you’ll be dropped at/ picked up from the nearest possible location. You might have to walk or take a union cab (at your own expense) to reach the hotel/ the pickup point.

During season time the vehicle may get delayed during pickup/ drop due to heavy traffic, bad weather, political/ social disturbances, roadblocks, VVIP movements & state transport rule prohibition. Customer discretion is advised.

Due to power shortages in the state, the government does not allow travelers to use electric room heaters. Also, it is possible that hotels may usually not have room heaters installed. However, in some hotels room heaters may be available on a chargeable basis (subject to availability).
As per state guidelines, travelers wearing a turban are not allowed in Lachen.

Foreign Nationals are not allowed to visit Lachen, Baba Mandir & Nathula Pass as per state authority due to security reasons. Foreign Nationals in groups of 2 or above will be allowed to visit Lachung & Tsomgo Lake with an Indian Guide (Mandatory). However, Foreign Nationals traveling solo are not granted permits to visit any part of North Sikkim.
Foreign National with Indian Spouse will be considered as a solo traveler unless the spouse also has an OCI Card.

If your permit for North Sikkim is canceled/ not issued due to adverse weather conditions/ political dispute, etc., Tripdekhoo will arrange alternate sightseeing for the travelers safety. In such cases, cost of alternative accommodation needs to be borne by the customer as the pre-booked hotels execute their cancellation policies & are non-refundable. The same policy applies when you book the hotels yourself as well.
Heavy rainfalls are observed between June – September & real time itinerary changes are possible in case of road blocks due to landslides or any other natural calamity.

Any change in the itinerary is subject to weather conditions, political manifestations, and government restrictions, etc. Tripdekhoo & On Ground Operators reserve the right to rearrange the itinerary in such cases.

Any sightseeing point which is not completed due to time constraints, traffic jams, natural calamity, travelers starting late, permits issued late or any other reason beyond Tripdekhoo’s control are not liable for a refund or a discount.
The entire tour passes through eco-friendly zones and littering is prohibited. Any traveller found guilty might have to face strict charges by the local law enforcing authorities.
Any Health Guidelines issued by the State-Government are to be followed. Social distancing to be maintained. Frequent hand sanitization and use of masks is recommended.

It is advised that the travelers do not consume alcohol or any other intoxicants during the tour as it may cause respiratory problems or dehydration at high altitudes which can lead to serious health conditions and can be fatal as there are limited medical facilities in remote locations.
Air fare / Train fare /Bus fare are not included in the package and the cost mentioned above.
The travelers will have to take care of their international airfare, visa fees, airport tax or any kind of insurance cover.
GST is applicable to the package and not included in the above cost.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Sikkim?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit Sikkim is from March to June (spring-summer) and September to December (autumn-winter). Avoid the monsoon season (July–August) due to landslides and roadblocks.

faqs.question: Is a permit required to visit North Sikkim and Nathula Pass?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Protected Area Permit (PAP) is required to visit North Sikkim (Lachen, Lachung, Yumthang, Gurudongmar Lake) and Nathula Pass. These are arranged by local operators and are issued only to Indian nationals. Foreign nationals are not allowed in some parts of North Sikkim.

faqs.question: Can foreign nationals travel to North Sikkim?
faqs.answer: No, foreign nationals are not permitted to travel to Lachen, Gurudongmar Lake, Nathula Pass, or Baba Mandir. They can visit Lachung and Tsomgo Lake, but only in a group of two or more and with a mandatory Indian guide.

faqs.question: How high is Gurudongmar Lake and is it safe for everyone?
faqs.answer: Gurudongmar Lake is at 17,800 ft. It is not recommended for children under 4 years, infants, or senior citizens due to low oxygen levels. Travelers must be in good health and should consult a doctor before the trip.

faqs.question: What vehicles are used for the trip and are they allowed everywhere?
faqs.answer: Vehicles like Innova, Xylo, or similar are used. However, Sumo/Bolero are not allowed inside main Gangtok city. Point-to-point travel is followed as per local union rules; deviation requires additional charges.

faqs.question: Can I add Nathula Pass, Zero Point, or Katao to my itinerary?
faqs.answer: Yes, these can be added at an extra cost (INR 4000–9000 per vehicle per spot), subject to permit availability and weather. Nathula Pass is open only from Wednesday to Sunday and is not guaranteed in advance.

faqs.question: Is travel to Sikkim suitable for children and elderly travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, Gangtok and moderate elevations are suitable. However, high-altitude areas like Gurudongmar Lake are not advisable for small children, infants, or elderly due to extreme altitude and oxygen deficiency.

faqs.question: What documents are required for the Sikkim tour?
faqs.answer: Each traveler must carry a valid government photo ID (Voter ID or Passport). PAN cards and Driving Licenses are not accepted for permits. Foreigners need valid visas and additional documentation for special permits.

faqs.question: Will I get mobile connectivity and internet access in North Sikkim?
faqs.answer: Mobile connectivity is limited in North Sikkim. BSNL and Jio work in some areas, but internet is weak or unavailable, especially in Lachen and Lachung.

faqs.question: What are the hotel standards in Sikkim, especially North Sikkim?
faqs.answer: In North Sikkim, hotels are basic with minimal amenities due to remote location and limited infrastructure. Power cuts are common and room heaters may not be available unless requested at an extra charge.

faqs.question: What is the policy in case permits are denied or weather disrupts travel?
faqs.answer: If permits are denied or roads are blocked due to weather, political issues, or natural calamities, alternate sightseeing will be arranged. However, hotel costs are non-refundable and travelers bear any extra costs.

faqs.question: Are electric heaters available in hotels?
faqs.answer: Due to government restrictions and power shortages, electric room heaters are not provided by default. Some hotels may offer them at a chargeable rate, subject to availability.

faqs.question: Can I travel to Sikkim by train or air?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Nearest airport: Bagdogra (IXB)
Nearest railway station: New Jalpaiguri (NJP)
From either, you can take a cab to Gangtok (4–5 hours drive).

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Gangtok | Leisure Day
activities: Welcome to Siliguri! Upon your arrival at the airport or railway station, you’ll be transferred to Gangtok. After checking in at your hotel, enjoy the day at leisure. You can visit Phodong Monastery, known for its beautiful murals or explore the Tashiding Monastery, perched on a hill, famous for its sacred relics and the vibrant Bhumchu festival. In the evening, you can stroll through Lal Bazaar, where you can shop for local crafts and savor delicious street food before returning to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Gangtok Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, get transferred for a sightseeing tour of Gangtok. Visit Tsomgo Lake, a glacial lake famous for its beauty and changing colours in every season. Then, see the world’s highest motorable roads at an altitude of 14,000+ ft., the NathuLa Pass, which connects India with China. Also, visit Baba Mandir, dedicated to Baba Harbhajan Singh, an Indian soldier who fought in the Sino-Indian War of 1967. Later, get transferred back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Transfer to Lachen via Chungthang
activities: Today, check out of the hotel and get transferred to Lachen, a beautiful village in North Sikkim, situated amidst the Himalayas. En route, pass by Chungthang Town, witnessing the confluence of Lachen Chu and Lachung Chu rivers. Upon arrival in Lachen, check in at your hotel and relax for a while. Later, you can explore the scenic town on your own, engaging with locals, learning about their culture and way of life. Later, head back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Transfer to Lachung | North Sikkim Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, after checking out of the hotel, you will be transferred to Lachung. On the way, enjoy a sightseeing tour of North Sikkim, where you'll marvel at the stunning Gurudongmar Lake, located at an impressive altitude of 17,800 ft. You'll also visit the majestic Bhim Nala Waterfalls, cascading down from a height of around 70 ft, offering a breathtaking view. Upon reaching Lachung, check in at your hotel and enjoy your overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 5 - Transfer to Gangtok | En route Visit Yumthang Valley | Leisure Day
activities: In the morning, check out of the hotel and get transferred to Gangtok. En route, visit Sikkim’s very own “Valley of Flowers”, Yumthang Valley. Then, continue your journey to Gangtok. Upon reaching your hotel, check in and relax. If time permits, you can also set out to explore the city on your own. We recommend key attractions like Reshi Hot Spring, Pemayangtse Monastery, and Kabi Lungchok, among others. Afterwards, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: DAY 6 - Transfer to Darjeeling | Leisure Day
activities: After checking out, you'll be transferred to Darjeeling. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel and enjoy the rest of the day at your leisure. You can explore the charming city on your own, visiting attractions like Nightingale Park, known for its lush greenery, St. Andrew’s Church, a beautiful colonial-era structure, and the sacred Mahakal Mandir. Additionally, you can hike up to Observatory Hill for stunning panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Afterward, return to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 7 - Darjeeling Sightseeing Tour
activities: Today, get driven for a city tour, starting with a visit to Tiger Hill for stunning views of Mt. Kanchenjunga. Next, explore the Peace Pagoda and the Batasia Loop, known for its scenic railway loop. Visit the Ghoom Monastery, the Tibetan Refugee Centre & the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute to learn about local culture and history. Additionally, explore the Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park, home to various endangered species. Afterward, get driven back to the hotel.

itinerary.day: DAY 8 - Transfer to Siliguri | Departure Day
activities: Check out of the hotel and get transferred to Siliguri. Upon arrival at New Jalpaiguri Railway Station or Bagdogra International Airport, you can take your journey back home, marking the end of your trip.

about_the_tour: If you enjoy summer adventures in the lap of the mountains, where expansive valleys and snow-draped peaks await,  treks are the perfect experience. Typically spread over 6 to 8 days, the trek is ideal for both beginners and seasoned trekkers, with guidance from expert trek leaders.

There are easy to moderate-level treks that earned its place in the trekking community for its natural beauty and diverse terrain. The trail winds through dense forests of pine and deodar, along glacial rivers, alpine meadows, and remote mountain hamlets — each day offering new and breathtaking landscapes.

The total trekking distance ranges between 40–50 km (round-trip), with the highest altitude reaching up to around 12,000 feet. The best time to undertake treks  is during the summer (April to June) or autumn (October to November) for clear skies, vibrant flora, and ideal weather conditions.

What makes this adventure even more rewarding is the logistical support you receive throughout. From comfortable camps and nutritious meals to safety equipment and trained personnel, every aspect is taken care of — allowing you to focus solely on the trail.
So lace up your boots, pack your bag, and set out on a journey through nature’s untouched paradise!

testimonals.name: Yash & Group
testimonals.review: The Hampta Pass trek with Tripdekhoo was like walking through changing worlds—lush valleys, river crossings, snow-covered passes. Our trek leader ensured safety and fun. Even the food at high altitudes was beyond expectation. Life-changing!

testimonals.name: Simran & Rahul
testimonals.review: A 7-day dreamland! Every lake felt like a painting. Tripdekhoo’s arrangements were flawless—mules, tents, meals, and expert local guides. We never felt unsafe or unprepared. It was more than a trek; it was a spiritual journey through nature.

testimonals.name: Neeraj
testimonals.review: The sliding descent on snow was wild fun! Tripdekhoo’s team was technically sound and ensured every hiker completed safely. The trek had forests, meadows, snowfields—perfectly balanced adventure.

testimonals.name: Divya
testimonals.review: Tripdekhoo helped me train, prepare, and conquer EBC. The acclimatization days, local guides, and group camaraderie made all the difference. I trusted them with my dream and they delivered beautifully.

testimonals.name: Tanmay
testimonals.review: One of the toughest treks I’ve done, and I wouldn’t have attempted it without Tripdekhoo’s expert planning. River crossings, glaciers, and high passes—all covered safely with top-quality gear and food. Unreal!

testimonals.name: Snehal & Dev
testimonals.review: This trek in Kashmir was poetic—alpine lakes, rolling meadows, and starry nights. Tripdekhoo’s Kashmir team was caring and enthusiastic. We felt immersed in a fairytale throughout the 8 days.

testimonals.name: Gaurav
testimonals.review: It was snow-covered beauty for 6 days! The team made sure beginners like me felt confident. Bonfire, mountain stories, and soul-warming food made it feel like home in the wild.

testimonals.name: Nivedita
testimonals.review: High-altitude Ladakh treks are challenging, but Tripdekhoo ensured oxygen support, Ladakhi porters, and gradual itinerary. It felt like a cultural expedition more than just a trek.

testimonals.name: Ayaan
testimonals.review: Nepal’s hospitality and Tripdekhoo’s coordination gave me a flawless trekking experience. The views of Machapuchare and Annapurna took my breath away—literally and metaphorically!

testimonals.name: Ruchi
testimonals.review: Less crowded, high on views, and a ridge walk that felt endless! The trek felt cinematic. Tripdekhoo’s planning, from transport to daily meals, was spot on. I want to do more with them.

testimonals.name: Jay & Palak
testimonals.review: We did this trek for New Year’s Eve and celebrated under the stars with our group. It was romantic, thrilling, and well-managed. Loved how Tripdekhoo made it special for couples!

testimonals.name: Devika
testimonals.review: Joined an all-women group for Goechala. The bonding, the scenery, and the strength we discovered in ourselves—it was unforgettable. Tripdekhoo’s women trek leaders were inspiring.

testimonals.name: Karan
testimonals.review: An offbeat 9-day trail, crossing villages and barren valleys. Tripdekhoo supported the whole thing with experienced guides, cultural insights, and even a surprise birthday celebration mid-trek!

testimonals.name: Parth
testimonals.review: We spotted two leopards on day 4! But what stood out was Tripdekhoo’s eco-sensitive approach—minimal footprint, local community support, and deep respect for nature.

testimonals.name: Tina & Sanjay
testimonals.review: At 55+, we weren’t sure if we could manage a long trek, but Tripdekhoo made it accessible. We did Dayara Bugyal over 6 days at a gentle pace with great care and amazing Himalayan hospitality.

testimonals.name: Ritika Sharma
testimonals.review: Being a beginner, I was nervous, but Tripdekhoo’s support made my first trek amazing! The views from the top were surreal, and the campsite was clean and cozy. I met lovely fellow trekkers, and our guide kept us engaged throughout. A perfect weekend escape into the wild.

testimonals.name: Anuj & Meera
testimonals.review: Triund was our first couple’s trek and Tripdekhoo made it magical. The stars at night, the campfire, and the Dhauladhar view in the morning—pure bliss! It was short, sweet, and perfectly arranged for city folks like us.

testimonals.name: Sarthak
testimonals.review: The trek was short but incredibly scenic. Tripdekhoo provided a local guide who shared legends about the temple, and we even got home-cooked food at the base village. This one will stay in my heart for years!

testimonals.name: Kavita Joshi
testimonals.review: I joined a women’s group trek with Tripdekhoo. Everything from permits to safety was well taken care of. Reaching the Chandrashila summit during sunrise was an emotional high. Even for a short trek, it felt like a big achievement!

testimonals.name: Ramesh & Friends
testimonals.review: Kareri Lake was frozen when we reached. The trail passed through wooden bridges and rivers, and Tripdekhoo’s trek leader was very motivating. It was short but not easy—just the kind of weekend adventure we wanted!

testimonals.name: Neelima
testimonals.review: Tripdekhoo added a twist to our trip with hot spring dips and a waterfall detour. Kheerganga was spiritual, scenic, and thrilling all in one. I’ll definitely be back for more short treks like this!

testimonals.name: Zoya & Aamir
testimonals.review: This trek had the best of everything—lake views, dense forests, and snow-capped peaks. For a short 3-day getaway, Tripdekhoo made sure every moment counted. We returned refreshed and full of memories.

testimonals.name: Aditya
testimonals.review: It was a lesser-known trail but so peaceful! Tripdekhoo ensured a comfortable trek for beginners like me, with great food and clean tents. Would love to try more short treks with them.

testimonals.name: Jyoti & Team
testimonals.review: Tripdekhoo customized a 2N/3D trek in the Manali region for our group. The itinerary had snow, forest walks, and fun camp activities. We didn’t need to plan anything—they took care of it all.

testimonals.name: Mahesh
testimonals.review: I combined work and trek near Kasol, arranged by Tripdekhoo. Strong Wi-Fi at base camp, morning hikes, and peaceful vibes—it was the perfect balance of productivity and nature.

testimonals.name: Sneha
testimonals.review: My first solo trek felt completely safe with Tripdekhoo. They had women trek leaders, backup support, and super helpful locals. Short trek, long memories!

testimonals.name: Ankit & Parents
testimonals.review: Tripdekhoo suggested a soft trek around Mussoorie for our parents and they loved it. Slow-paced, scenic, and completely hassle-free. A great way to experience the mountains at any age.

testimonals.name: Tanvi
testimonals.review: Booked a weekend trek to Nag Tibba through Tripdekhoo. Left on Friday, returned Sunday night with a clearer mind and happy soul. Seamless experience and a great guide!

testimonals.name: Tushar & Manan
testimonals.review: We were short on time but craving snow. Tripdekhoo planned a quick yet snowy adventure to a hidden trail in Uttarakhand. We got our snow fix and returned satisfied!

testimonals.name: Arpita
testimonals.review: Tripdekhoo curated a short trek near Rishikesh with daily yoga sessions. It was healing, energizing, and ideal for people who love a mix of movement and mindfulness.

how_to_reach: The base camp for most treks is a remote village or town accessible from a major city. You can reach the nearest city using any of the options below and then travel further by road.
By Air: Nearest airport is typically located in a nearby city. Regular direct and connecting flights are available from all major cities in India.
By Train: Regular trains connect the nearest major railway station to most metropolitan areas.
By Bus: Public and private buses run frequently from nearby towns and cities. State transport services are often reliable.
By Car: Scenic road routes connect the region via national highways. Self-driving or hiring a taxi is a great way to travel at your own pace.
Upon reaching the nearest city or town, you can take a cab or shared vehicle to the trek base.

know_before_you_go: Fitness: Light fitness prep recommended – cardio, leg strength, and stamina
Temperature: Expect cold nights (up to -5°C); layer your clothing accordingly
Connectivity: No mobile signal beyond base village; inform family beforehand
Water: Natural spring water is available en route; carry purification tablets if needed
Waste: Strictly follow a carry in-carry out waste policy – leave no trace
Network: Only emergency satellite comms may be available at campsites
Guidelines: Follow instructions of trek leaders strictly for safety and coordination
Permits: Trekking permits (if required) will be arranged by the operator

faqs.question: Who can join this trek?
faqs.answer: Anyone aged 10+ in decent physical health can participate. It is suitable for first-timers, families, and regular trekkers.

faqs.question: How difficult is this trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is Easy to Moderate, with daily trekking of 5–10 km. Altitude gain is gradual, and acclimatization is included.

faqs.question: When is the best time to go for the trek?
answer: April to June (Summer): Pleasant weather, clear skies, blooming flora.
October to November (Autumn): Post-monsoon freshness, fewer crowds.

faqs.question: Will I get altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: Unlikely, as acclimatization is part of the itinerary. However, stay hydrated and follow your trek leader’s guidance.

faqs.question: What’s the accommodation like?
answer: Base location: Clean guesthouses or homestays.
During trek: Sturdy tents (2–3 sharing), sleeping bags provided.

faqs.question: Are meals provided during the trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, simple and healthy vegetarian meals (Jain options on request) are served including breakfast, lunch, evening snacks, and dinner.

faqs.question: How do I reach the trek base?
faqs.answer: Nearest city/town is accessible by air, train, and bus. From there, cabs or shared vehicles can be hired to reach the base village.

faqs.question: Is there any network or ATM availability?
answer: ATM: Available in nearest town before trek.
Mobile network: Available till base village; beyond that, it's disconnected.

faqs.question: What if I need to quit mid-trek?
faqs.answer: Emergency exit protocols are in place, but all extra costs incurred will be borne by the trekker. Notify the trek leader at once in case of issues.

faqs.question: What should I carry?
answer: Mandatory: Backpack, hiking shoes, walking stick, headlamp.
Clothing: Warm layers, thermals, waterproof jacket, socks.
Other: Water bottle, day pack, wipes, cap, gloves, toilet paper.

activities: Return trek from Nag Tibba to Pantwari and drive back to Dehradun, soaking in the lush landscapes and panoramic views along the way.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Rishikesh → Joshimath
activities: Drive from Rishikesh to Joshimath and settle into your accommodation. Enjoy the scenic views of the Garhwal Himalayas along the route and relax after your journey.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Joshimath → Tugasi → Gulling (~9,600 ft)
activities: Trek from Joshimath to Gulling (~9,600 ft), enjoying lush forests and Himalayan landscapes along the way. Arrive at Gulling and acclimatize while soaking in the panoramic views of surrounding peaks.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Gulling Top → Forest Camp (~11,000 ft)
activities: Trek from Gulling Top to Forest Camp (~11,000 ft), passing through alpine meadows and dense conifer forests. Spend the evening at Forest Camp, enjoying the tranquility and starry skies of the Himalayas.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Tali Top → Kuari Pass (~12,763 ft) → Khullara
activities: Trek from Tali Top to the Kuari Pass (~12,763 ft), enjoying breathtaking views of Nanda Devi and other Himalayan peaks. Descend to Khullara for an overnight stay, relishing the serenity of high-altitude meadows.

itinerary.day: Days 5–6: Khullara → Joshimath → Rishikesh
activities: Descend from Khullara to Joshimath and board your drive back to Rishikesh. Enjoy scenic river valleys and mountain views along the route, marking the completion of your memorable trek.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Govindghat → Ghangaria (~13 km)
activities: Drive to Govindghat and start the trek to Ghangaria (~13 km), enjoying the scenic river valleys and lush Himalayan landscapes along the way. Upon arrival, check into the guesthouse or campsite and rest for the night.

itinerary.day: Day 2: Ghangaria → Valley of Flowers (~3 km)
activities: Embark on a short trek (~3 km) from Ghangaria to the stunning Valley of Flowers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the vibrant alpine flora, colorful meadows, and scenic trails, soaking in the natural beauty before returning to Ghangaria for the night.

itinerary.day: Day 3: Ghangaria → Hemkund Sahib
activities: Trek from Ghangaria to Hemkund Sahib, the revered Sikh pilgrimage site nestled at high altitude. Witness the pristine glacial lake, snow-capped peaks, and serene surroundings before returning to Ghangaria for rest.

itinerary.day: Day 4: Ghangaria → Govindghat → Joshimath
activities: Return trek from Ghangaria to Govindghat and continue by vehicle to Joshimath. Enjoy the river valley views and the Himalayan scenery along the way before checking into your accommodation in Joshimath.

itinerary.day: Days 5–6: Buffer/Travel
activities: These are flexible days reserved for travel adjustments, acclimatization, or unforeseen weather conditions. Use this time to rest, explore nearby villages, or enjoy scenic drives in the region.

itinerary.day: Day 1: Manali → Jobra → Chika (3,048 m)

itinerary.day: Day 4: Shea Goru → Chatru → Chandratal Lake → Chatru
activities: Trek from Shea Goru to Chatru and onward to the mesmerizing Chandratal Lake, famous for its crystal-clear waters and scenic beauty. Return to Chatru for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 5: Chatru → Manali
activities: Descend from Chatru back to Manali, enjoying the last glimpses of the Himalayan landscapes before concluding the trek.

packages.title: Spiritual Journey by the Ganga
packages.name: Varanasi 4 Days / 3 Nights
packages.subTitle: (Kashi Vishwanath, Ganga Aarti, Sarnath, Temples & Ghats)
highlight: Kashi Vishwanath Temple – One of the 12 Jyotirlingas, dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat – Evening ritual with fire, chants & devotion.
Boat Ride on River Ganga – Sunrise or evening boat rides offering spiritual vibes.
Sarnath – The place where Lord Buddha gave his first sermon.
Assi Ghat – Famous for morning rituals, yoga, and cultural activities.
Manikarnika Ghat – Sacred cremation ghat symbolizing Moksha (salvation).
Ramnagar Fort – 17th-century Mughal-style fort with museum & vintage collection.
Banaras Hindu University (BHU) & Bharat Kala Bhavan – Cultural & educational landmark.
Tulsi Manas Temple & Durga Kund Mandir – Temples of historical & spiritual importance.
Local Markets of Varanasi – Famous for Banarasi silk sarees, handicrafts, and street food.
things_not_to_miss: Sunrise boat ride on the Ganges.
Evening Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat.
Tasting Banarasi paan.
Shopping for Banarasi silk sarees.
Trying local delicacies – Kachori-Sabzi, Malaiyo (winter special).
Visiting Manikarnika Ghat for cultural understanding.
Yoga session at Assi Ghat.
Exploring narrow lanes of old Varanasi.
Witnessing Subah-e-Banaras cultural program.
Walking tour through ghats & temples.
how_to_reach: Varanasi is well-connected by air, rail, and road. The Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport links Varanasi to major Indian cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bangalore, and Hyderabad. Varanasi Junction and Mughalsarai Junction are among India’s busiest railway stations, connecting the city nationwide. By road, national highways make Varanasi accessible from Lucknow, Allahabad, and Patna. Local transport includes auto-rickshaws, cycle rickshaws, and cabs. With connectivity via air, rail, and road, Varanasi is convenient for both domestic and international travelers.
placedesc: Kashi Vishwanath Temple: Devotees believe visiting this Jyotirlinga grants liberation from the cycle of rebirth.
Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat: Visitors experience divine energy, mesmerizing chants, and synchronized rituals.
Boat Ride on Ganga: Tourists enjoy stunning views of sunrise & ghats, capturing the eternal charm of Varanasi.
Sarnath: A major Buddhist pilgrimage, symbolizing peace, wisdom, and the spread of Dharma.
Assi Ghat: Popular for spiritual yoga sessions, morning Subah-e-Banaras programs, and cultural events.
Manikarnika Ghat: Pilgrims believe cremation here ensures salvation, attracting both devotees & seekers.
Ramnagar Fort: Travelers explore royal heritage, antique weapons, and the famous Ramnagar Ramlila tradition.
BHU & Bharat Kala Bhavan: Art, culture, and heritage blend for knowledge seekers and tourists alike.
Tulsi Manas Mandir & Durga Kund: Rich history tied to Tulsidas and Goddess Durga, visited by pilgrims year-round.
Banarasi Markets: Travelers buy Banarasi silk sarees, jewelry, and taste iconic street food like kachori-sabzi & malaiyo.
about_the_tour: This 4 Days / 3 Nights Varanasi tour offers a unique blend of spirituality, history, and cultural richness. Witness the sacred Ganga Aarti, explore ancient temples, and immerse in the city’s vibrant ghats. A visit to Sarnath provides peace, while the boat rides on the Ganges reveal the timeless beauty of the city. Alongside temples and rituals, experience the heritage at Ramnagar Fort and local flavors in Banarasi bazaars. This tour ensures a perfect balance of faith, culture, and exploration, making it ideal for both pilgrims and explorers.

Guided boat ride on Ganga (sunrise ride)

Photography is restricted inside some temples.
Expect crowded conditions during peak festivals.
Bargain while shopping in local markets.

itinerary.day: DAY 1 - Arrival in Varanasi – Evening Ganga Aarti
activities: Arrive in Varanasi by flight/train. Transfer to hotel & freshen up. In the evening, head to Dashashwamedh Ghat to witness the famous Ganga Aarti with chants, diyas, and rituals on the banks of the sacred river. Take a short walking tour through the narrow lanes around the ghats to experience local street food and bustling markets. Overnight stay in Varanasi.

itinerary.day: DAY 2 - Kashi Vishwanath Darshan & City Temples
activities: Early morning boat ride on the Ganga during sunrise – watch the ghats come alive with prayers, rituals, and spiritual vibes. Later, visit the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Annapurna Temple, and Vishalakshi Temple. Explore Banaras Hindu University (BHU) and Bharat Mata Mandir. Evening free for shopping (Banarasi silk sarees, handicrafts). Overnight in Varanasi.

itinerary.day: DAY 3 - Excursion to Sarnath & Ghats Tour
activities: After breakfast, proceed to Sarnath (10 km) – where Lord Buddha delivered his first sermon. Visit Dhamek Stupa, Chaukhandi Stupa, Mulagandha Kuti Vihar, and the Sarnath Museum. Return to Varanasi by evening and enjoy a spiritual walk along the ghats – Assi Ghat, Manikarnika Ghat (famous cremation ghat), and Tulsi Ghat. End the day with another mesmerizing Ganga Aarti.

itinerary.day: DAY 4 - Departure from Varanasi
activities: Early morning visit to Ramnagar Fort & Museum (if time permits). Breakfast at hotel, check out, and transfer to airport/railway station for onward journey.

faqs.question: Best time to visit Varanasi?
faqs.answer: October to March (pleasant weather & festivals).

faqs.question: Is Varanasi safe for solo travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, but stay alert in crowded areas.

faqs.question: Do I need to pre-book the boat ride?
faqs.answer: Recommended during peak season.

faqs.answer: Around 45 minutes.

faqs.answer: Some temples allow entry, but few restrict.

faqs.question: Is photography allowed during Aarti?
faqs.answer: Yes, but without flash and from a distance.

faqs.question: What should I wear in Varanasi?
faqs.answer: Modest and comfortable clothes.

faqs.question: Is street food safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, if eaten from hygienic and popular stalls.

faqs.question: How many days are enough for Varanasi?
faqs.answer: 3–4 days for a complete experience.

faqs.question: Can I combine Varanasi with nearby destinations?
faqs.answer: Yes, trips often extend to Prayagraj, Ayodhya, or Bodhgaya.

about_the_tour: This 3 Days / 2 Nights journey through Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Rama, is a soul-enriching pilgrimage blending history, spirituality, and culture, covering the newly built Ram Janmabhoomi Temple, riverside ghats, and heritage temples, with darshan, evening aartis, devotional music, cultural parks, and quiet riverside rituals, making it perfect for families, solo travelers, and devotees, ensuring a deep connection with Lord Rama’s legacy.

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival in Ayodhya – Evening Aarti
activities: Arrive in Ayodhya by flight or train and check in to your hotel. After some rest, proceed to Ram Ki Paidi Ghats on the banks of the Saryu River to witness the mesmerizing Saryu Aarti, with lamps floating on the water creating a divine atmosphere. Later, take a short walking tour around the local markets before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Ram Mandir & Temples of Ayodhya
activities: Start your day with a visit to the grand Shri Ram Mandir (Ram Janmabhoomi Temple) for prayers, followed by exploration of Hanuman Garhi, Kanak Bhawan, Dashrath Mahal, and Treta Ke Thakur Temple. In the evening, enjoy a spiritual walk through the holy ghats, including a visit to Nageshwarnath Temple, before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay in Ayodhya.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Departure from Ayodhya
activities: After breakfast, if time permits, visit Guptar Ghat, associated with Lord Ram’s departure to Vaikuntha, before checking out and transferring to the airport or railway station for your onward journey.

about_the_tour: This 3 Days / 2 Nights Prayagraj tour takes you through India’s spiritual and cultural heart, beginning at the holy Triveni Sangam where saints, sages, and pilgrims gather for blessings. Explore Mughal heritage at Allahabad Fort, take blessings at ancient temples, and walk through historical gardens and museums narrating India’s freedom struggle. Evening aartis on the ghats, serene boat rides, and local delicacies complete the experience, offering a perfect blend of spirituality, history, and culture for every traveler.
know_before_you_go: Early mornings are best for Sangam visits to avoid crowds
Carry light cotton clothes in summer and woolens in winter
Pre-book hotels during Kumbh or Magh Mela season
Respect local customs while bathing in the Sangam

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival in Prayagraj – Evening Sangam Aarti
activities: Arrive in Prayagraj and check in to your hotel. In the evening, proceed to the iconic Triveni Sangam, the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers, for a holy dip or boat ride. Attend the enchanting Sangam Aarti, where the riverbanks glow with countless diyas, and stroll through the local bazaars before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Temples & Heritage Walk
activities: After breakfast, visit Akshayavat Tree and Hanuman Mandir, famous for its reclining idol. Explore the historic Allahabad Fort built by Akbar, Anand Bhavan, the ancestral home of the Nehru family, and Khusro Bagh, a Mughal garden with tombs. In the evening, take a spiritual walk through city temples such as Lete Hanuman Mandir and enjoy local street food before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Departure – Optional Kumbh Mela Experience
activities: On the final day, partake in early morning prayers at the ghats. If your trip coincides with the Kumbh Mela, you can participate in the spiritual festival activities at the mela grounds. After breakfast, check out and proceed to the railway station or airport for your onward journey.

about_the_tour: This pilgrimage to Guruvayur Temple offers a divine blend of spirituality, tradition, and Kerala’s cultural richness. Dedicated to Lord Krishna, the temple is visited by millions each year for its powerful darshans and elaborate rituals. The itinerary includes darshans, temple visits, elephant sanctuary tours, and cultural experiences in Thrissur, making it perfect for families, pilgrims, and spiritual seekers.
know_before_you_go: Strict dress code applies – men: mundu/dhoti (no shirts inside sanctum); women: saree/salwar/mundu.
Non-Hindus are not permitted inside Guruvayur Temple.
Photography is prohibited inside the temple.
Temple can get crowded – especially on weekends & festivals.
Darshan queues may take 2–3 hours; plan accordingly.
Senior citizens & disabled devotees have separate entry.
Shoes & leather items must be left outside.
Best time to visit: October – March (pleasant weather).
Book accommodations early during Ekadasi festival season.
Carry some cash – temple counters may not accept cards.

itinerary.day: Day 1 – Arrival at Guruvayur & Evening Darshan
activities: Arrive at Guruvayur, Kerala’s spiritual heart. Check into your hotel and freshen up. In the evening, visit the Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple, one of India’s most revered shrines, often called “Bhooloka Vaikunta” (Heaven on Earth). Witness the enchanting Deeparadhana (lamp offering) and vibrant evening rituals. Overnight stay in Guruvayur.

itinerary.day: 🗓 Day 2 – Temple Visits & Cultural Exploration
activities: Wake up early to attend the Nirmalyam Darshan (early morning ritual) at Guruvayur Temple. After darshan, visit Mammiyoor Mahadeva Temple, where Lord Shiva is worshipped. Later, explore Punnathur Kotta, an elephant sanctuary that houses temple elephants donated by devotees. In the afternoon, proceed to Thrissur, known as Kerala’s cultural capital. Visit Vadakkunnathan Temple and the Kerala Kalamandalam (traditional art training center). Return to Guruvayur for overnight stay.

itinerary.day: 🗓 Day 3 – Local Exploration & Departure
activities: After breakfast, take a stroll through Guruvayur town, visiting small Krishna-themed handicraft shops and sweet stalls offering the temple’s famous Pal Payasam (milk pudding prasadam). Optional visit to Chavakkad Beach, located just 5 km away, before departure with divine blessings of Lord Krishna.

faqs.question: What is Guruvayur Temple famous for?
faqs.answer: It is one of the most important Krishna temples in India, known as Bhooloka Vaikunta.

faqs.question: Can non-Hindus enter the temple?
faqs.answer: No, entry is restricted to Hindus.

faqs.question: Is there a dress code?
faqs.answer: Yes, men wear mundu (dhoti), and women wear saree or salwar.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit?
faqs.answer: October to March; also during the Ekadasi festival season.

faqs.question: Are special poojas available?
faqs.answer: Yes, including Udayasthamana Pooja, Thulabharam, and Choroonu (child’s first feeding).

faqs.question: What is Punnathur Kotta?
faqs.answer: It is an elephant camp housing temple elephants.

faqs.question: What prasadam is famous here?
faqs.answer: Pal Payasam (sweet milk pudding).

faqs.question: Is accommodation available nearby?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are plenty of hotels and guesthouses around the temple.

faqs.question: How long does darshan take?
faqs.answer: Darshan usually takes 1–3 hours depending on the season and queue.

faqs.question: Are children allowed in the temple?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many families bring infants for the Choroonu ritual.

about_the_tour: The Haridwar & Rishikesh 4 Days / 3 Nights Tour is a soulful blend of spirituality and adventure. Begin your journey at Haridwar, the Gateway to Gods, where you witness sacred ghats, spiritual rituals, and vibrant Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri. Visit hilltop temples like Mansa Devi and Chandi Devi, and explore ancient shrines. Move to Rishikesh, the Yoga Capital of the World, where the Ganges flows amidst serene mountains. Here, you engage in meditation, attend yoga sessions, and explore the iconic Ram & Laxman Jhula. Add thrill with river rafting or bungee jumping, making this journey both divine and adventurous.
know_before_you_go: Dress modestly at temples and ghats.
Carry valid ID proof.
Respect local customs and rituals.
Adventure activities depend on river conditions.
Alcohol & smoking prohibited near ghats.
Evening aarti gets crowded—arrive early.
Carry light woolens (cool evenings).
Book rafting/bungee in advance.
Ashrams have strict discipline & timings.
Best time to visit: Oct–Apr (avoid monsoon rafting).

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival in Haridwar – Spiritual Gateway
activities: Arrive at Haridwar and check in to your hotel. Visit local temples like Mansa Devi and Chandi Devi via ropeway. In the evening, witness the mesmerizing Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri, where thousands of lamps float on the holy river. Overnight stay in Haridwar.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Haridwar → Rishikesh – Yoga & Riverbank Bliss
activities: After breakfast, drive to Rishikesh (30 km / 1 hr). Explore Ram Jhula, Laxman Jhula, and Triveni Ghat. Visit iconic ashrams such as Parmarth Niketan or Sivananda Ashram for a yoga or meditation session. In the evening, attend the Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan and enjoy the serene riverbank ambiance. Overnight stay in Rishikesh.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Rishikesh – Spiritual & Adventure Blend
activities: Start the day with a morning yoga session by the Ganges. You can then choose between a spiritual route—visiting Beatles Ashram, Neelkanth Mahadev Temple, and Vashishta Cave for meditation—or an adventure route with river rafting, bungee jumping, or trekking around Rishikesh. In the evening, enjoy a leisurely stroll along the Ganga ghats and café hopping. Overnight stay in Rishikesh.

itinerary.day: Day 4 - Rishikesh – Departure
activities: Begin the morning with meditation or yoga by the river. After breakfast, check out and depart, taking with you spiritual memories and the blessings of Mother Ganga.

Baltal & Pahalgam – The two main base camps offering trekking and helicopter routes. Baltal is shorter but steeper; Pahalgam is longer but scenic.
Chandanwari – Picturesque meadow with snow even in summer, believed to be where Lord Shiva left his moon.
Sheshnag Lake – Sacred lake resembling the serpent of Lord Shiva.
Panchtarni – Named after five rivers that flow together, it is the last stop before reaching the cave.
Sonmarg & Pahalgam – Scenic valleys filled with lush meadows, snow peaks, and pine forests.
Betaab Valley – Known for its beauty and Bollywood connections.
how_to_reach: By Air – Nearest airport is Srinagar (70 km from Baltal, 90 km from Pahalgam). Well connected to Delhi, Mumbai & other metros.
By Train – Jammu Tawi is the nearest railway station (approx. 250–300 km). From there, buses/taxis are available.
By Road – Regular buses and cabs connect Jammu–Srinagar–Pahalgam–Baltal. Pilgrims usually travel to base camps by taxi or bus.

about_the_tour: The Amarnath Yatra 5 Days / 4 Nights is one of India’s most revered pilgrimages, attracting lakhs of devotees every year. The journey combines faith, devotion, and adventure as devotees trek through high-altitude terrain to reach the sacred Amarnath Cave, where the natural ice Shivlinga is worshipped as a manifestation of Lord Shiva. With routes from Baltal and Pahalgam, the yatra offers both challenging treks and helicopter options for those seeking ease. Along the way, pilgrims experience the breathtaking beauty of the Himalayas, serene lakes like Sheshnag, and spiritually charged landscapes. This tour is not just a pilgrimage but a life-changing spiritual experience.
know_before_you_go: Yatra is open only June–August (Shravan month)
Medical fitness certificate is mandatory for all pilgrims
Carry woolens, raincoat, trekking shoes, and essential medicines
Altitude ranges from 2,700 m to 3,888 m – risk of AMS (altitude sickness)
Children below 13 & adults above 75 are not allowed
Pregnant women beyond 6 months are restricted
Photography inside the cave is strictly prohibited
Carry ID proofs & Yatra permit at all times
Weather is unpredictable – always keep warm clothes handy
Pre-book helicopter services & accommodations early

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival in Jammu/Srinagar – Gateway to Yatra
activities: Arrive at Jammu or Srinagar airport/railway station and meet our representative. Drive to Pahalgam via Anantnag or Sonmarg depending on the chosen Yatra route. Check into your hotel or camp. Spend the evening at leisure with a short walk along the river. Overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Yatra Begins – Trek/Helicopter to Panchtarni
activities: Early morning proceed to Baltal or Chandanwari base camps. Begin the trek of 12–14 km towards Panchtarni, the last stop before the cave, or opt for a helicopter ride from Baltal to Panchtarni (subject to availability). Stay in tents at Panchtarni and prepare for the cave darshan in the evening.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Darshan of Shri Amarnath Ji – Holy Cave
activities: Wake up early and trek or ride a pony 6 km to the Amarnath Cave (3,888 m altitude). Seek blessings of the naturally formed Shivling of ice, symbolizing Lord Shiva. After darshan, return to Panchtarni and trek back to Baltal or fly down by helicopter. Overnight stay at Baltal or Sonmarg.

itinerary.day: Day 4 - Baltal/Sonmarg – Srinagar
activities: After breakfast, drive back to Srinagar. Visit Dal Lake, Shankaracharya Temple, and Mughal Gardens (Nishat, Shalimar, Chashme Shahi). Enjoy an evening shikara ride on Dal Lake. Overnight stay in a houseboat or hotel.

itinerary.day: Day 5 - Departure from Srinagar/Jammu
activities: Morning free for shopping or local sightseeing. After breakfast, transfer to Srinagar airport or Jammu railway station for onward journey, taking with you divine memories of the Amarnath Yatra.

faqs.answer: No, advance registration is compulsory.

about_the_tour: The Badrinath Dham Yatra (5 Days / 4 Nights) is one of the most significant pilgrimages for Hindus, being part of the Char Dham Yatra. Nestled in the Himalayas at an altitude of 3,133 meters, Badrinath is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. The journey is a blend of devotion, spirituality, and natural beauty. Pilgrims experience divine darshan at the Badrinath Temple, holy dips in the Tapt Kund, and exploration of mythological sites like Mana Village, Vyas Gufa, and Bheem Pul. With snow-capped peaks, gushing rivers, and sacred shrines, this yatra is considered a path to moksha (liberation).
know_before_you_go: Badrinath temple is open from May/June to October/November only
The weather is cold; carry woolens, jackets, and rain gear
Pilgrims should be physically fit as the altitude is 3,133 m
Medical facilities are limited – carry essential medicines
Photography inside the temple is prohibited
Roads are narrow and prone to landslides during rains
Accommodation ranges from simple dharamshalas to budget hotels
Carry valid ID proof for registration and temple entry
Elderly people and children should take precautions due to altitude
Mobile connectivity is limited in higher regions

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival in Haridwar – Gateway to the Himalayas
activities: Arrive at Haridwar by train or road and check in at the hotel. In the evening, witness the divine Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri, marking a perfect spiritual start to the Char Dham journey. Overnight stay in Haridwar.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Haridwar to Rudraprayag to Joshimath (Approx. 8–9 hrs drive)
activities: After breakfast, drive along the Alaknanda River with stops at Devprayag (confluence of Bhagirathi & Alaknanda), Rudraprayag, and Karnaprayag. Arrive at Joshimath, check into the hotel, and relax amidst serene mountain views. Overnight stay in Joshimath.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Joshimath – Badrinath Darshan – Mana Village – Return
activities: Drive to Badrinath Dham (3,133 m), take a holy dip in Tapt Kund, and offer prayers at Shri Badrivishal. Explore Mana Village, the last Indian village near Tibet, visiting Vyas Gufa, Ganesh Gufa, and the Saraswati River. Return to Joshimath for overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 - Joshimath to Rishikesh
activities: After breakfast, drive down to Rishikesh, revisiting Rudraprayag and Devprayag en route. Check in at the hotel, then enjoy the evening Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat and a peaceful walk on Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula. Overnight stay in Rishikesh.

itinerary.day: Day 5 - Rishikesh to Haridwar (Departure)
activities: After breakfast, drive back to Haridwar and transfer to the railway station or airport for onward journey, carrying divine blessings of Lord Vishnu from Badrinath.

about_the_tour: The Gangotri & Yamunotri Yatra (6 Days / 5 Nights) forms half of the revered Char Dham Yatra in Uttarakhand. Devotees begin their spiritual journey by visiting Yamunotri, the origin of the sacred Yamuna River, followed by Gangotri, where the holy Ganga originates. The yatra involves scenic drives through Haridwar, Barkot, Uttarkashi, and Harsil Valley, combined with treks to Yamunotri and optional Gaumukh. This pilgrimage not only holds religious importance but also offers mesmerizing Himalayan landscapes, riverside serenity, and cultural experiences of Garhwal villages.
know_before_you_go: Both shrines are open only from May/June to October/November
Trek to Yamunotri is 5–6 km uphill from Janki Chatti
Pony, palanquin, and doli services available for Yamunotri trek
Carry woolens, thermals, and rain gear; weather is unpredictable
Roads are narrow and prone to landslides during monsoon
Limited accommodation near Yamunotri; book in advance
Mobile network is weak or unavailable in higher regions
Carry medicines; medical facilities are basic
Photography inside temples is restricted
Pilgrims should be physically fit for trekking at high altitude

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival at Haridwar – The Spiritual Gateway
activities: Arrive in Haridwar and check into your hotel. In the evening, witness the divine Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri where thousands of diyas float on the river, chants echo in the air, and priests perform rituals with large lamps, creating an unforgettable spiritual atmosphere. Return to your hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Haridwar to Barkot (Approx. 7–8 hrs drive)
activities: After breakfast, drive towards Barkot via the scenic Mussoorie hills. Stop by Kempty Falls and enjoy the refreshing cascade before continuing through winding mountain roads, apple orchards, and pine forests. Arrive at Barkot, check into your hotel or camp, and enjoy dinner amidst cool mountain air. Overnight stay in Barkot.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Barkot – Yamunotri Darshan – Barkot
activities: Early morning, drive to Janki Chatti and begin a 6 km trek to Yamunotri Temple, passing forests, streams, and snow-clad peaks. Take a dip in Surya Kund, cook rice in its hot spring water as prasad, and offer prayers at the temple of Goddess Yamuna. After darshan, trek back to Janki Chatti and return to Barkot for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 4 - Barkot to Uttarkashi (Approx. 4 hrs drive)
activities: After breakfast, drive towards Uttarkashi along scenic mountain valleys. On arrival, check into your hotel and visit the famous Vishwanath Temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. Spend the evening strolling through the serene town and soaking in its spiritual aura. Dinner and overnight stay in Uttarkashi.

itinerary.day: Day 5 - Uttarkashi – Gangotri Darshan – Return
activities: Drive through pine forests and Himalayan villages along the Bhagirathi River to reach Gangotri (3,048 m). Take a holy dip in the river before offering prayers at Gangotri Temple dedicated to Goddess Ganga. Spend quiet moments meditating by the river before returning to Uttarkashi for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.day: Day 6 - Uttarkashi – Rishikesh – Haridwar (Departure)
activities: After breakfast, drive back towards Haridwar with an en-route stop at Rishikesh. Visit Ram Jhula, Laxman Jhula, and the peaceful ghats, and if time permits, attend the soulful Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat. Continue your drive to Haridwar for departure, concluding your yatra with divine blessings and cherished memories.

about_the_tour: The Mathura & Vrindavan – Krishna Janmabhoomi Yatra (4 Days / 3 Nights) takes you on a sacred journey through the land of Shri Krishna’s birth and pastimes. This pilgrimage includes the Janmabhoomi Temple in Mathura, the vibrant temples of Vrindavan, and holy sites like Govardhan, Barsana, and Gokul. Devotees experience a blend of spirituality, architecture, cultural traditions, and the blissful aura of Krishna bhakti. Evening aartis by the Yamuna, bhajan sandhyas, and temple darshans make this tour a divine and soulful retreat.
know_before_you_go: Best time to visit is October to March (pleasant weather)
Summers are hot; carry water, caps, and light cotton clothes
During Janmashtami & Holi, expect heavy crowds
Photography inside some temples is restricted
Always remove shoes before entering temples
Be cautious with belongings at crowded ghats and bazaars
Most temples have fixed darshan timings – plan accordingly
Try local vegetarian cuisine; non-veg & alcohol are strictly prohibited
Carry cash; many small shops don’t accept digital payments
Respect local traditions and avoid visiting Nidhivan at night (entry is restricted)

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival in Mathura – Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi & Ganga Aarti
activities: Arrive in Mathura and check into your hotel. In the evening, visit Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple, the sacred birthplace of Lord Krishna, where devotees feel deeply connected to his divine stories. Later, head to Vishram Ghat for the mesmerizing Yamuna Aarti, with lamps floating on the river and devotional chants filling the air. Return for an overnight stay in Mathura.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Vrindavan – The Land of Krishna’s Leelas
activities: After breakfast, drive to Vrindavan and begin at Banke Bihari Temple, known for its lively darshan. Continue to the serene ISKCON Temple, where the chanting of Hare Krishna creates a spiritual aura, and later visit the grand Prem Mandir, which glows beautifully with illuminated carvings in the evening. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Mathura/Vrindavan.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Gokul – Nandgaon – Govardhan
activities: Start the day exploring Gokul, where Krishna lived with Yashoda Maiya, including Chaurasi Khamba. Continue to Nandgaon, the village of Nand Baba, with its temple atop a hill. In the afternoon, visit Govardhan Hill and participate in the sacred Govardhan Parikrama, recalling how Krishna lifted the hill to protect his devotees. End with darshan at Radha Kund and Shyam Kund before retiring for the night.

itinerary.day: Day 4 - Dwarkadhish Temple & Departure
activities: On the final morning, visit the famous Dwarkadhish Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna as the King of Dwarka. Afterwards, explore Krishna Nagar Market to shop for Mathura peda and local souvenirs. Conclude your journey with cherished memories of Krishna’s divine leelas before departing from Mathura.

faqs.answer: Not mandatory but highly recommended

faqs.answer: Yes, but avoid isolated areas at night

about_the_tour: The Kurukshetra – Land of Bhagavad Gita (3 Days / 2 Nights) tour takes you through India’s sacred land where the Mahabharata was fought and Bhagavad Gita was spoken. Explore sarovars, temples, Jyotisar, museums, and Mughal monuments, blending spirituality, history, and culture. Perfect for pilgrims, families, and history lovers.

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival & Brahma Sarovar – The Eternal Waters of Creation
activities: Arrive in Kurukshetra, the sacred land where Lord Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita. Begin your journey at Brahma Sarovar, believed to be created by Lord Brahma. Participate in the evening Aarti at the Sarovar, where floating diyas illuminate the waters, creating a serene spiritual atmosphere. Overnight stay in Kurukshetra.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - Jyotisar – Where Lord Krishna Revealed the Gita
activities: After breakfast, visit Jyotisar, the divine spot where Lord Krishna revealed the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna, and see the ancient Banyan Tree that stands as a silent witness. Explore the Sri Krishna Museum to view epics and relics from the Mahabharata era. Continue to Sannihit Sarovar, considered the meeting point of all sacred rivers, and later seek blessings at the Bhadrakali Temple, where Pandavas and Kauravas once prayed before the great war. Overnight stay in Kurukshetra.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Heritage & Departure
activities: Begin the day with a visit to the Kurukshetra Panorama & Science Centre, which presents the Mahabharata battle in a unique artistic and scientific way. Explore Sheikh Chilli’s Tomb, an example of Mughal architecture blending history and spirituality. Collect souvenirs, local prasadam, and memories before departure, carrying with you the eternal wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita.

itinerary.day: Day 1 - Arrival in Amritsar – Sacred Welcome
activities: Arrive in Amritsar and check into your hotel. In the evening, visit the Golden Temple, beautifully illuminated with shimmering reflections in the sacred pool. Participate in the evening aarti and kirtan, followed by langar – a soulful community dining experience that embodies the spirit of equality and devotion. Overnight stay in Amritsar.

itinerary.day: Day 2 - History & Patriotism – Jallianwala Bagh & Wagah Border
activities: Start the morning with a visit to Jallianwala Bagh and the Partition Museum to witness the stories of India’s freedom struggle. Spend the afternoon shopping at Hall Bazaar and tasting authentic Punjabi street food. In the evening, drive to Wagah Border to experience the electrifying Beating Retreat Ceremony, before returning to Amritsar for dinner and rest.

itinerary.day: Day 3 - Forts, Culture & Departure
activities: Begin with a visit to Gobindgarh Fort for cultural performances and heritage walks. Continue to the Durgiana Temple and Ram Bagh Gardens, which houses the Maharaja Ranjit Singh Museum. Conclude your journey with a food trail, savoring Amritsari Kulcha and refreshing lassi, before departure with cherished memories of Amritsar.

about_the_tour: The Kedarnath 5 Days / 4 Nights Yatra is a soul-stirring blend of spirituality, nature, and devotion. Starting from Haridwar or Rishikesh, the journey takes you through sacred towns, confluences, and valleys. From Gaurikund, a 16 km trek (or pony/palki/helicopter) leads you to the Kedarnath Temple, set amidst snow-clad peaks. The darshan of Lord Shiva, visit to Bhairav Nath Temple, and exploration of nearby holy places like Triyuginarayan and Guptkashi, make this journey both divine and memorable. It’s not just a yatra—it’s an experience of surrender, faith, and Himalayan bliss.

Registration is mandatory for all pilgrims
Carry government ID proof at all checkpoints
Weather changes rapidly—carry warm clothes
Keep rain gear and sturdy shoes for trek
Mobile network is weak beyond Sonprayag

faqs.question: What type of accommodation is at Kedarnath?
faqs.answer: Accommodation options include GMVN guest houses, dharamshalas, and limited lodges.

faqs.answer: Yes, medical camps and support are available at trek points and Kedarnath base.

faqs.question: Can I do the yatra in winter?

Pilgrims walk barefoot, follow strict rituals, and trek through forested paths to reach the shrine. The temple represents faith, equality, and brotherhood, attracting millions of devotees annually. The tour includes sacred river baths, darshan, rituals, and heritage visits to Erumeli and Pandalam, making it a soulful pilgrimage in Kerala.

After a holy bath in the Pamba River, begin the sacred trek of ~5 km through forested paths leading to Sannidhanam (Sabarimala Temple), experiencing the spiritual chants of 'Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa' echoing all around. Overnight stay in pilgrim accommodation at Sannidhanam.

itinerary.day: Day 2 – Darshan of Lord Ayyappa & Pilgrim Circuit
activities: Wake up early for darshan of Lord Ayyappa at Sabarimala Temple, considered one of the most sacred pilgrimages in India. After darshan, visit nearby spots such as Malikappuram Devi Temple and Vavar Swamy Mosque, a unique symbol of communal harmony. Later, return to Pamba and transfer to Nilakkal. Overnight stay in Nilakkal/Pandalam.
